वृत्तिः ॥ उदात्त इति वर्तते । यस्मिन्नुदात्ते परत उदात्तो लुप्यते तस्यादुदात्तस्यादिदात्तो भवति ॥

161. An unaccented vowel gets also the acute accent, when on account of it the preceding acute is elided.

The word udatta is understood here. Thus कुमार्+ई=कुमार् ॥ The word कुमार् has acute on the last, when the unaccented (anudatta) कीप् is added to it, the अँ is elided (VI. 1. 148), the anudatta ई becomes udatta. So also पथिन्+इस्=पथैः (VII. 1. 88), पथिन्+ए=पथैः, पथिन्+आ=पथैः ॥ The पथिन् has acute on the last. So also कुमुद+इमुद=कुमुदीन् (IV. 2. 87), मृदु, वेतस्वन् ॥ The words कुमुद &c, are end-acute, and the affix मन् (वन्) is anudatta (III. 1. 4).

Why 'an anudatta vowel gets &c'. Observe प्रासङ्गः+यन्=प्रासङ्गः ॥ (प्रासङ्ग बहत IV. 4. 76). Here though प्रसङ्ग is end-acute (VI. 2. 144 formed by घञ् with gati) it is followed by यं which is svarita (VI. 1. 185), this svarita causes the lopa of अँ udatta: but it does not itself become udatta. No, this is not a proper counter-example. For by the general rule of accent VI. 1. 158, when one syllable is ordained to be udatta or svarita, all the other syllables of that word become anudatta. Therefore when यं is taught to be svarita, all the other syllables (like ई) will become anudatta. So there is no lopa of udatta when यं comes. The word अनुदात्त is used to indicate that the initial anudatta becomes udatta. Had anudatta not been used, the sutra would have been यत्रोदात्तलोपश्च, which would mean यस्मिन् प्रत्यये परत; उदात्तालुप्यते तस्यान्त उदात्तो भवति, for the anuvritti of अन्तः would then be read from the last. There would then be anomaly in the case of मा हि घुशाताम्, and माहि घुशायाम् ॥ From the root दुष्ट we have formed घुशाताम् and घुशायाम् in the Aorist Atmanepada, dual. दुष्ट+वर्त+आताम् = दुष्ट+स् (VII. 3. 72)+आताम् ॥ Here आताम् causes the elision of the udatta अ of स ॥ Therefore the final of आताम् would be udatta, which is not desired. The augment अ is not added because of मा, had it been added, the अँ would have been udatta (VI. 4. 71). Had हि not been given, then also the whole of घुशाताम् would have become anudatta in माघुशाताम् because of तिङ्+तिङ् (VIII. 1. 28). See VIII. 1. 34 (हि च). Why have we used the word यत्र in the sutra? If it was not employed, then the subsequent anudatta may be such which would not have caused the elision of the previous udatta; such udatta being elided by some other operator, and still such anudatta would have become udatta. Thus in भार्गवः, भार्गवैः, भूगवः ॥ Here भूगवः is plural of भार्गवः ॥ The word भार्गव is end-acute and this acute (अणु) was elided in the plural, before the affix जस् was added.

1114

END-ACUTE.

[ Bk. VI. Ch. I § 165.

The elision here is not *caused* by जस्, but is a subject of जस् (not निमित्त but विषय). Therefore जस् does not become udatta, which would have been the case, had यत्र not been used. प्राक् सुबुत्वने गोत्रप्रत्यस्य लुक् ॥ The gotra affix was elided prior to the adding of the case-ending. Why do we say “when an *udatta* is elided”? Observe बिब्+अम् (IV. 1. 104) = बंइ ॥ The feminine of this will be बे+डीन (IV. 1. 73 = बेही ॥ Here ई causes the elision of au*udatta* अ of इ, and hence remains unchanged. So also अी धी ॥

धातोः ॥ १६२ ॥ पदानि ॥ धातोः, (अन्तः, उदात्तः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अन्त इत्येव । धातोरन्त उदात्तो भवति ॥

162. A root has the acute on the end-syllable.

The word अन्त is understood here. Thus पँचति, पँडति, ऊँगति, गोपायँति, याँति ॥

चितः ॥ १६३ ॥ पदानि ॥ चितः, (अन्तः उदात्तः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ चितो ऽन्त उदात्तो भवति ॥

163. A stem (formed by an affix or augment or substitute) having an indicatory च्, gets acute on the end syllable.

Thus मेघुरम्, भाघुरम्, नेदुरम्. These are formed by पुरन् III. 2. 161. So also कुण्डिनः by II. 4. 70 where the substitute कुण्डिनन् is employed. To कुण्ड is added दान in the sense of मतुप्, then is added the feminine affix डोप, thus कुण्डिनी has middle-acute. The descendants of Kuṇḍinī will be कौण्डिन्यः (by यम् of Gargādi). The plural of Kaṇḍinya will be formed by eliding यम् and substituting कुण्डिनन् for the remaining portion. In the cases of affixes having an indicatory च्, the acute accent falls on the final, taking the stem and the affix in an aggregate. Thus बहुपट्टः ॥ The affix बहुपट्टः is one of those few affixes which are really prefixes. (V. 3. 68). The accent will not, therefore, fall on हु, but on the last syllable of the whole word compounded of the prefix + the base. So also with the affix अकच्. It is added in the *middle* of the word, but the accent will fall on the *end*; as उच्चैकः (V. 3. 71).

तद्धितस्य ॥ १६४ ॥ पदानि ॥ तद्धितस्य, (अन्तः, उदात्तः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ चित्त इत्येव । चित्तसद्धितस्यान्त उदात्तो भवति ॥

164. A stem formed with a Taddhita-affix having an indicatory च्, has acute on the end syllable.

Thus कौञ्जायनः formed by the affix च्फम् (IV. 1. 98). कुञ्ज+च् फण्+ञ्=कौञ्जायन्यः dual कौञ्जायन्यो, pl. कौञ्जायनः (ञ् being elided by II. 4. 62, and thus giving scope to च्फम् accent). In this affix there are two indicatory letters च् and म्; the च् has only one function, namely, regulating the accent according to this rule, while म् has two functions, one to regulate accent by VI. 1. 197, and another to cause Vṛddhi by VII. 2. 117. Now arises the question, should the word get the accent of च् or of म् ॥ The present rule declares that it should get

BK. VI. CH. I § 167 ]

END-ACUTE.

1115

the accent of च and not of म, for the latter finds still a function left to it, while if म was to regulate the accent, च would have no scope.

कितः ॥ १६५ ॥ पदानि ॥ कितः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तद्धितस्यैवेव । तद्धितस्य कित्तोन्त उदात्तो भवति ॥

165. A stem formed by a Taddhita affix having an indicatory क, has acute accent on the end syllable.

Thus नाडायुर्नः formed by फक् (IV. 1. 99), so also चायुर्नः ॥ Similarly भाभिर्कः, भाभिर्कः formed by ठक् (IV. 4. 1).

तिसृभ्यो जसः ॥ १६६ ॥ पदानि ॥ तिसृभ्यः, जसः, (अन्तः, उदात्तः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तिसृभ्य उत्तरस्य जसोन्त उदात्तो भवति ॥

166. The Nominative plural (जस्) of तिसृ has acute accent on the last syllable.

Thus तिर्बस्तिवन्ति ॥ This debars the Svarita accent ordained by VIII. 2. 4. The word तिसृ (feminine of वि VII. 2. 99) meaning 'three' is always plural. There are no singular or dual cases of this numeral; of the seven plural cases, the accusative plural will have acute on the final by VI. 1. 174; the remaining cases (Instrumental, Dative, Ablative, Genitive and Locative) have affixes beginning with a consonant, and by VI. 1. 179 they will be udatta. Thus the only case not covered by any special rule is जस् (nom. pl); which would have been Svarita, but for this rule. If जस् be the only case not provided for, then merely saying तिसृभ्यः would have sufficed to make the rule applicable to जस् only, why has then it been employed in the sutra? This is done, in order that in compounds, where तिसृ may come as a subordinate member, and where singular and dual endings will also be added, this rule will not apply. Had जस् been not used in tois sutra, then in the case of simple तिसृ there would be no harm, but when it is seconded member in a compound there would be anomaly. Thus अतितिश्री would have become end-acute. But that is not desired. It is svarita on the final by VIII. 2. 4.

चतुरः शसि ॥ १६७ ॥ पदानि ॥ चतुरः, शसि (अन्तउदात्तः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ चतुरः शसि परतो ऽन्त उदात्तो भवति ॥

167. The word चतुर, followed by the accusative plural, has acute accent on the last syllable.

Thus चतुरः पद्य the accent is on तु ॥ The feminine of चतुर is चतस् (VII. 2. 99), which has acute accent on the first (VII. 2. 99 Vārt), and its accusative plural will not have accent on the last syllable. This is so, because चतुर has acute on the first, as formed by उरन् affix. Its substitute चतस् will also be so, by the rule of स्थानिवत् ॥ The special enunciation of आयुवाच with regard to चतस् in the Vārtika चतसर्थायुवाचनिपातनं कर्तव्यं (VII. 2. 99) indicates that the

1116

END-ACUTE.

[ Bk. VI. Ch. I § 169

present rule does not apply to चतस् ॥ Another reason for this is as follows: चतस् + शस् = चतस + शस् ॥ Now comes the present Sūtra; here, however, the substitute of क् being sthānivat, will prevent the udatta formation of the अ of त; nor will क् be considered as final and take the acute, as there exists no vowel क् but a consonant र which cannot take an accent. As चतसः पद्य ॥ Professor Bohtlingk places the accent thus चतुरः, Pro. Māx Muller चतुरः ॥ I have followed Prof. Māx Muller in interpreting this sūtra; for Bohtlingk's interpretation would make the ending शस् accented, and not the final of चतुर ॥

साविकाचस्तृतीयादिर्विभक्तिः ॥ १६८ ॥ पदानि ॥ सौ, एकाचः, तृतीयादिः, विभक्तिः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ साविति सप्तमीबहुवचनस्य ध्रुवस्वस्थं महणम् । तत्र सौ य एकाच् तस्मात्सरा तृतीयादिर्विभक्तिः स्वता भवति ॥

168. The case-affixes of the Instrumental and of the cases that follow it have the acute accent, if the stem in the Locative Plural is monosyllabic.

The word सो (locative of सु) refers to the सु of the Locative plural. Thus वाचो, वाग्भ्याम्, वाग्भिः, वाग्भ्यः, वातो, वाद्भ्याम्, वाग्भिः ॥ Why do we say 'in the Locative plural'? Observe रीझा, रीझे ॥ Why do we say 'monosyllabic'? Observe हेरिणा, गिरिणा, रीझु ॥ Why do we say 'the Instrumentals and the rest'? Observe वाँचो, वाँचः ॥ Why do we say 'the case-endings (विभक्तिः)?' Observe वाँक्ता, वाँक्ता ॥ The plural of the Locative being taken in the sūtra, the rule does not apply to त्वया and त्वयि, as in the plural of the Locative they have more than one syllable, though in singular locative their stem has one syllable.

अन्तोदात्तादुत्तरपदादन्यतरस्यामनित्यसमासे ॥ १६९ ॥ पदानि ॥ अन्तोदात्तात, उत्तरपदात, अन्यतरस्याम्, अनित्यसमासे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ एकाच इति वर्तते, तृतीयादिर्विभक्तिरिति च । नित्यशब्दः स्वयते । तेन नित्याधिकारविहितः स- मासः पर्युक्त्यते । नित्यसमासादन्यत्रानित्यसमासे यदुत्तरपदमन्तोदात्तमेकाच् तस्मात्परातृतीयादिर्विभक्तिरन्य- तरस्याद्युक्ता भवति ॥

169. The same case endings may optionally have the acute accent, if the monosyllabic word stands at the end of a compound, and has acute accent on the final, when the compound can be easily unloosened.

The phrases 'एकाचः' and तृतीयादिर्विभक्तिः are understood here also. The nitya or invariable compounds are excluded by this rule. Thus परमवाँचा or परमवाँचो, परमवाँचो or वाँचो; परमवाँचः or 'वाँचः' ॥ So also परमवाँचा or 'वाँचः' &c. According to VI. I. 223, the compounds have acute accent on the final: that rule applies in the alternative when the case-affixes are not acute and gives us

BK. VI. CH. I § 171.]

END-ACUTE.

1117

the alternative forms. Why do we say 'is acutely accented on the final'? Observe अंबाचा, खुंचाचा, सुखचा ॥ These are Tatpurusha compounds and by VI. 2. 2. the first term of the compound retains its original accent. Why have we used the word 'standing at the end of a compound' when the word नित्यसमासे indicated that the compound was meant? Had we not used the word उत्तर-पातः, the aphorism would have stood as, अन्तोदात्तादन्यतरस्यामनित्यसमासे 'In a loose-compound having acute on the final, the above affixes are acute, if the compound consists of a monosyllable'. The word एकाचः will thus qualify the compound and not the second member of the compound, which is intended. And thus the rule will apply to इबोक् (इन कर्क) Ins. भोजः, भोजः &c, and not to compounds having more than one syllable. Why do we say 'in loose compounds'? Observe आग्निर्चिता, सोमर्चिता ॥ These words form invariable (nitya) compounds by II. 2. 19, and by VI. 2. 139, the second member retains its original accent, which makes चि udatta.

अञ्चेष्टन्दस्यसर्वनामस्थानम् ॥ १७० ॥ पदानि ॥ अञ्चेः, छन्दसि, असर्वनामस्थानम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अञ्चेः परा असर्वनामस्थानविभक्तिरहाता भवति छन्दसि विधेय ॥

170. In the Chhandas, the case-endings other than the sarvanāmasthāna get the acute accent when coming after अञ्चि ॥

In the Vedas, a stem ending in the word अञ्च, has the acute not only on the affixes previously mentioned, but on the accusative plural affix also. Thus इन्द्रा पृथिवी अस्यानः (Rig I. 84. 13). Here the word पृथिवी had accent on भी by VI. 1. 222, but by the present sūtra, the accent falls on the case-affix अस् ॥ Though the anuvritti of 'Instrumentals and the rest' was understood here, the word asarvanāmasthāna has been used here to include the ending वस् also. As प्रार्थना बाहुल् प्रतिभश्चापम् ॥

ऊडिदम्पदाद्यपुत्रैद्युभ्यः ॥ १७१ ॥ पदानि ॥ ऊट्, इदम, पदादि, अप्, पुम्, रै, धुभ्यः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ऊट् इदम पदादि अप् पुम् रै दिव् इयेतेभ्यो असर्वनामस्थानविभक्तिरहाता भवति ॥

171. The same (asarvanāmasthāna) case-endings have the acute accent, when the stem ends in वाह्, also after इदम, after पद् &c (upto निश VI. 1. 63), after अप्, पुम्, रै and दिव् ॥

The ऊट् is the substitute of the वा of वाह् (VI. 4. 132) and not the ऊट् taught in VI. 4. 19 &c). Thus प्रष्टोः, प्रष्टोः, but not in अस्युवा (Ins. sing of अस्युवाः derived by ऊट् substitution of व् in असादिव् VI. 4. 19 &c). इदम—आभ्याम्, एभिः The anuvritti of 'अन्तोदात्तात्' is understood here, therefore, when the word

11

1118

END-ACUTE.

[ Bk. VI. Ch. I § 173 ]

इदम् is not end-acute, this rule will not apply. When, therefore, there is anvāḍesa under II. 4. 32, the final being anudātta, this rule does not apply, as अयो आभ्यां निपुणमभीत् ॥ The पदादि words are पद, दत् &c upto निश in VI. 1. 63. Thus निपुणैश्चतुरो अहि, या इ साँधावति, अर्पैः पद्यः, अज्जैः, अदृश्यैः, पुंसैः, पुण्यैः, पुण्यैः, पुंसौ, पुंसै, रार्यैः पद्य, राभ्यैष, राभैः, दिवैः, दिवैः, दिवैः ॥ As regards the other cases of दिव् the accent is governed by VI. 1. 183. The word असत् and those which follow it, in VI. 1. 63, are not governed by this rule because they consist of more than one vowel, and the anuvritti of एकाचः is understood here from VI. 1. 168. When these become monosyllable by the elision of अ (penultimate), then the vibhakti will be udātta by VI. 1. 161 even after these. The case endings after these words are of course, anudātta, except when these words become monosyllabic:—As श्रीवायां बन्धो अपि कश्च आसनि, मत्स्यं न दीन उर्दीनि क्षियन्तं ॥

अष्टनो दीर्घात् ॥ १७२ ॥ पदानि ॥ अष्टनः, दीर्घात् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अष्टनो दीर्घान्तादसर्वनामस्थानविभक्तिद्वान्ता भवति ॥

172. The asarvanāmasthāna case-endings after अष्टन् 'eight', have acute accent, when it gets the form अष्टा ॥

The word अष्टन् has two forms in the acc. pl. and the other cases that follow it, namely अष्टा and अष्ट ॥ The affixes of acc. pl. &c are udātta after the long form अष्टा and not after अष्ट ॥ Thus अष्टाभिः opposed to अष्टेभिः, अष्टाभ्यः con. अष्टेभ्यः, अष्टाच्च con. अष्टेच्च ॥ The word अष्टेन has acute on the last syllable, as it belongs to the class of पदादि words (Phit I. 21); and by VI. 1. 180 the accent would have been on the penultimate syllable. This rule debars it. The use of दीर्घात् indicates that the word अष्टन् has two forms, and the substitution of long अ taught in VII. 2. 84, thus becomes optional, because of this indication. Otherwise the employment of the word दीर्घात् would be useless, for by VII. 2. 84 which is couched in general terms, अष्टन् would always end in a long vowel. There is another use of the word दीर्घात्, namely, it makes the word अष्टान् with long आ (VII. 2. 84) to get also the designation of पद ॥ For if अष्टान् was not to be called a पद, like अष्टन्, then there would be scope to the present sūtra in the case of अष्टान् while it would be debarred in the case of अष्टन् without long आ, by the subsequent rule VI. 1. 180 which applies to पद word, and hence the employment of the word दीर्घात् would become useless.

शत्रुसुमो नद्यजादी ॥ १७३ ॥ पदानि ॥ शत्रुः, अनुमः, नदी, अजादी ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अन्तोवासाविति वच्यते । अनुवयः शत्रुवत्यस्तदन्तादन्तोवासावपरा नदी अजादिविभक्तिरसर्वनामस्थानवृत्तान्ता भवति ॥

वैश्विकम् ॥ ब्रह्ममहतीरपसंख्यानम् ॥

173. After an oxytone Participle in अत् the feminine suffix ई, (nadi) and the case endings beginning with vowels

BK. VI. CH. I. §. 175.]

VIBHAKTI-ACCENT.

1119

(with the exception of strong cases) have acute accent, when the participial affix has not the augment न (i. e. is not अन्त).

The word अन्तोवाचात् 'after an oxytoned word' is understood here. Thus तुवती, तुवती, लुनती, पुनती, तुवती, लुनती, पुनती, लुनती from तुवैत, तुवैत लुनैत and पुनैत ॥

Why do we say "not having the augment नुम्?" Observe तुवैन्ती, तुवैन्ती ॥ Here also by VI. I. 186, after the root तुव् which has an indicatory अ, in the Dhātupāṭha, being written तुव्, the sārvadhāṭuka affix शतु (अत्) is anu-dātta. This anudātta अत्, coalescing with the udātta अ of तुव् (VI. I. 162), becomes udātta (VIII. 2. 5); and Rule VIII. 2. 1 not being held applicable here, the Participle gets the accent, and not the feminine affix. Why do we say "a नदी (feminine in ई) word and before vowel-endings?" Observe तुवैद्भ्याम, तुवैद्भ्याम &c. If the participle is not an oxytone, the rule does not apply. As वैदवी, वैदवी ॥ Here the accent is on the first syllable by VI. I. 189.

Vārt:—The words वृहती and महती should also be included: as वृहती महती, वृहती, महती ॥

उदात्तयणो हृत्पूर्वात् ॥ १७४ ॥ पदानि ॥ उदात्त, यणः, हृत्, पूर्वात् ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ उदात्तस्थानं यो यण् हृत्पूर्वस्तस्मात्परा नदी अजादिषां स्सर्वनामस्थानविभक्तिरुदात्ता भवति ॥
वार्तिकम् ॥ नकारमहणं च कर्तव्यम् ॥

174. The same endings have the acute accent, when for the acutely accented final vowel of the stem, a semi-vowel is substituted, and which is preceded by a consonant.

Thus कर्त + ई = कर्ती; कर्ता, हर्ता, हर्ती, प्रतिवर्ती, प्रतिवर्ती ॥ प्रतिवर्ती, प्रतिवर्ती ॥ All these are तुव् ending words and have consequently acute accent on the final (VI. I. 163). Why 'actually accented final vowel is replaced &c'? Observe कर्ती, कर्ती, हर्ती, हर्ती, formed by तुव् having acute on the first syllable. Why do we say 'preceded by a consonant'? Observe बहुतितवै - बहुतितवै ब्राह्मण्या (VIII. 2. 4) बहूनि तितकनि अस्या इति बहुश्रीहि ॥ This compound with बहु gets udātta on the final by VI. 2. 175. In making the Instrumental singular of बहुतितवै, the उ is replaced by व्, but as this व् is preceded by a vowel, the affix gets the svarita accent.

Vārt:—The rule applies when the stem ends in न् though not in a semi-vowel, as वाक्पक्षी, चित्पक्षी ॥

नोङ् धात्वोः ॥ १७५ ॥ पदानि ॥ न, ऊङ्, धात्वोः ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ ऊङ् धात्वोः य उदात्तयण् हृत्पूर्वस्तस्मात्परा जाजासर्वनामस्थानविभक्तिरुदात्ता भवति ॥

175. But not so, when the vowel is of the feminine affix ऊ (IV. 1. 66), or the final of a root.

After the semi-vowel substitutes of the udātta ऊ (IV. 1. 66) or of the udātta final vowels of the root, when preceded by a consonant, the weak case-

1120

VIBHATI-ACCENT.

[BK. VI. CH. I. §. 176]

endings beginning with a vowel do not take the acute accent. Thus ब्रह्मबद्धां, ब्रह्मबद्धां, धीरबद्धां, धीर बद्धां from धीरबद्धां, which has acute accent on ऊ, because ऊँच is udatta (III. 1. 3), and the ekadesa of it, when it combines with the preceding vowel is also udatta (VIII. 2. 5). The व substituted for ऊ before the ending आ, is a semi-vowel substitute of an udatta (उदात्तयण्) the affix after it would have become udatta by the last sutra, but not being so, the general rule VIII. 2. 4 applies and makes it svarita. Let us take an example of a semi-vowel substitute of the vowel of a root (धातु-यण्):—सकुल्लुं, सकुल्लुं; खलुण्डं from सकुल्लुं, खलुण्डं formed by क्रीष् affix, the second member of the compound retaining its original accent, namely, the oxytone, the semi-vowel being substituted by VI. 4. 83 before the vowel case-endings.

हस्वतुङ्ग्यां मतुप् ॥ १७६ ॥ पदानि ॥ हस्व, तुङ्ग्याम्, मतुप् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अन्तोदात्तादिव्येव । हस्वान्तादन्तोदात्तानुत्तृध्वपरोमतुप् उदात्तो भवति ॥

वृत्तिकम् ॥ रेशब्धाश्च मतुप् उदात्तत्वं वक्तव्यम् ॥ वा० ॥ चैव प्रतिषेधो वक्तव्यः ॥

176. The otherwise unaccented मत (वृत्त) takes the acute accent, when an oxytoned stem ends in a light vowel, or the affix has before it the augment न (VIII. 2. 16).

The word अन्तोदात्तान् is understood here also. Thus अभिमान्, वायुमान्, कर्तुमान्, हर्तुमान् ॥ So also when मतुप् takes नुत, as अश्वप्यन्ता, ईश्वरप्यन्ता ॥ Here by VII. 1. 76, the word अश्वि takes अनड and becomes अशन्, then is added नुत by VIII. 2. 16, and we have अशन् न मतुप् ॥ The preceding न is elided. When the stem is not oxytone (antodatta) this rule does not apply: as वैद्युमान् ॥ The word वैद्यु has acute on the first syllable, as it is formed from वत्त with the affix उ (Un I. 10) which is नित् (Un I. 9) so the मतुप् retains its anudatta here. So also in the case of मरुत्वान्, the affix does not become acute, though the word मरुत्व has acute on the final as the intervening न makes the उ of क heavy when the affix is added: the general maxim स्वरविधो व्यंजनमविधमानवत् does not apply here, because the very fact that न is only taken as an exception, shows this.

Vårt:—The affix मतुप् becomes acute after the heavy vowel of रे : as आरैर्वान=रथिरस्यास्ति ॥ There is vocalisation of य of रथि, as र इ ह then substitution of one, as र इ, then guna, रे ॥

Vårt:—The prohibition should be stated after वि : as विवर्तीयाज्यानु-प्राक्या भवन्ति ॥

नामन्यतरस्याम् ॥ १७७ ॥ पदानि ॥ नाम, अन्यतरस्याम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ हस्वमहामनुवर्तते मतुवमहं च । तेन मतुपा हस्वो विश्वेभ्यते । मतुपि यो हस्वस्तदन्तादन्तोक्ष-तादन्यतरस्यां नाम उदात्तो भवति ॥

177. After an oxytoned stem which ends in a light vowel, the genitive ending नाम has optionally the acute accent.

BK. VI. CH. I § 179. ]

VIBHAKTI-ACCENT.

1121

Thus अग्नीनाम् or अग्नीनाम्, वायूनाम् or वायूनाम्, कर्तृणाम् or कर्तृणाम् (see VII. I. 54). It might be objected, that नाम् is not preceded by a short vowel, as is shown in the above examples, then how can the anuvritti of ब्रह्म 'short or light vowel' be read into this sutra? The reply is that the anuvritti of मत्तु should also be read into this sutra, the meaning being "a stem which has a light vowel when followed by मत्तु, will cause the नाम acute, though the light vowel may become heavy before this ending, in its present form". Otherwise, this rule will apply to forms like तिसृणाम्, चतसृणाम् having light vowels before नाम् and not to the forms above given. Why do we read नाम् with the बृह् augment (VII. I. 54) and not आम्? The rule will not apply to धेन्वाम् शक्याम् which get the acute on the final by VI. I. 174. Why do we say 'after a stem ending in a light vowel'? Observe कुमारीणाम् (the word कुमारे is end-acute by Un III. 138 and so is कुमारी by VI. I. 161). Why do we say after an oxytoned word? Observe वैष्णवाम्, वैष्णवाम् the words षषु and षषु have acute on the first syllable.

इयाश्चन्दसि बहुलम् ॥ १७८ ॥ पदानि ॥ इयाः, छन्दसि, बहुलम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इयन्ताच्छन्दसि विषये नासुशान्तो भवति बहुलम् ॥

178. In the Chhandas, the ending नाम has diversely the acute accent after the feminine affix ई ॥

Thus देवसेनानाम् अभिभञ्जतीनाम्, बह्वीनाम् पिता ॥ Sometimes it does not take place, as नंदीनाम् पारे; जयन्तीनाम् मरुतः ॥

पट्ट्रिचतुभ्यो हलादिः ॥ १७९ ॥ पदानि ॥ पट्ट्रि, चतुभ्यः, हलादिः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अन्तोदात्तादित्येतन्नित्येतम्। पट्ट्रसंज्ञकेभ्यस्ति चतुर् इत्येताभ्यां च परा हलादिर्विभक्तिस्तात्ता भवति ॥

179. The case-endings beginning with a consonant, have the acute accent after the Numerals called पद् (I. 1. 24), as well as after त्रि and चतुर् ॥

The anuvritti of अन्तोदात्ताद् ceases, for the present rule applies even to words like वैष्णव and नैष्णव which are acute on the initial by Phit II. 5. Thus प्रणणाम्, षड्भिः, षड्भ्यः, पंचानाम्, ससानाम्, विभिः, विभ्यः, त्रयाणाम्, चतुष्णाम् (See VII. I. 55). Why do we say 'before case-affixes beginning with consonants'? Observe चैतसः पदम् (VI. I. 167 and VII. 2. 99).

इत्युपोत्तमम् ॥ १८० ॥ पदानि ॥ इळि, उपोत्तमम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पट्ट्रिचतुभ्यो वा इत्यादिर्विभक्तिस्तात्ते पदे यदुपोत्तममुदात्तं भवति। विप्रभूतीनामन्यमुत्तमं तत्समीपे च यतदुपोत्तमम् ॥

180. The above numerals, when taking a case-affix beginning with a भ् or स्, get the acute accent on the penultimate syllable, when the said numerals assume a form consisting of three or more syllables.

1122

ACCENT.

[ Bk. VI. Ch. I. §. 182

The numerals षट्, षि and चतुर् when ending in a case-affix beginning with a झल् consonant, form a full word (षट्), in such a word the penultimate syllable gets the acute accent. The very word penultimate shows that the षट् must be of three syllables at least. Thus पंचमिः, सप्तमिः, तिसमिः, चतुर्मिः ॥ Why do we say 'beginning with म् and स्'? Observe, पंचमाम्, सप्तमाम् ॥ Why do we say 'the penultimate syllable'? Observe षड्मिः, षड्मिः ॥

विभाषा भाषायाम् ॥ १८१ ॥ पदानि ॥ विभाषा, भाषायाम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ षट्चिचतुर्यो वा झलादिर्विभक्तिस्तदन्ते षट् उपोत्तममुद्यन्तं भवति विभाषा भाषायां विषये ॥

181. In the Secular language this is optional.

The झलादि case-affixes coming after the above numerals षट्, षि and चतुर् may make the words so formed take the acute on the penultimate optionally, in the spoken ordinary language. Thus पंचमिः or पंचमिः ॥ In the alternative VI. I. 179 applies. So also सप्तमिः or सप्तमिः, तिसमिः or तिसमिः ॥

न गोश्वन्साववर्णराडङ्कुङ्कद्भ्यः ॥ १८२ ॥ पदानि ॥ न. गो, श्वन्, सौ अवर्ण, राड्, अङ्, कुङ्, कद्भ्यः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ गो श्वन् साववर्ण सौ प्रथमैकवचने यदवर्णान्तं राड् अङ् कुङ् कद इत्येतेभ्यो यदुक्तं तत्र भवति ॥

182. The foregoing rules from VI. I. 168 downwards have no applicability after गो, and श्वन् and words ending in them; nor after a stem which before the case ending of the Nominative singular has अ or आ, nor after राज्, or after a stem ending in अञ्च्, nor as well as after कुञ्च् and कुत् ॥

Thus गैवा, गेवे, गोभ्याम् ॥ Here by VI. I. 168, the case-endings would have got otherwise the accent, which is however prohibited. So also सुगैना, सुगैवे and सुगैभ्याम् ॥ Here VI. I. 169 is prohibited. So also गैना, गैने, गैभ्याम्, परमगैना, परमगैने and परमगैभ्याम् ॥ The word साववर्णः (सौ अवर्णः) means 'what has अ or आ' before सु (1st. sing.) Thus 'गैभ्यः', 'तेभ्यः', 'केभ्यः' ॥ राज्-रैजा, रैजे, परमरैजा ॥ (The word राज् is formed by किप् affix): अङ्=अञ्च्+किप्; the prohibition applies to that form of this word wherein the nasal is not elided (VI. 4. 30). Thus गैञ्चा, गैञ्च्याम् ॥ Where the nasal is elided, there the case-ending must take the accent; as प्राचै, प्राचै प्राग्याम् ॥ कुङ् is also a किप् formed word. Thus कुञ्चा, कुञ्चे, परमकुञ्चा ॥ कुत् is derived from क् 'to do' or from कुत् 'to cut' by किप्; as क्त्ता क्त्ते and परमक्त्ता ॥ Why has the word श्वन् been especially mentioned in this sutra, when the rule would have applied to it even without such enumeration, because in the Nominative Singular this word assumes the form श्वा and consequently it is साववर्णः? The inclusion of श्वन् indicates that the elision of न should not be considered asiddha for the purposes of this rule. Therefore, the present rule will not apply to words like न् and पित् which in Nom. Sing. end in आ, as ना and पितां after the elision of न् of अनङ्ग (VII. 3. 94). Thus the Locative Singular of न् will

BK. VI. CH. I § 186 ]

VIBHAKTI ACCENT.

1123

be नरे$^{7}$ by VI. I. 168, this prohibition not applying, and the affix मनुष्य will get udatta after पिता by VI. I. 176 as पितृमौन् ॥ But rule VI. I. 176 will be debarred by the present in the case of वृक्षवान् because वृक्ष is a सावर्ण ॥

दिवो झल् ॥ १८३ ॥ पदानि ॥ दिवः, झल् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ दिवः परा झलादिविभक्तिनोदात्ता भवति ॥

183. After दिव् a case-ending beginning with म or स is unaccented.

Thus वृक्षान्, वृक्षः ॥ This debars VI. I. 168, 171. Why do we say 'beginning with a झल् consonant'? Observe दिवो, दिवे ॥

नृ चान्यतरस्याम् ॥ १८४ ॥ पदानि ॥ नृ, च, अन्यतरस्याम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ नृ इत्येतस्मात्परा झलादिविभक्तिन्यतरस्यां नोदात्ता भवति ॥

184. After नृ, a case ending beginning with म or स is optionally unaccented.

Thus वृक्षः or वृक्षः, वृक्षः, वृक्षः, वृक्षान्, वृक्षान्, वृक्षः, वृक्षः ॥ But not so वृक्षः, वृक्षः ॥

तितस्वरितम् ॥ १८५ ॥ पदानि ॥ तित, स्वरितम्, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तितस्वरितं भवति ॥

185. An affix having an indicatory न, is svarita i. e. has circumflex accent.

Thus चित्तीर्थम्, चित्तीर्थम्, formed by यत् (III. I. 97). कार्यम्, कार्यम् with ण्यत् (III. I. 124). This is an exception to III. I. 3 which makes all affixes ādyudatta. For exception to this rule see VI. I. 213 &c.

तास्यनुदात्तेनडिदुपदेशाल्लासार्धधातुकमनुदात्तमहन्धिडोः ॥ १८६ ॥ पदानि ॥ तासि, अनुदात्तेत्, डिद्, अनुपदेशात्, ल, सार्वधातुकम्, अनुदात्तम्, अ-मु, इडो, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तासेरनुदात्तेनडिडोः ऊकारान्तोपदेशाच्च रक्षात्परं लसार्धधातुकमनुदात्तं च भवति हुड् इड् इत्य-ताभ्यां परं वर्जयित्वा ॥

186. The Personal-endings and their substitutes (III. 2. 124-126) are, when they are sārvadhātuka (III. 4. 113 &c), unaccented, after the characteristic of the Periphrastic future (तासि), after a root which in the Dhātupātha has an unaccented vowel or a ङ् (with the exception of हुड् and इड्) as indicatory letter, as well as after what has a final अ in the Grammatical system of Instruction (upadesa).

Thus तासि:—कत्ती, कत्तीरो, कत्तीः, this debars the affix accent (III. I. 3). Anudāttet:—as, आस्—आस्ते, वस्—वैस्ते ॥ डित्:—इड्—इते, शीड्—शेते ॥ अत् उप-देशः:—as द्वैततः, द्वैततः, पँचतः, पँचतः ॥ A root taking शप् (अ) is considered as

1124

ACCENT.

[ Bk. VI. Ch. I. § 137 ]

taught (upadesa) as if ending with an अ, as the indicatory letters ण् and ण् are disregarded on the maxim अनुबन्धस्यानैकान्तिकत्वं (= अनवयवत्वं) ॥ Thus पंचमानः, यजमानः ॥ The augment मुक is added by आनि मुक VII. 2. 82 which may be explained in two ways; first, the augment मुक is added to the final अ of the base (anga) when आन (आनच् &c) follows; or secondly, the the augment मुक is added to the base (anga) which ends in अ, when आनें follows. In the first case मक् becomes part and parcel of अ and will be taken and included by the enunciation of अ, and therefore अनुपदेश will mean and include an अ having such मुक, on the maxim यदागमास्तदुर्गमुतास्तदुमहणेन गुह्यन्ते "That to which an augment is added denotes, because the augment forms part of it, not merely itself, but it denotes also whatever results from its combination with that augment". Therefore मुक will not prevent the verb becoming अनुपदेश ॥ But if secondly मक् be taken as part of the base which ends in अ, then the लसावधातुक does not follow an अनुपदेश, because म intervenes. But we get rid of this difficulty by considering मुक augment as Bahiranga and therefore asiddha, when the Antaranga operation of accent is to be performed. The augment मुक (म्) in the last two examples consequently does not prevent the application of the rule. Though the affix शानच् has an indicatory च, yet चित् accent (VI. 1. 163) is debarred by this rule, as it is subsequent.

Why do we say after तासि &c. Observe चितुतः चिन्तनिः ॥ The vikaraṇa ण् is डित् (I. 2. 4) with regard to operations affecting the prior term, and not those which affect the subsequent. Therefore though ण् is considered as डित् for the purposes of preventing the guna of the prior term चि, it will not be considered so for the purposes of subsequent accent. Or the word डित् in this sūtra may be taken as equal to डित्पदेश and not the आतिशीक डित् like डतु ॥

Why do we use the word upadesa? So that the rule may apply to पैचावः, पचामः, but not to हतः, हयः the dual of हत् which ends in न् in upadesa. though before तस् and यस् it has assumed the form ह ॥ Therefore हतः हयः ॥ Why do we use the word ल (Personal endings)? Observe कतिह पैवमाना formed by शानच् added to प् (III. 2. 128), which not being a substitute of लद्, is not a personal ending like शानच् ॥ Why do we use the word Sārvadhātuka? Observe शिदेवै, शिदवैति, शि-दिये ॥ Why do we say with the exception of हतुह् and इह्? Observe हतुह्, यद् अधीते ॥

आदिः सिचो ऽन्यतरस्याम् ॥ १८७ ॥ पदानि ॥ आदिः, सिचः, अन्यतरस्याम्, युक्तिः ॥ उदात्त इति वर्तते । सिजन्तस्यान्यतरस्यामादिरुदात्तो भवति ॥
वार्तिकम् ॥ सिच आयुदात्तत्वे ऽनितः पितः पते उदात्तत्वं वक्तव्यम् ॥

187. In सिच् Aorist, the first syllable may optionally have the acute accent.

The word उदात्त is understood here. Thus मा हि कादीनः, मा हि कादीनः; मा हि लेविहाम् or मा हि लाविहाम् ॥ In the last example the accent is on पि; and the

BK. VI. CH. I. §. 189 ]

VERB-ACCENT.

1125

reason why मा and हि are used in these illustrations, has already been explained in VI. I. 161. The indicatory च् of सिच् shows that by VI. I. 163 the acute will be on the otherwise unaccented augment इद, when it takes this augment. The सिच् being a वलावि affix will take the augment इद (VII. 2. 35), and it is a general rule that augments are unaccented; so in the above the वि would have been unaccented, and the accent would have been on the final, but for the indicatory च् of सिच्, which otherwise would find no scope. Thus वि gets acute.

*Vārti*:—An affix having an indicatory प् (पित्) when coming after an Aorist formed by सिच् without the augment इद (अनिद् सिच्) is in one alternative udātta (in the other, it is non-acute). This vārtika restricts the scope of the sūtra with regard to पित् affixes. Thus we get the following two forms, which otherwise would have one form only by dhātu-accent, namely, acute on the first, for पित् is anudātta. Thus माहि कार्पम् or मा हि कार्पम् ॥ But when it takes the इद augment, there are two forms (1st.) मा हि लेविषम् as a तिडन्त, (2nd.) मा हि लाविषम् accent on वि (VI. I. 163). but never मा हि लाविषम् ॥ When however the augment अ is added, the accent falls on this augment (VI. 4. 71).

स्वपादिहिंसामच्यनिति ॥ १८८ ॥ पदानि ॥ स्वपादि, हिंसाम, अचि, अनिति ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ लसार्धातुकमहणं यदुवर्तते तदच्यनितीति सम्बन्धादिह समन्यन्तं भवति स्वपादीनां हिंसेधाजा-शावनिति लसार्धातुके परतो ऽन्यतरस्यामादिरुवातो भवति ॥

188. The acute accent is optionally on the first syllable when a Personal-ending, being a Sārvadhātuka tense affix beginning with a vowel, provided that the vowel is not the augment इद, follows after स्वप् &c, or after हिंस ॥

The phrase लसार्धातुके in the locative case is understood here. Thus स्वपन्ति or स्वपन्ति, भंसन्ति or भसन्ति, हिंसन्ति or हिंसन्ति ॥ The accent on the middle falls by the accent of the affix III. I. 3. Why do we say 'before an affix beginning with a vowel'? Observe स्वप्यौन्, हिंस्यौन् ॥ Why do we say 'not taking the augment इद?' Observe स्वपितैः and भसितैः ॥ This rule applies to those vowel-beginning affixes which are डिन्; it does not apply to स्वपानि, हिंसानि ॥

अभ्यस्तानामादिः ॥ १८९ ॥ पदानि ॥ अभ्यस्तानाम्, आदिः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अभ्यस्तानामादावनिति लसार्धातुके परतं आदिरुवातो भवति ॥

189. The acute accent falls on the first syllable of the reduplicate verbs when followed by an affix beginning with a vowel (the vowel being not इद) and being a sārvadhātuka personal ending.

Thus ईदति, ईदतु, ईधति, ईधतु, अंसति, अंसतु, अंसति, अंसतु ॥ Before consonant affixes: इद्यात् ॥ Before सेद affixes:—असितैः ॥ Though the word आदि was

12

1126

VERB-ACCENT.

[ Bk. VI. Ch. I. § 158

understood here from the last aphorism, the repetition is for the sake of making this an *invariable* rule and not an *optional* rule as those in the foregoing.

अनुदाते च ॥ १९० ॥ पदानि ॥ अनुदाते, च, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अविद्यमानोदाते च लसार्धधातुके परतो ऽभ्यस्तानामादिरुदात्तो भवति ॥

190. Also when the unaccented endings of the three persons in the singular follow, the first syllable of the reduplicate has the acute.

The endings तिप् सिप् and मिप् are anudatta (III. 1. 4). This sutra applies to those personal endings which do not begin with a vowel. Thus दैदाति, जैहाति, दैधाति, जिहीति, मिथीति ॥ The word अनुदात्त is to be construed here as a Bahuvrihi i. e. an affix in which there is no udatta vowel, so that the rule may apply when a portion of the affix is elided or a semivowel is substituted : as मा हि स दैधात्, and दैधात्यत्र ॥

सर्वस्य सुपि ॥ १९१ ॥ पदानि ॥ सर्वस्य, सुपि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सर्वशब्दस्य सुपि परत आदिरुदात्तो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ सर्वस्यो ऽनकङ्कस्येति वङ्कव्यम् ॥

191. The acute is on the first syllable of सर्व when the case-endings follow.

Thus सर्वः, सर्वैः सर्वैः ॥ Why do we say when the *case-endings* follow? Observe सर्वैतरः, सर्वैतमः the acute is on वै ॥ The word सर्व has acute on the final, as it is so taught in the Uṇādi list by निपातत् ॥ It thus being anudattādi takes the affix अस् and forms सार्वः (सर्वस्य विकारः) This rule applies even when the case affix is elided in spite of the prohibition of न लुमताङ्गस्य (I. 1. 63) : as सर्वैस्तोमः ॥

*Vārt* :—The rule does not apply when the affix अकङ्क is put in : as सर्वैः ॥ Here the accent is on the final by चित् accent (VI. 1. 163).

भीहीभूहुमदजनधनदरिद्राजागरां प्रत्ययात्पूर्वं पिति ॥ १९२ ॥ पदानि ॥ भी, ही, भू, हु, मद, जन, धन, दरिद्रा, जागराम, प्रत्ययात, पूर्वम्, पिति ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ भी ही भू हु मद जन धन दरिद्रा जागु इत्येतेषामभ्यस्तानां लसार्धधातुके पिति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वमुदात्तं भवति ॥

192. In भी, ही, भू, हु, मद, जन, धन, दरिद्रा, and जागु, in their reduplicates, the acute accent is, before the sār-vadhātuka unaccented endings of the three persons in singular, (पित), on the syllable which precedes the affix.

This debars the accent on the beginning. Thus बिभीति, जिहीति, बिभीति, जिहीति, मर्मसु नः परिजमा ॥ Here the root मद has diversely taken in the Chhandas the vikaraṇa ऽहु, though it belongs to Divādi class. जर्जैनत्, इन्द्रम् ॥ The verb is here लेद् or the Vedic Subjunctive, so also is the next example. वचनम् from धन धान्ये,

BK. VI. CH. I. §. 159]

VERB-ACCENT.

1127

the ई of नि being elided by III. 4. 97, and the augment अद् being added by III. 4. 94. इध्मन्, परिद्रिति, जामन्ति ॥ In the case of other verbs we have ईदाति ॥ Before affixes which have not the indicatory ए (i. e. all endings other than the three singular endings), the accent will be on the first syllable: as ईरिद्रिति ॥

लिति ॥ १९३ ॥ पदानि ॥ लिति ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ लिति प्रत्ययाख्युप्रभूवात् भवति ।

193. The acute accent falls on the syllable immediately preceding the affix that has an indicatory ल् ॥

Thus चिकीर्षकः, जिहीर्षकः with the affix णुल् (III. 1. 133), भौरिकिविधम् and ऐपुकारि भैक्तम् with the affixes विधल् and भक्तल् (IV. 2. 54) accent on the कि and रि ॥

आदिर्णमुल्यन्यतरस्याम् ॥ १९४ ॥ पदानि ॥ आदिः, णमुलि, अन्यतरस्याम् ॥

वृत्तिः । णमुलि परतो ऽन्यतरस्यामादिरुवात्तो भवति ।

194. The first syllable may be optionally acute when the absolutive affix णमुल् follows.

Thus लोलूयम् or लोलूयम् ॥ In the reduplicate form लोलू, the second part लु is unaccented by VIII. 1. 3. The present sūtra makes लो accented. When लो is not accented, लु will get the accent by लिल् accent. This rule is confined to polysyllabic Absolutives, namely to reduplicated Absolutives (VIII. 1. 4).

अचः कर्तृयकि ॥ १९५ ॥ पदानि ॥ अचः, कर्तृयकि ॥

वृत्तिः । उपदेशइति वर्तते । अजन्ताये उपदेशे धातवस्तेषां कर्तृयकि अन्यतरस्यामादिरुवात्तो भवति ।

195. The roots which are exhibited in Dhātupāṭha with a final vowel, may optionally have the acute on the first syllable, before the affixes of the Passive (यक्), when the sense of the verb is Reflexive.

The word उपदेश is understood here. Thus लूयते or लूयते केवारः स्वयमेव ॥ सीयते or सीयते केवारः स्वयमेव ॥ When the accent does not fall on the first syllable, it falls on य (VI. 1. 186). This rule applies to जन्, खन्, and सन् when they get the form जायते, सायते and खायते; the long आ (VI. 4. 43) substitute is considered as if these verbs were taught in the Dhātupāṭha with long आ ॥ Thus जायते or जायते स्वयमेव सीयते or सीयते स्वयमेव; सीयते or खायते स्वयमेव ॥ Why do we say 'when ending in a vowel'? Observe भिर्यते स्वयमेव ॥ Why do we say 'when the sense is Reflexive (कर्तृ)'? Observe लूयते केवारो देववृत्तेन ॥

थलि च सेटीडन्तो वा ॥ १९६ ॥ पदानि ॥ थलि, च, सेटि, इडन्तः, वा ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सेटि थलि इड वा उवात्तो भवति अन्तो वा आदिर्यो ऽन्यतरस्याम् ।

1128

VERB-ACCENT.

[ Bk. VI. Ch. I. § 199

196. Before the ending थ of the Perfect, second person singular, when this ending takes the augment ङ; the acute accent falls either on the first syllable, or on this ङ, or on the personal ending.

Thus लुलविथ, लुलविथ, लुलविथ, and लुलावैथ. As थल् has an indicatory ङ, the syllable preceding the affix may have also the accent (VI. I. 193). Thus we get the four forms given above. In short, with ङथ termination, the accent may fall on any syllable. When the थ is not सेङ, the accent falls on the root and we have one form only by लिङ् accent (VI. I. 193):—यथाँथ ॥

अनित्यादिर्नित्यम ॥ १९७ ॥ पदानि ॥ भिन्ति, आदिः, नित्यम ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ भिन्ति भिन्ति च नित्यमादिह्वात्तो भवति ।

197. Whatever is derived with an affix having an indicatory ञ or ञ, has the acute accent invariably on the first syllable.

Thus गाँर्य with यम् (IV. I. 105), वैद्युदेवकः, अँजुनकः with वृन् (IV. 3. 98). This is an exception to III. I. 3. When the affixes are, however, elided, the word loses this accent, i. e. the affix does not leave its mark behind, as it generally does by I. I. 62. Therefore गाँर्यः, विदीः, चञ्चोः having lost प्रम्, अम् and कम्, have lost their accent also.

आमन्त्रितस्य च ॥ १९८ ॥ पदानि ॥ आमन्त्रितस्य, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आमन्त्रितस्यादिह्वात्तो भवति ।

198. The first syllable of a Vocative gets the acute accent.

Thus 'देवदत्तः !, 'देवदत्तो !, 'देवदत्ताः ॥ This debars the final accent ordained by VI. 2. 148. Though the affix may be elided by a लुमान् word (लुक्, लुप् or लङ्), yet the effect of the affix remains behind in spite of I. I. 63. As सैपिरा-गच्छ ! सैपिरा गच्छत ! ॥

पथिमथोः सर्वनामस्थाने ॥ १९९ ॥ पदानि ॥ पथि, मथोः, सर्वनामस्थाने ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पथिमथिद्वाद्वायोगादिकाविनिप्रत्ययान्तो प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोश्चात्तो तथोः सर्वनामस्थाने परत आदिः ह्वात्तो भवति ।

199. The acute accent is on the first syllable of पथिन् and मथिन् when followed by a strong case-ending.

The words पथिन् and मथिन् are derived by the Unādi affix इति, (IV. 12. and 13) and are oxytone by III. I. 3. They become ādyudātta before strong cases. Thus पैन्या, पैन्यानो, पैन्यानः, मैन्याः, मैन्यानो, मैन्यानः ॥ Before other cases we have:—पथैः पद्य, मथैः पद्य ॥ The accent is on the final by VI. I. 162, there being elision of the udātta इन् ॥ The rule I. I. 62, about the remaining effect of the affix, does not apply here. As पथिमिथः, has acute on the final of the first

BK. VI. Ch. I. § 203 ]

FIRST-ACUTE.

1129

word, by retaining its original accent.

अन्तश्च तवै युगपत् ॥ २०० ॥ पदानि ॥ अन्तः, च, तवै, युगपत्, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तवैप्रत्ययान्तस्यान्तश्चशब्दादिश्व युगपद्वदातो भवतः ।

200. The Infinitive in तवै has the acute on the first syllable and on the last syllable at one and the same time.

Thus क्तवै, ह्तवै ॥ This is an exception to III. 1. 3 by which त of तवै ought to have got the accent, and it also countermands rule VI. 1. 158 by which there can be only a single acute in a single word.

क्षयो निवासे ॥ २०१ ॥ पदानि ॥ क्षयः, निवासे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ क्षयशब्दो निवासे अभिधेये आह्वादातो भवति ।

201. The word क्षय has the acute on the first syllable in the sense of 'house, dwelling'.

Thus क्षेये जागृहि प्रपद्यत् ॥ The word is formed by ष affix (III. 1. 118) and would have had accent on the affix (III. 1. 3). When not meaning a house we have: क्षयो वर्तते दृश्यनाम् ॥ The word is formed by अच् (III. 2. 31),

जयः करणम् ॥ २०२ ॥ पदानि ॥ जयः, करणम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ जयशब्दः करणवाची आह्वादातो भवति ॥

202. The acute accent falls on the first syllable of जय, in the sense of 'whereby one attains victory'.

Thus जैयोऽभ्यः, but otherwise जयो वर्तते ब्राह्मणानाम् ॥ The former जय is by ष affix, (III. 1. 118) the second by अच् (III. 2. 31) ॥

वृषादीनां च ॥ २०३ ॥ पदानि ॥ वृषादीनाम्, च, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ वृष इत्यवमादीनामादिश्वदातो भवति ॥

203. The words वृष &c have the acute on the first syllable.

Thus 1. वृषः, 2. जैनः, 3. उर्वरः, 4. मैनः, 5. हेयः, 6. गेयः ॥ These are formed by अच् (III. 1. 134). The word गय is from गे-गायते, irregularly it is treated as गे ॥ 7. नयः, 8. तायः, 9. तयः, 10. चयः, 11. अमः, 12. वेदः, 13. सूदः, 14. वदः (formed by अच् numbers 8 to 11 are not in Kāśika). सूद is formed by क (III. 1. 135) 15. अंशः, 16. गुहा (formed by अच् III. 3. 104). 17. शमरणो संज्ञायां संमतौ भावकर्मणोः :— शमः and रणः, 18. मन्त्रः (formed by अच् III. 1. 134), 19. शान्तिः formed by खिच्च, 20. कामः, 21. यामः, both formed by घम्, 22. आरा, 23. धारा, 24. कारा, (all three formed by अच् III. 3. 104), 25. वहः = गोचरादिषु formed by घम् 26. कल्पः, 27. पादः formed by घम्, which may either take the accent indicated by the affix or by VI. 1. 159, 28. पयः, 29. वदः ॥ It is आकृतिगणः ॥ All words which are acutely accented on the first, should be considered as belonging to this class, if their accent cannot be accounted for by any other rule.

1130

FIRST-ACUTE.

[ Bk. VI. Ch. I § 206.

1 वृक्षः, 2 जनः, 3 उवर, 4 महः, 5 हयः, 6 गयः, 7 नयः, 8 तायः, 9 तवः, 10 चयः, 11 भ्रमः, 12 वेदः, 13 मृदः, 14 अंशः, 15 सुहः, 16 शमरणी संज्ञायां संमती भावकमणोः, 17 मन्त्रः, 18 शान्तिः, 19 कामः, 20 यामः, 21 आरा, 22 धारा, 23 कारा, 24 बहः, 25 कल्पः, 26 पादः, 27 पयः, 28 इवः, 29 आकृतिगणः ॥

संज्ञायामुपमानम् ॥ २०४ ॥ पदानि ॥ संज्ञायाम्, उपमानम् ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ उपमानशब्दः संज्ञायामायुवाचो भवति ॥

204. The acute accent falls on the first syllable of that word with which something is likened, provided that it is a name.

Thus चञ्चा, वैष्णिका, वैष्णुकुटी, वैष्णी ॥ All these are उपमान words used as names of the उपमेय (the thing compared). The affix कन् (V. 3. 96) is elided here by V. 3. 98. It might be asked when कन् is elided, its mark, namely causing the first syllable to be acute (VI. 1. 197), will remain behind by virtue of I. 1. 62, where is then the necessity of this sutra. The formation of this sutra indicates that the प्रत्ययलक्षण rule is not of universal application in the rules relating to accent.

When the word is not a Name, we have अभिर्माणवकः ॥ When it is not an upamāna we have देवदत्तैः (VI. 2. 148).

निष्ठा च द्रव्यजनात् ॥ २०५ ॥ पदानि ॥ निष्ठा, च, द्रव्यच, अनात् ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ निष्ठान्तं च द्रव्य संज्ञायां विषये आयुवाचो भवति चेदादिराकारी न भवति ॥

205. A disyllabic Participle in त (Nishthā), when a Name has the acute on the first syllable, but not if the first syllable has an आ ॥

Thus ईषः, ईषः, ईषः ॥ This debars the affix accent (III. 1. 3). In non-participles we have देवैः, भीनैः ॥ In polysyllabic Participles we have चिन्तितैः, रक्षितैः ॥ In Participles having long आ in the first syllable, we have, भानैः, भानैः ॥ When the Participle is not a Name we have, कृतैः, हृतैः ॥

शुष्कधृष्टौ ॥ २०६ ॥ पदानि ॥ शुष्क, धृष्टौ ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ आदिरुवाच इति वच्यते । शुष्क धृष्ट इत्येतावायुवाचो भवतः ॥

206. Also शुष्क and धृष्ट have acute on the first syllable.

These are non-Names. Thus शुष्कः and धृष्टः ॥

आशितः कर्ता ॥ २०७ ॥ पदानि ॥ आशितः, कर्ता ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ आशितशब्दः कर्तृवाचो आयुवाचो भवति ॥

207. The word आशित meaning 'having eaten' has acute on the first syllable.

BK. VI. CH. I § 212 ]

FIRST-ACUTE.

1131

Thus आश्चितो देववत्तः 'Devadatta, having eaten'. Here it is used as an active participle. The क्त is added to अश् preceded by आ, to form both Active and Passive Participles: which by VI. 2. 144 would have taken acute on the final. This debars that. In the Passive Participle we have आश्चितम् देववत्तेन 'eaten by Devadatta'. आश्चितम् 'the eaten food'. The former is भावे क्त, the second is कर्मणि क्त ॥

रिक्ते विभाषा ॥ २०८ ॥ पदानि ॥ रिक्ते, विभाषा ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ रिक्तशब्दे विभाषा आदिश्वान्तो भवति ॥

208. The word रिक्त may have optionally the acute on the first syllable.

Thus रिक्तः or रिक्तः ॥ This debars VI. 1. 204 and 205.

जुष्टापिते च छन्दसि ॥ २०९ ॥ पदानि ॥ जुष्टा, अपिते, च, छन्दसि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ जुष्ट अपिते इत्येते शब्दरूपे छन्दसि विषये विभाषा आश्वान्तो भवतः ॥

209. In the Chhandas, the words जुष्ट and अपित have optionally the acute on the first syllable.

Thus जुष्टः or जुष्टः; अपितः or अपितः ॥ In the secular literature the accent is always on the last syllable (III. 1. 3).

नित्यं मन्त्रे ॥ २१० ॥ पदानि ॥ नित्यम, मन्त्रे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ जुष्ट अपिते इत्येते शब्दरूपे मन्त्रविषये नित्यमाश्वान्तो भवतः ॥

210. In the Mantras, these words जुष्ट and अपित have always the acute on the first syllable.

Thus जुष्ट देवानामर्पितं पितृणाम् ॥ Some say that this rule applies only to जुष्ट and not to अपित; in which option is allowed even in the Mantra: so that it has acute on the last in the Mantra even: e. g. तस्मिन्साकं विशता न शंकयोर्पितौ ॥

युष्मदस्मदोडसि ॥ २११ ॥ पदानि ॥ युष्मद-अस्मदोः-, डसि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ युष्मदस्मदी मदिकप्रत्ययान्ते उन्तादान्ते तयोर्डसि परत आदिश्वान्तो भवति ॥

211. The acute accent is on the first syllable of युष्मद and अस्मद in the Genitive Singular.

This applies when the forms are मम and तव, and not मे and ते ॥ Thus मेम स्वम्, तैव स्वम् ॥ The word युष्मद and अस्मद are derived from युष and अस by adding the affix मदिक (Un I. 139) युष्मद+अस=युष्मद+अश् (VII. 1. 27)=तव अइ+अश् (VI. 2. 96)=तव+अश् (VII. 2. 90)=तव (VI. 1. 97). Here by VIII. 2. 5, व would have been udatta, the present sutra makes त udatta. So also with मम ॥

डयि च ॥ २१२ ॥ पदानि ॥ डयि, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ युष्मदस्मदोरिति वर्तते, आदिश्वान्त इति च । इत्येतस्मिन्न परतो युष्मदस्मदोरादिश्वान्तो भवति ॥

212. The acute accent is on the first syllable of युष्मद and अस्मद in the Dative Singular.

1132

FIRST-ACUTE.

[ Bk. VI. Ch. I § 215

Thus तृतीयम् and मैत्रम्, the forms त and मे are not governed by this rule. The making of two separate sūtras is for the sake of preventing the application of यथासंख्य rule (I. 3. 10). Had the sūtra been युग्मसम्पदं डिङ्गसाः, then yushmad in the Dative, and asmad in the Genitive alone would have taken this accent.

यतोऽनावः ॥ २१३ ॥ पदानि ॥ यतः, अनावः ॥

वृत्तिः । निष्ठा च ह्यजनादित्यतो ह्यजग्रहणमनुवर्तते । यत्रत्ययान्तस्य ह्यच आदिरुदातो भवति न चैत्री-शब्दापरो भवति ।

213. Whatever is formed by the affix यत्, has, if it is a disyllabic word, the acute on the first syllable, with the exception of नाव्यः from नौ ॥

The word ह्यच is understood here from VI. 1. 205. Thus चैत्यम्, जेयम् (III. 1. 97); कैप्यम्, औप्यम् (V. 1. 6). This rule debars the Svarita accent required by तित् (VI. 1. 185) ॥ But नौ—नाव्यम् ॥ The rule does not apply to words of more than two syllables, thus:—चिकीर्त्यम्, लताव्यम् ॥

ईडवन्दवृशंसदुहां ण्यतः ॥ २१४ ॥ पदानि ॥ ईड, वन्द, वृ, शंस्, दुहाम्, ण्यतः ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ ईड वन्द वृ शंस् दुह इत्येतेषां यो ण्यत् तदन्तस्यादिरुदातो भवति ।

214. The acute accent is on the first syllable of ईड, वन्द, वृ, शंस् and दुह, when they are followed by the affix ण्यत् ॥

Thus ईडवम्, वैत्यम्, वैर्यम्, वैस्यम्, वैह्या घेतुः ॥ The two letters ण and त् being indicatory, the 'nyat' is not included in 'yat' of the last sūtra. The accent would be regulated by त् ॥ The accent of त् however is debarred by this rule. The वृ in the sūtra is वृङ् संभक्तौ of Kriyadi class: the वृम् of स्वादि class takes kyap affix. See III. 1. 109.

विभाषा वेणिवन्धानयोः ॥ २१५ ॥ पदानि ॥ विभाषा, वेणु, इन्धानयोः ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ वेणु इन्धानि इत्येतयोविभाषा आदिरुदातो भवति ।

215. The acute accent is optionally on the first syllable of वेणु and इन्धान ॥

Thus वेणु or वेणु; इन्धान or इन्धीन or इन्धानः ॥ The word वेणु is derived by the Uṇādi affix णु (III. 38), which being a तित् would always have acute on the first. This allows an option. The word इन्धान, if it is formed by णानम् it will have the accent on the final. If it is considered to be formed by णानम्, the affix being a sārvadhātuka is anudātta, and as it replaces udātta final of the root, it becomes udātta (VI. 1. 161), and thus इन्धान gets acute on the middle. It would never have acute on the first syllable, the present rule ordains that also. When वेणु is used as an upamāna वेणुरिव वेणु, then it is invariably acutely accented on the first (VI. 1. 204).

BK VI. CH. I. §. 219 ]

ACUTE.

1133

त्यागरागहासकुहभठकथानाम् ॥ २१६ ॥ पदानि ॥ त्याग, राग, हास, कुह, भठ, कथानाम् ॥

वृत्तिः । त्याग राग हास कुह भठ कथ इत्येतेषां विभाषा आदिश्वान्तो भवति ।

216. The acute accent is optionally on the first syllables of त्याग, राग, हास, कुह, भठ, and कथ ॥

Thus त्यागः or त्यागः, रागः, रागः, हासः, हासः ॥ These are formed by पम् affix and by VI. I. 159 would take acute on the final, this ordains acute on the first syllable also. कुहः or कुहः, भठः or भठः, कथः or कथः formed by अच् (III. I. 13).

उपोत्तमं रिति ॥ २१७ ॥ पदानि ॥ उपोत्तमम्, रिति ॥

वृत्तिः । रिवन्तस्योपोत्तममुदात्तं भवति । त्रिप्रवृत्तीनामस्यमुत्तमं तस्य समीपे यत्तदुपोत्तमम् ।

217. What is formed by an affix having an indicatory र, has acute on the penultimate syllable, the full word consisting of more than two syllables.

A penultimate syllable can be only in a word consisting of three syllables or more. Thus करणीयम् and हरणीयम् formed by अनीयम् (III. I. 96); पदुजातीयः, पदुजातीयः by जातीयम् (V. 3. 19). This debars III. I. 3.

चङ्घन्यतरस्याम् ॥ २१८ ॥ पदानि ॥ चङ्घ, अन्यतरस्याम् ॥

वृत्तिः । चङ्घनं ऽन्यतरस्यामुपोत्तममुदात्तं भवति ।

218. The acute accent may be optionally on the penultimate syllable of the reduplicated Aorist in चङ्घ, the word consisting of more than two syllables.

Thus मा हि चोकरताम् or चोकरताम् ॥ The augment अङ्घ is elided by the addition of मा, VI. 4. 74; हि prevents the verb from becoming anudatta VIII. I. 34 then comes the चित् accent of चङ्घ ॥ The augmented form with अङ्घ has acute always on the first syllable VI. 4. 71. When the word is of less than three syllables, the rule does not apply, as, माहि वर्धन् ॥

मतोः पूर्वमासंज्ञायां स्त्रियाम् ॥ २१९ ॥ पदानि ॥ मतोः, पूर्वम्, आत्, संज्ञायाम्, स्त्रियाम् ॥

वृत्तिः । मतोः पूर्व आकार उदात्तो भवति तथैन्मथन्तं खीष्टिं संज्ञा भवति ।

219. The आ before the affix मत् has the acute accent, when the word is a name in the Feminine Gender.

Thus अदृश्यवती, पुष्करवती, शरवती (IV. 2. 85). The lengthening takes place by VI. 3. 120. शीरवती ॥ Why do we say 'the आ'? Observe इष्वती, कुमवती ॥ The words इष्व Un. III. 157 and कुम (V. 2. 108) are end-acute, so accent is on मतुप by VI. I. 176. Why do we say when a name? Observe सैद्ववती ॥ सैद्ववती is formed by कुम and has acute on the first (Un. I. 151). Why do we say in

[ Bk. VI. Ch. I. § 223

the Feminine Gender? Observe शाबाबू ॥ Why do we say when followed by मम्? Observe शाबाबू ॥

अन्तो उवत्याः ॥ २२ ॥ पदानि ॥ अन्तः, अवत्याः ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ संज्ञायामित्येव । अवतीशब्दान्तस्य संज्ञायामन्त उदात्तो भवति ।

220. The Names ending in अवती have the acute accent on the last syllable.

Thus अजिरवती, खारिवती, ईसवती, कारण्डवती ॥ These words being formed by क्रीष would have been unaccented on the final (III. 1. 4). Why do we use अवती and not वती? Then the rule would apply to राजवती also, for this word is really राजवती ending in अन्वती, the subsequent elision of नु is held to be non-valid for the purposes of the application of this rule (VIII. 2. 2). But the change of म into व (मन्=वत्) is considered asiddha for the purposes of this rule.

ईवत्याः ॥ २२१ ॥ पदानि ॥ ईवत्याः, ( उदात्तः ) ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ ईवतीशब्दान्तस्यान्त उदात्तो भवति खियां संज्ञायां विपये ।

221. The Names ending in ईवती have the acute on the last syllable.

Thus अहीवती, क्रीवीती, मृनीवती ॥
चौ ॥ २२२ ॥ पदानि ॥ चौ ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ चावित्यञ्चलितेनकारो गुह्यते । तस्मिन्पत्तः पूर्वस्यान्त उदात्तो भवति ।
वार्तिकम् ॥ चावतद्वितरति वक्तव्यम् ॥

222. In compound words ending in अञ्च, the final vowel of the preceding word has the acute accent in the weak cases in which only च् of अञ्च remains.

Thus ईधीचः पञ्च; ईधीचा, इधीचेः मधूँचः पञ्च, मधूँचा, मधूँचे ॥ This is an exception to VI. 1. 161, 170 and VI. 2. 52.

Vārt:—This rule does not apply before a Taddhita affix. As शाधीचैः, माधूँचैः ॥ Here the accent is regulated by the affix (III. 1. 3).

समासस्य ॥ २२३ ॥ पदानि ॥ समासस्य, ( उदात्तः ) ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ समासस्यान्त उदात्तो भवति ।

223. A compound word has the acute on the last syllable.

Thus राजपुरुषैः ब्राह्मणकन्दनैः, कन्यारत्नैः, पदशब्दैः, नतीयोपैः, राजदृष्टैः, ब्राह्मणसंगीतैः ॥ The consonants being held to be non-existent for the purposes of accent, the udatta will fall on the vowel though it may not be final, the final being a consonant. The exceptions to this rule will be mentioned in the next chapter.

ॐ ।

## षष्ठाध्यायस्य द्वितीयः पादः ।

### BOOK SIXTH.

#### CHAPTER SECOND.

बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम् ॥ १ ॥ पदानि ॥ बहुव्रीहौ, प्रकृत्या, पूर्वपदम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पूर्वपदमहानमच पूर्वपदस्थे स्वेरे उवाते स्वरिते वा वचते । बहुव्रीहौ समाते पूर्वपदस्थे यः स्वरः स प्रकृत्या भवति, स्वभावेनावतिष्ठते, न विकारमनुवात्स्वभावयते ॥

I. In a Bahuvrihi, the first member preserves its own original accent.

The word पूर्वपदम् means here the accent—whether udatta or svarita—which is in the first member: प्रकृत्या means, retains its own nature, does not become modified into an anudatta accent. By the rule VI. 1. 223, the final of a compound gets the accent, so that all the preceding members lose their accent and become anudatta, as in one word all syllables are unaccented except one. VI. 1. 158. Thus the first member of a Bahuvrihi would have lost its accent and become anudatta; with the present sūtra commences the exceptions to the rule that the final of a compound is always udatta. Thus काष्णोत्तरसङ्गः ॥ The word काष्ण is derived by the Taddhita affix अञ् (IV. 3. 154) from कृष्ण 'a kind of antelope;' and has the भिन्न accent (VI. 1. 197) i. e. on the first syllable: which the word preserves in the compound also. So also कूपवलजः; the word कूप is derived from यु by the Unādi affix प (Un III. 27), before which the vowel becomes lengthened (Un III. 25) and the affix is treated as नित् (Un III. 26), and hence the word is acutely accented on the first syllable (VI. 1. 197). So also ब्रह्मचारि परिरस्कन्धः; the word ब्रह्मचारिन् has a Krit-formed word as its second part, and gets the acute on the final (VI. 2. 139). So also स्नातकपुत्रः, the word स्नातक is derived by कन् (V. 4. 29) affix and has नित् accent (VI. 1. 197) i. e. udatta on the first syllable. So also अध्यापकपुत्रः, the word अध्यापक is accented on the middle as it is formed by a लिन् affix (III. 1. 133, VI. 1. 193). श्रोत्रियपुत्रः, the श्रोत्रिय being enounced with an indicatory न् in Sūtra V. 2. 84 is acutely accented on the first. मनुष्यनायः, the word मनुष्य being formed by अन् (IV. 1. 161) a लिन् affix is svarita (VI. 1. 185).

1136

ACCENT.

[ Bk. VI. Ch. II. § 2

The words udatta and svarita are understood in this aphorism. Therefore if all the syllables of the pūrvapada are anudatta, the present rule has no scope there, and such a compound will get udatta on the final by the universal rule enunciated in VI. I. 223. Thus समभानः, here सम being all anudatta, the accent falls on ग ॥

तत्पुरुषे तुल्यार्थतृतीयासममुपमानाव्ययद्वितीयाकृत्याः ॥ ५ ॥ पदानि ॥ तत्पुरुषे, तुल्यार्थ, तृतीया, सप्तमी, उपमान, अव्यय, द्वितीया, कृत्याः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तत्पुरुषे समासे तुल्यार्थ तृतीयान्ते समममुपमानाव्ययादि अव्यये द्वितीयान्ते कृत्यान्ते च यत्पूर्वपर्वं तथाकृतिस्सर्वं भवति ॥

वात्तिकम् ॥ अव्यये नमुकुनिपासानामिति वक्तव्यम् ॥

2. In a Tatpurusha, the first member preserves its original accent, when it is a word (1) meaning “a resemblance”, or (2) an Instrumental or (3) a Locative or (4) a word with which the second member is compared, (5) or an Indeclinable, or (6) an Accusative, or (7) a Future Passive Participle.

Thus (1) तुल्यभेतः, तुल्यलोहितः, तुल्यमहान्, सटैकच्छेतः, सटैगलोहितः, सटैगमहान् ॥ These are Karmadhāraya compounds formed under II. I. 68; and तुल्य being formed by यत is acutely accented on the first (VI. I. 216). The word सदृश is formed by कित (III. 2. 60 Vārt), and has acute on the final (VI. I. 197 and VI. 2. 139). So also सटैगभेतः सटैगलोहितः, सटैगमहान् ॥ The word सदृश is formed by कस् added to हृश, and by VI. I. 197 the accent falls on हृ (VI. 2. 139). (2) When the first member is in the Instrumental case, as:—शकुलया खण्डः=शकुली-खण्डः, so also किरिकाणः (II. I. 30) शकुला is derived from शकु+ला ॥ To the root ला is added the affix क with the force of घम्, and thus the noun ला is udatta; or the whole word शकुला is a word formed by क affix and hence VI. I. 165 applies and is final-acute. किरिः is formed by the Unādi affix हृ to कृ (Un IV. 143), and it being treated as a कित (Un. IV. 142) has udatta on the final.

(3) When the first member is a word in the Locative case, as:—अशेषु शीण्डः=अशेषीण्डः, so also पीनशीण्डः ॥ The word अश is formed by the affix स added to अश (Un III. 65), and is final acute (III. I. 3). The word पान is formed by खण्ड affix added to पा, and is acute on the first (VI. I. 193) owing to the कित accent. (4) When the first member is a word with which the second member is compared, as:—शक्तीश्यामा, कुष्ठश्येनी, हंसगद्वा, न्यमोघेपरिमण्डला, पूर्वा-कौण्डश्यामा, शरकाण्डगौरी ॥ These compounds are formed by II. I. 55. शक्ती is formed by कुष्ठ and is final-acute; कुष्ठ is formed by क affix (की मोदत=कुष्ठ) see III. 2. 5. Vārt; and is acutely accented on the first, or by Phit sūtra II. 3 it has acute on the first. हंस is formed by the Unādi affix स added to हृ

BK. VI. CH. II § 3 ]:

SAMASA-ACCENT.

1137

(Un III. 62), and is finally accented (III. 1. 3). न्यमोहति=न्यमोहः formed by अच् (III. 1. 134), and इ is irregularly changed into ध as Pānini himself uses this form (VII. 3. 5): and it is accented in the middle. The words यूनाकाण्ड, शाकाण्ड are Genitive Tatpurusha, and their second member has accent on the first syllable (VI. 2. 135). (5) When the first member is an Indeclinable, as, अँब्रह्मणः, अँवृषलः, कुँब्राह्मणः, कुँवृषलः ॥ निम्नोक्ताः, निर्वाणसिः, अँतिखटुः, अँतिमालः ॥ All these Indeclinable compounds have udatta on the first. they are formed by II. 2. 5 &c.

Vārī:—In cases of Indeclinable compounds, the rule applies only to those which are formed by the negative Particle अ, by कु, and by Particles (nipāta). Though नम् is one of the Nipātas, its separate mention indicates that नम्-accent debars even the subsequent क्तु-accent as अकरणः ॥ Therefore, it does not apply here स्नात्वाकालकः which has acute on the final and belongs to Mayuravyāsakādi class.

(6) When the first member as in the accusative case, as:—मुहूर्तमणीयम्, सर्वरार्यकल्याणी, सर्वरार्यशोभना ॥ They are formed by II. 1. 29. मुहूर्त belongs to पुपोदरादि class and is acutely accented on the last. सर्वरार्य is formed by the samāsanta affix अच् and is finally accented.

(7) When the first member is a Kritiya-formed word, as, भोज्यलवणम्, भोज्योणम्, पानीयशीतम्, हरणीयचूर्णम् (II. 1. 68). भोज्य is formed by ण्यत् and has svarita on the final: पानीय and हरणाय are formed by अनीच् and are accented on the penultimate (VI. 1. 185 and 217) i. e. on इ ॥

वर्णोर्वर्णेष्वनेते ॥ ३ ॥ पदानि ॥ वर्णः, वर्णेषु, अनेते ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदं, तत्पुरुषवृत्ति च वर्तते। वर्णं वर्णवाचि पूर्वपदं वर्णवाचिष्वेवोत्तरपदेषु एतदशब्दवर्णैः सेषु परतस्तत्पुरुषे समासे प्रकृतिस्वरं भवति ॥

3. The first member of a Tatpurusha preserves its original accent, when a word denoting color is compounded with another color denoting word, but not when it is the word एत ॥

Thus कृष्णसारङ्गी, लोहितसारङ्गी, कृष्णकल्पायः, लोहितकल्पायः ॥ कृष्ण is formed by नक affix (Un. III. 4) and has acute on the final (III. 1. 3). लोहित is formed by the affix तत् added to इह (Un. III. 94) and has accent on the first (VI. 1. 197).

Why do we say 'color-denoting word'? Observe परमकृष्णः (VI. 1. 223). Why do we say 'with another color denoting word'? Observe कृष्णतिलैः (VI. 1. 223). Why do we say 'but not when it is एत'? Observe कृष्णैः, लोहितैः ॥ The compounding takes place by II. 1. 69.

गाधलवणयोः प्रमाणे ॥ ४ ॥ पदानि ॥ गाध, लवणयोः, प्रमाणे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ प्रमाणवर्णचिनि तत्पुरुषे समासे गाध लवण इत्येतयोरुत्तरपदयोः पूर्वपदं प्रकृतिस्वरं भवति ॥

4. The first member of a Tatpurusha preserves its original accent, when the second term is गाध or लवण, and the compound expresses a 'measure or mass'.

Thus 'water as low or fordable as a Samba or an Aritra i. e. of the depth of an oar or a pestle'. 'so much salt as may be given to a cow or a horse'. These are Genitive Tatpurusha compounds. 'water is formed by adding 'to' (Un. IV. 94), and has acute on the first (VI. 1. 197). 'to' is formed by the affix 'added to' (III. 2. 184), and has acute on the middle (III. 1. 3): 'to' is formed by 'to' (Un. II. 68) and has acute on the final 'to'; 'to' is formed by 'to' affix added to 'to' (Un. I. 151), and has acute on the first (VI. 1. 197). The word प्रमाण here denotes 'quantity', 'measure', 'mass', 'limit', and not merely the length. The power of denoting measure by these words is here indicated by and is dependent upon accent.

When not denoting प्रमाण we have परमार्थम् and परमलवणम् ॥

दायादे दायादे ॥ ५ ॥ पदानि ॥ दायाद्यम्, दायादे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तत्प्रभे समासे दायादशब्दउत्तरपेरे दायाद्यावाप्ति पूर्वपेरे प्रकृतिस्वरे भवति ॥

5. In a Tatpurusha compound, having the word दायाद as its second member, the first member denoting inheritance preserves its original accent.

Thus विध्यैदायाः, धनदायाः ॥ The word विध्या is formed by the affix 'वय' (III. 3. 99) which is udatta (III. 3. 96). The word धन is derived by adding 'वय' to 'धाय' (Un. II. 81). Though the Unādi Sūtra II. 81 ordains 'वय' after the root 'धा' preceded by 'नि', yet by 'बहुत' (III. 3. 1) rule it comes after 'धा' also when it is not preceded by 'नि' and 'धन' has acute on the first (III. 1. 3).

In the forms विद्यादायाः &c, what Genitive case has been taken? If it is the Genitive case which the word दायाद requires by Rule II. 3. 39, then by the Vārtika प्रतिपदविधाना 'व' पद्यी न समस्यते (II. 2. 10 Vart), there can be no compounding. The Genitive case there is the ordinary Genitive case of II. 3. 50. i. e. a शेषिक Genitive case, and not a प्रतिपद Genitive. If it is a शेषलक्षण Genitive case, then why the other Genitive case is taught in II. 3. 39 with regard to दायाद &c. That sūtra only indicates the existence of the Locative case in the *alternative*, and does not prevent the Genitive. In fact, had merely Locative been ordained in that sūtra, this particular case would have prevented the Genitive on the maxim that a particular rule debars the general. But the employment of both terms Genitive and Locative in that sūtra indicates the *alternative* nature of the rule and shows that the Genitive case so taught is not a प्रतिपद Genitive, but a general Genitive. In short the Genitive taught in II.

BK. VI. CH. II § 8.]

3. 39, is not an apūrva-vidhi, the words naturally would have taken Genitive; the taking of the Locative is the only new thing taught there.

Why do we say 'when meaning inheritance'? Observe परमशब्दः (VI. 1. 223) taking the final acute of a compound.

प्रतिबन्धि चिरकृच्छ्रयोः ॥ ६ ॥ पदानि ॥ प्रतिबन्धि, चिर, कृच्छ्रयोः ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ तत्पुरुषे समासे चिरकृच्छ्रयोः ॥
प्रतिबन्धियाचि पूर्वपदं प्रकृतिस्वरं भवति ॥

6. In a Tatpurusha compound, having the words चिर or कृच्छ्र as its second member, the first member, when it denotes that which experiences an obstacle, preserves its original accent.

Thus गैमनचिरम्, गैमनकृच्छ्रम्, व्याहैरणचिरम् or व्याहैरणकृच्छ्रम् ॥ The words गमन and व्याहरण are formed by व्यूह affix, and have लिप्त accent (VI. 1. 193). This compound belongs either to the class of Mayūra-vyānsakādi (II. 1. 72), or of an attribute and the thing qualified. When going to a place is delayed owing to some defective arrangement or cause, or becomes difficult, there is produced an obstacle or hinderance, and is called गमनचिरं or गमनकृच्छ्रं ॥ Why do we say 'which experiences a hinderance'? Observe गमनकृच्छ्रम् ॥

पदे उपदेशे ॥ ७ ॥ पदानि ॥ पदे, अपदेशे ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ अपदेशे व्याजस्तद्वाचिनि तत्पुरुषे समासे पदशब्दउत्तरपदे पूर्वपदं प्रकृतिस्वरं भवति ॥

7. In a Tatpurusha compound the first member preserves its original accent, when the second member is the word पद denoting 'a pretext'.

The word अपदेश means 'a pretext', 'a contrivance'. Thus मूत्रपदेन प्रस्थितः, उधारपदेन प्रस्थितः ॥ Gone on pretext of voiding urine or excreta.

The word मूत्र is derived by adding the affix हृत् to the root मूत्र, the ऋ being substituted for उष् of मूत्र, (Un. IV. 163), and has acute on the first (VI. 1. 197) or it may be a word formed by घञ् to the root मूत्रयति ॥ The word उधार is also formed by घञ् and by VI. 2. 144 has acute on the final. The compounding takes place by II. 1. 72 or it is an attributive compound.

Why do we say 'when meaning a pretext?' Observe विण्णोः पदम्=वि-ण्णुपदम् ॥

निवाते वातत्राणे ॥ ८ ॥ पदानि ॥ निवाते, वात-त्राणे ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ निवातशब्दउत्तरपदे वातत्राणवाचिनि तत्पुरुषे समासे पूर्वं पदं प्रकृतिस्वरं भवति ॥

8. In a Tatpurusha compound, the first member preserves its original accent, when the second member is the word निवात in the sense of 'a protection from wind'.

Thus कुञ्चेयं निवात=कुण्डेनिवातम् 'a hut as the only shelter from the wind'. So also शमीनिवातम्, कुञ्चेनिवातम् or कुञ्चेनिवातम् ॥ The word निवात is an Avyayi-

[Bk. VI. Ch. II. §. 10]

bhāva compound = वात्स्य अभावः (II. 1. 6): or a. Bahuvrīhi = निरुद्धो वातोऽस्मिन् ॥
The words कुटीनिवातम् &c, are examples of compounds of two words in apposition. कुटी and शमी are formed by क्रीष (IV. 1. 41) and have acute on the last (III. 1. 3). Some say that कुञ्च is derived from कु by adding यत् with the augment उक् and treating it as कित्, is has the acute on the first; others hold that it is derived by the affix उक् to कु and the affix has the accent.

Why do we say when meaning 'a shelter from wind'? Observe राजनिवातं वसति, सुखं मातृनिवातं = 'he lives under the shelter of the king'; 'pleasant is the shelter or the protection of the mother'. Here निवात = पार्थः or vicinity.

शारदे उनातवे ॥ ९ ॥ पदानि ॥ शारदे, अनातवे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ क्तौ भवमातवम् । अनातववाचिनि शारदशब्दवत्तपदे तत्पुरुषे समासे पूर्वपदं प्रकृतिस्वरं भवति ॥

9. In a Tatpurusha compound the first member preserves its original accent, when the second member is the word शारद, having any other sense than that of 'autumnal'.

The word आतव means appertaining to season (कतु) i. e. when the word शारद does not refer to the season of शरत् or autumn. Thus रञ्जुशारदशब्दकम् 'fresh drawn water'. So also हर्षत् शारदाः सक्त्वः 'the saktu flour fresh from the mill'. The word शारद means here 'fresh' 'new': and it forms an invariable compound. The word रञ्जु is formed by उ affix added to सुज् (Up. I. 15), the स being elided. The affix उ is treated as नित् (Up. I. 9) and the accent falls on the first syllable (VI. 1. 197). The word हर्षत् is formed by the augment ष and shortening of the vowel of the root द 'to tear' (दृणाति), and the affix अदिक् (Up. I. 131) and has accent on the final (III. 1. 3).

Why do we say 'when not meaning autumnal'? Observe परमशारदम्, उत्तमशारदम् 'the best autumnal grass &c'. (VI. 1. 223).

अध्वर्युकपाययोजातौ ॥ १० ॥ पदानि ॥ अध्वर्यु, कपाययोः, जातौ ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अध्वर्युकपाय हर्षतयोजातवाचिनि तत्पुरुषे समासे पूर्वपदं प्रकृतिस्वरं भवति ॥

10. In a Tatpurusha compound denoting a genus, the first member preserves its original accent, when the second member is the word अध्वर्यु or कपाय ॥

Thus प्राच्याध्वर्युः, कडाध्वर्युः, कालापाध्वर्युः ॥ These are Appositional compounds denoting 'genus or kind', with a fixed meaning. प्राच्य is formed by यत्, and has accent on the first (VI. 1. 213). कड is derived by अच् affix (III. 1. 34), and to it is added the Taddhita affix णिनि (IV. 3. 104), in the sense of कडेन प्रोक्तं (IV. 3. 101), and the affix is then elided by IV. 3. 107. The word कालाप comes from कलापिन् + अण् (IV. 3. 108) in the sense of कलापिना प्रोक्तं (IV. 3.

101), and it would have preserved its form without change before this affix (VI. 4. 164) but for a vārtika which declares that the इन् of कलापिन् will be elided (See VI. 1. 144 vart). The words सर्पिमण्ड and उमापुष्प are Genitive compounds and have accent on the final (VI. 1. 223). The word दीवारिक is formed by ठक् affix added to द्वार and has acute on the final (VI. 1. 165). Why do we say when meaning a 'genus'? Observe, परमाच्छ्रुतः, परमकषायाः (VI. 1. 223).

सहस्रप्रतिरूपयोः साहस्रये ॥ ११ ॥ पदानि ॥ सहस्र, प्रतिरूपयोः, साहस्रये ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सहस्र प्रतिरूप इत्येतयोरुत्तरपदयोः साहस्रयवाचिनि तत्पुरुषे समासे पूर्वपदे प्रकृतिस्वरं भवति ॥

11. In a Tatpurusha compound expressing resemblance with some one or something, the first member preserves its original accent, when the second member is

सहस्र or प्रतिरूप ॥

Thus पितृसदृशः, मातृसदृशः ॥ The words पितृ and मातृ are formed by Unādi affix तृच् (Un. II. 95) and are finally accented. By II. 1. 31, सहस्र forms Instrumental Tatpurusha. That case, however, is governed by VI. 2. 2, which provides for Instrumental compounds. The examples here given are of Genitive Tatpurusha: and it applies to cases where the case-ending is not elided. As शास्त्रीः सहस्रो, वृषभ्यौ सहस्रः ॥ Here शास्त्री and वृषभ्यौ are finally acute, and the case-affix gets the accent when semivowel is substituted (VI. 1. 174), So also पितृप्रतिरूपः, मातृप्रतिरूपः ॥ Why do we say 'when meaning resemblance'? Observe परमसदृशैः, उत्तमसदृशैः (VI. 1. 223): here the sense of the compound is that of 'honor' and not 'resemblance'.

द्विगौ प्रमाणे ॥ १२ ॥ पदानि ॥ द्विगौ, प्रमाणे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ द्विगावुत्तरपदे प्रमाणवाचिनि तत्पुरुषे समासे पूर्वपदे प्रकृतिस्वरं भवति ॥

12. In a Tatpurusha compound denoting 'measure or quantity', the first member preserves its original accent, when the second member is a Dvigu.

Thus प्राच्यसमसः and गान्धारिससः ॥ The word सप्तसमः=सप्तसमाः प्रमाण-मस्य, the affix मात्रच् denoting 'measure' (V. 2. 37) is elided (See V. 2. 37 Vart) प्राच्यशास्त्री सप्तसमः=प्राच्यसमसः 'an Eastern seven-years old'. So also गान्धारिससः or 'षट्समः' ॥ प्राच्य has acute on the first; while गान्धारि is either accented on the first or on the middle; as it belongs to the Kardamādi class (Phit III. 10). Why do we say 'before a Dvigu'? Observe श्रीप्रत्ययः ॥ Why do we say 'when denoting measure'? Observe परमससः ॥

13. Before the word वाणिज 'a trader', the first member of a Tatpurusha preserves its accent, when it is a word specifying the place whither one has to go, or the ware in which one deals.

Thus मङ्गैबाणिजः, काङ्गैबाणिजः, गौन्धारिबाणिजः=मङ्गादिषु गत्वा व्यवहरन्ति 'the Madra-merchants i. e. who trade by going to Madra &c' All these are Locative compounds. मङ्ग is derived by रक् affix (Un II, 13) and is acutely accented on the last (VI. 1. 165). काङ्गै belongs to Kṛṣṇodarādi class (VI. 3. 109), and has acute either on the first or the second syllable. The word गौन्धारि belongs to the Kārdamādi class, and is consequently acute on the first or the second (Phit III. 10) In the sense of पण्य we have: गोबाणिजः 'a dealer in cows', अश्वबाणिजः &c. गौ is finally accented (Un II. 67): and अश्व has acute on the first (Un I. 151) the affix being कुण्ड ॥

Why do we say 'the place whither one goes, or the goods in which one deals?' Observe परमबाणिजः, उत्तमबाणिजः ॥

मात्रोपक्षेपक्रमच्छाये नपुंसके ॥ १४ ॥ पदानि ॥ मात्रा, उपक्षा, उपक्रम, छाये, नपुंसके ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ मात्रा उपक्षा उपक्रम छाया एतेऽप्युपक्षेप नपुंसकवाचिनि तत्प्रस्थे समासे पूर्वपदं प्रकृतिस्वरं भवति ॥

14. The first member of a Tatpurusha preserves its accent before the words मात्रा, उपक्षा, उपक्रम and छाया when these words appear as neuter.

Thus भिक्षामात्रं न इदाति याचितः, समुद्रमात्रं न सरोऽस्ति किंचन ॥ The word मात्रा is here synonymous with तुल्य, the phrase being=भिक्षायास्तुल्यमाणं, and is a Genitive compound. The word भिक्षा is derived from भिक्षा, by the feminine affix अ (III. 3. 103), and has acute on the final (III. 1. 3). The word समुद्र has also acute on the final as it is a word denoting 'a sea', (Phit sūtra I. 2). So also with उपक्षा, as पाणिनोपक्रमकालकं व्याकरणम्; व्यौडुपपतं दुष्करणम्, औपिशलपपतं गुरुलापपतं (see II. 4. 21). All these are Genitive compounds. The word पाणिन is derived by अणु affix from पणिन् (पणिनोपक्रम=पाणिनै), and has acute on the final, (III. 1. 3). The word व्याकि being formed by इषु affix has acute on the first (VI. 1. 197), so also आपिशलि ॥ So also with उपक्रम, as आङ्योपक्रमं प्रासादः, दशैर्नैयोपक्रमम्, सुकुमारि पक्रमम्, नन्दो पक्रमाणि मानानि ॥ All these are Genitive compounds. The word आङ्यै (तच्चैर्नै च्यायन्ति) is derived from आ+चै+क affix added with the force of घस, the घ being changed to इ the word belonging to पृथोदरादि class (VI. 3. 109), and it has acute on the final by VI. 2. 144. The word दशैर्नैय is formed by अनीयर and has acute on the penultimate नी owing to the indicatory र् (VI. 1. 217). The word सुकुमार has acute on the final by VI. 2. 172.
