SANNITA-CHANGES

[ Bk. VI. Ch. III § 119

Observe शोभनकर्णः ॥ Why do we say 'with the exception of बिड &c'? Observe बिडकर्णः ॥ अटकर्णः, पञ्चकर्णः, भिन्नकर्णः, छिन्नकर्णः, छिन्नकर्णः, सबकर्णः, स्वस्तिककर्णः and मणिकर्णः ॥

नहिवृत्तिवृषिव्यधिरुचिसहितनिषु कौ ॥११६॥ पदानि ॥ नहि, वृत्ति, वृपि, व्यधि, रुचि, सहि, तनिषु, कौ, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ नहि वृत्ति वृपि व्यधि रुचि सहि तनि इलेतेषु विव्यत्ययान्तवृत्तरपवेषु पूर्वपवस्य दीर्घो भवति संहितायां विधेय ॥

116. A long vowel is substituted for the final vowel of the preceding word, before the verbs नह, वृत, वृष, व्यध्, रुच, सह and तन, when these roots take the affix कि ॥

Thus उपानह (उपानह Nom. S.), so also, परीणह, नीवृत, उपावृत, (with vrt) प्रादृत, उपावृत, (with vrsh) मर्मावित, हृदयावित, श्रावित, (with vyadh) नीरुक, अभीरुक, (with ruch) कर्तारक, (with sah) तरीतद (with tan). The nasal is elided after गम् before कि (VI. 4. 40), by an extension of that rule, it is elided after तन also. Why do we say when कि follows? Observe परिणहनम् ॥

वनगिर्योः संज्ञायां कोटरकिशुलकादीनाम् ॥ ११७ ॥ पदानि ॥ वन, गिर्योः, संज्ञायाम्, कोटर, किशुलकादीनाम्, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ वन गिरि इलेतयोरुत्तरपवयोर्यसख्यं कोटरादीनां किशुलकादीनां च दीर्घो भवात संज्ञायां विधेय ॥

117. For the final vowel of कोटर &c. a long vowel is substituted before वन, and so also of किशुलक &c. before गिरि, when the compound is a Name.

Thus कोटरावणम्, मिश्रकावणम्, सिघ्रकावणम्, सारिकावणम् ॥

So also किशुलकागिरिः, अञ्जनागिरिः, &c.

The न is changed to ण in वन by VIII. 4. 4. But असिपत्रवनम् and कृष्णगिरि as these words do not belong to the above classes.

1 कोटर, 2 मिश्रक, 3 सिघ्रक, 4 पुरग (पुरक), 5 सारिक (सारिक) ॥

1 किशुलक (किशुलक), 2 शाल्व (साल्वक), 3 नङ* 4 अञ्जन, 5 भञ्जन, 6 लोहित, 7 कुक्कुट ॥

वले ॥ ११८ ॥ पदानि ॥ वले, ( पूर्वस्य दीर्घः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ वले परतः पूर्वस्य दीर्घो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ अनुत्साहभ्रातृपितृणमिति ॥

118. The final of the preceding word is lengthened before the affix वल ॥

Thus आहुतीवलः, कृधीवलः, इन्तावलः ॥ These are formed by the affix वलम् (V. 2. 112).

VArt:—Not so, of उत्साह, आहु and पितृ : as उत्साहवलः, आहुवलः and पितृवलः ॥

मती बह्वचो ञजिरादीनाम् ॥ ११९ ॥ पदानि ॥ मती, बह्व चः, अनजिरादीनाम्, ( संज्ञायाम् ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ मती परतो बह्वचो ञजिरादिवर्जितस्य दीर्घो भवति संज्ञायां विधेय ॥

BK. VI. CH. III § 122 ]

SAMHITA-LENGTHENING.

124 5

119. The final vowel of a word consisting of more than two syllables is lengthened before the affix मत, when it is a name, but not of the words अजिर &c.

Thus उद्भववती, मशकावती, वीरणावती, पुष्करावती, अमरावती ॥ These are formed by the affix मतुप (IV. 2. 85) The मत is changed to वत, by VIII. 2. 11. Why do we say 'of a word consisting of more than two syllables? Observe श्रीहिमती ॥ Why 'with the exception of अजिर &c'. Observe अजिरवती, खदिरवती, पुलिनवती, हंसकारण्डवती, चक्रवाकवती ॥ When the word is not a name, there is no lengthening, as वलयवती ॥

1 अजिर, 2 खदिर, 3 पुलिन, 4 हंस, 5 कारण्डव (हंसकारण्डव) 6 चक्रवाक.

शरादीनां च ॥ १२० ॥ पदानि ॥ शरादीनाम्, च, (दीर्घः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ शरादीनां च मतो दीर्घो भवति संज्ञायां विधये ॥

120. The final vowel of शर &c. is lengthened before मत when it is a Name.

As शरावती, वंशावती ॥ The म of मत is changed to व because it is a Name (VIII. 2. 11). But not so after श्रीहि &c as these belong to यबादि class (VIII. 2. 9).

1 शर, 2 वंश, 3 घूम, 4 अहि, 5 कपि 6 मनि, 7 मुनि, 8 शुचि, 9 हतु.

इको वहे उपीलोः ॥ १२१ ॥ पदानि ॥ इकः, वहे, अपीलोः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इगन्तस्य पूर्वपवस्य पीलुवर्जितस्य वहउत्तरपदे दीर्घो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ अपील्वादीनामिति वक्तव्यम् ॥

121. The final इ and the उ of a word, with the exception of पीलु, are lengthened before वह ॥

Thus कपीवहम्, कपीवहम्, मुनीवहम् ॥ Why do we say 'ending in इक vowels'? Observe पिण्डवहम् ॥ Why not of पीलु? Observe पीलुवहम् ॥

Vart:—It should be stated 'with the exception of पीलु and the rest.' As शरवहम् ॥

उपसर्गस्य घञघमनुष्ये बहुलम् ॥ १२२ ॥ पदानि ॥ उपसर्गस्य, घञि, अमनुष्ये, बहुलम्, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ उपसर्गस्य घञन्तउत्तरपदे अमनुष्येभिषे बहुले दीर्घो भवति ॥

122. The final vowel of a Preposition is diversely lengthened, before a word formed by the krit-affix घञ, but not when the compound denotes a human being.

Thus नीक्रेदः, बीमार्गः, अपामार्गः ॥ It does not take place, as प्रतेचः, प्रसारः ॥ It is lengthened before साद and कार, when building is meant, as प्रसादः and प्राकारः, otherwise प्रसादः and प्रकारः ॥ Optionally in वेश &c. as प्रतिवेशः or प्रतीवेशः, प्रतिरोधः or प्रतीरोधः ॥ When human beings are meant, there is no lengthening, as निपादो मनुष्यः ॥

27

1246

SAMHITA-LENGTHENING.

[ Bk. VI. Ch. III. § 127

इकः काशे ॥ १२३ ॥ पदानि ॥ इकः, काशे, ( दीर्घः ) ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ इगन्तस्योपसर्गस्य काशशब्दउत्तरपेरे दीर्घो भवति ॥

123. A Preposition ending in इ, or उ lengthens its final before काश ॥

As मीकाशः, बीकाशः, अनुकाशः ॥ काश is formed by अच् (III. 1. 134). Why do we say 'ending in इ or उ'? Observe प्रकाशः where the Preposition does not end in इक् ॥

वृत्ति ॥ १२४ ॥ पदानि ॥ इः, ति, ( दीर्घः इकः उपसर्गस्य ) ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ वा इत्येतस्य यस्तकारादिरवेशस्तस्मिन्नत इगन्तस्योपसर्गस्य दीर्घो भवति ॥

124. A Preposition ending in इ or उ lengthens its final vowel, before the verb दा, when the latter is changed to त ॥

Thus नीचम्, नीचम्, परीचम् ॥ See VII. 4. 47 for the change of दा to त ॥ But प्रचम्, अवचम्, where the prepositions do not end in इ or उ ॥ Why do we say 'दा is changed to त'? Observe विनोर्णम्, विनोर्णम् ॥ Why do we say ति 'a substitute of दा, beginning with a त'? Observe सुवचम्, here दद् is the substitute of दा (VII. 4. 46).

अष्टनः संज्ञायाम् ॥ १२५ ॥ पदानि ॥ अष्टनः, संज्ञायाम्, ( दीर्घः ) ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ अष्टनित्येतस्योत्तरपेरे संज्ञायां दीर्घो भवति ॥

125. A long vowel is substituted for the final of अष्टन् before the second member, when the compound is a name.

Thus अष्टावक्रः, अष्टावन्धुरः अष्टापदम् ॥ But अष्टपुष्पः, अष्टमार्यः where the compounds are not names.

छन्दसि च ॥ १२६ ॥ पदानि ॥ छन्दसि, च, ( दीर्घः ) ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ छन्दसि विधेये ऽष्टन उत्तरपेरे दीर्घो भवति ॥
वार्णिकम् ॥ गवि च युक्ते भाषायामष्टनो दीर्घो भवतीति वक्तव्यम् ॥

126. In the Veda also, the long vowel is substituted for the final of अष्टन् before a second member.

Thus आग्नेयमहाकपानं निर्वपेत्, अष्टादिरण्या दक्षिणा, अष्टापदी देवता सुमती ॥ The form अष्टापदी is the feminine in क्रीप (IV. 1. 8) of अष्टपाद (V. 4. 138 the अ of पाद being elided in a Bahuvrihi), पद being substituted for पाद by VI. 4. 130.

Vart:—The final of अष्टन् is lengthened before गो even in the vernacular, when yoking is meant. Thus अष्टागवं शकटम् ॥

चितेः कपि ॥ १२७ ॥ पदानि ॥ चितेः, कपि, ( दीर्घः ) ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ चितिशब्दस्य कपि परतो दीर्घो भवति ॥

127. The final vowel of चिति is lengthened before the affix कप् ॥

BK VI. CH. III § 133 ] SAMHITA-LENGTHEMING.

1247

Thus एकचित्तीकः, द्विचित्तीकः, त्रिचित्तीकः ॥

विश्वस्य वसुराटोः ॥ १२८ ॥ पदानि ॥ विश्वस्य, वसु, राटोः, ( दीर्घः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ विश्वशब्दस्य वसु राडिलेतयोरुत्तरपदयोर्दीर्घ आविशो भवति ॥

128. The final vowel of विश्व is lengthened before वसु and राट् (the form assumed by राज्).

Thus विश्वावसुः, विश्वराट् ॥ The rule applies to the राट् form of राज् in the Nominative singular, and not when it retains its own form: as विश्वराजो, विश्वराजः ॥

नरे संज्ञायाम् ॥ १२९ ॥ पदानि ॥ नरे, संज्ञायाम्, ( दीर्घः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ नरशब्दउत्तरपदे संज्ञायां विषये विश्वस्य दीर्घो भवति ॥

129. The final of विश्व is lengthened before नर, when the compound is a Name.

Thus विश्वानरः, वैश्वानरिः (the son of Vishvānara). But विश्वानरः = विश्वे नरा यस्य when it is not a name.

मित्रे चर्षौ ॥ १३० ॥ पदानि ॥ मित्रे, च, ऋषौ, ( दीर्घः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ मित्रे चोत्तरपदे ऋषावभिषये विश्वस्य दीर्घो भवति ॥

130. The final of विश्व is lengthened before मित्र when it is the name of a Rishi.

As विश्वामित्रः 'the sage Viśvāmitra'. But विश्वामित्रः 'a boy called Viśvāmitra'.

मन्त्रे सोमाश्वेन्द्रियविश्वदेव्यस्य मतौ ॥ १३१ ॥ पदानि ॥ मन्त्रे, सोम, अश्व, इन्द्रिय, विश्वदेव्यस्य, मतौ, ( दीर्घः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ मन्त्रविषये सोम अश्व इन्द्रिय विश्वदेव्य इत्येतेषां मनुष्यत्वे परतो दीर्घो भवति ॥

131. In a Mantra, the final vowels of सोम, अश्व, इन्द्रिय and विश्वदेव्य are lengthened when the affix मनुष्य follows.

Thus सोमावती, अश्वावती, इन्द्रियावती, विश्वदेव्यावती ॥

ओषधेश्च विभक्तावप्रथमायाम् ॥ १३२ ॥ पदानि ॥ ओषधेः, च, विभक्तौ, अग्र-थमायाम्, ( मन्त्रे ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ओषधिशब्दस्य विभक्तावप्रथमायां परतो दीर्घो भवति ॥

132. In a Mantra, the final of ओषधि is lengthened before the case-endings, but not in the Nominative.

Thus ओषधीभिरपीपत्तत्, नमः पृथिव्यै नमः ओषधीभ्यः ॥ Why do we say 'before case-endings'? Observe ओषधिपते ॥ Why do we say 'but not in the Nominative'? Observe स्थिरयमस्थौषधिः ॥

ऋचि तुतुमधमधुतङ्कुत्रोरुध्याणाम् ॥ १३३ ॥ पदानि ॥ ऋचि, तु, तु, घ, मधु, तङ्, कुत्र, उरुध्याणाम्, ( दीर्घः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ऋचि विषये तु तु घ मधु तङ् कु त्र उरुध्य इत्येषां दीर्घो भवति ॥

1248

SAMHITA-LENGTHENING.

[BK. VI, CH. III. § 137]

133. In the Rig-Veda the finals of the particles
तू, तु, घ, मधु, the tense-affix तङ्, कु, the ending ञ and the word
उरुच्य are lengthened.

Thus तु:—आ तु न इन्न् वृत्रहम् (Rig IV. 32. 1) तु—तु करणे ॥ घ:—उत बाधा
स्थालात् ॥ मधु:—मधु गोमन्तमीये ॥ तङ्:—भरत जातवेवसम् (Rig X. 176. 2). तङ् is
the substitute of घा, when it is treated as क्ति, therefore it does not apply
here, गुणोत मायाणः (I. 2. 4). कु—कृमनस; ञ—अन्ना गोः; उरुच्या गोः ॥

इकः सुभि ॥ १३४ ॥ पदानि ॥ इकः, सुभि, (दीर्घः) ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ सुभ् निपातो गुह्यते । इगन्तस्य सुभि परतो मन्त्रविषये दीर्घो भवति ॥

134. In a Mantra, the finals of the preceding
member ending in इ or उ are lengthened before the particle
सु ॥

Thus अभी पु णः सखीनाम् (Rig. IV. 31. 3) उर्ध्वं ऊ पुण उतेय (Rig I. 36. 13).
The स is changed to ष by VIII. 3. 107; and न changed to ञ by VIII. 4. 27.

इधचोतस्तिञः ॥ १३५ ॥ पदानि ॥ धचः, अतः, तिङ्, (ऋचि दीर्घः) ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ इधचतिष्ठन्तस्यात् ऋग्विषये दीर्घो भवति ॥

135. A tense affix ending in अ is lengthened in
the Rig-veda, when the Verb consists of two syllables.

Thus विद्या हि वा सस्पति धूर गोनाम् &c. See Rig III. 42. 6, विद्या हि तस्य पितरम्
&c. But not here देवा भवत वाजिनः, as the verb consists of more than two syllables:
not also here आ देवान् वशि याति च, as the verbs do not end in अ ॥

निपातस्य च ॥ १३६ ॥ पदानि ॥ निपातस्य, च, (ऋचि) (दीर्घः) ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ निपातस्य च ऋग्विषये दीर्घ आवेशो भवति ॥

136. In the Rig Veda the final of a particle is leng-
thened.

Thus एवा ते, अच्छाते, अच्छा जरितारः (R. I. 2. 2).

अन्येषामपि हृदयते ॥ १३७ ॥ पदानि ॥ अन्येषाम्, अपि, हृदयते, (दीर्घः) ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ अन्येषामपि दीर्घो हृदयते स शिष्टप्रयोगाद्विगन्तव्यः ॥ यस्य दीर्घत्वं न विहितं हृदयते च प्रयोगे तद्-
नेन कर्तव्यम् ॥

वात्तिकम् ॥ सुनो इन्तर्वेद्याकर्णकुन्दवराहपुष्पतेषु ॥

137. The elongation of the final is to be found
in other words also.

Here we must follow the usage of the Śishthas. Where the lengthening
is not ordained by any of the rules of Grammar, but occurs in the writing of
standard authors, there we should accept such lengthening as valid. Thus
केशाकाशि, कथाकाशि, जलासाह, मारकः, पुरुषः ॥

B. K. VI. Ch. III. § 139]

SAMHITA-LENGTHENING.

1249

Vårt:—The final of अन् is lengthened before the following नन्, वद्गा, कर्ण कुन्द, वराह, पुच्छ, and पद:—as आवन्तः आवेद्गः, आकर्णः, आकुन्दः, आवराहः, आपुच्छः, आपदः ॥

चौ ॥ १३८ ॥ पदानि ॥ चौ, ( पूर्वस्यदीर्घः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ चौ परतः पूर्वपदस्य दीर्घो भवति ॥ यावित्यञ्चातिर्लेपनकाराकारो गृह्यते ॥

138. The final vowel of the preceding member is lengthened before अञ्च, when it assumes the form च, having lost its nasal and the vowel.

Thus दधीचः पञ्च, दधीचा, दधीचे, मधुचः पञ्च, मधुचा, मधुचे ॥ The nasal of अञ्च is elided by VI. 4. 24, and the अ by VI. 4. 138. In दधि+अञ्च the इ is not changed to its semivowel, though that is an antaranga rule, because the present sutra ordains specifically long ई, and so also दधी+अञ्च and मधु+अञ्च ॥ See also VI. 3. 92.

संप्रसारणस्य ॥ १३९ ॥ पदानि ॥ संप्रसारणस्य, ( उत्तरपदे दीर्घः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ संप्रसारणान्तस्य पूर्वपदस्योत्तरपदे दीर्घो भवति ॥

139. The vowel substituted for a semivowel is lengthened, when it stands as the first member of a compound.

As कारीषगन्धीपुत्रः, कारीषगन्धीपतिः, कौमुदगन्धीपतिः ॥ See VI. 1. 13. कारीषस्य गन्धोऽस्य=करीषगन्धिः (इ being added as samāsānta by V. 4. 136 and 137). The optional shortening ordained by VI. 3. 61. does not apply here, for that option is a definite and restricted option; moreover, on the maxim of परत्व, 'a subsequent rule superseding a precedent,' rule VI. 3. 61 is superseded by VI. 3. 139; and the rule VI. 3. 61 can not be revived by the maxim पुनः प्रसङ्ग विज्ञानं "occasionally the formation of a particular form is accounted for by the fact that a preceding rule is allowed to apply again, after it had previously been superseded, by a subsequent rule." For here the following maxim will prevent the revival सकृता, विभक्तिपेवदाधितं तदाधितमेव "when two rules, while they apply simultaneously, mutually prohibit each other, that rule of the two which is once superseded by the other, is superseded altogether, and cannot, therefore, apply again, after the latter rule has taken effect."

ॐ ॥

## षष्ठाध्यायस्य चतुर्थः पादः ।

### BOOK SIXTH.

#### CHAPTER FOURTH

अङ्गस्य ॥ १ ॥ पदानि ॥ अङ्गस्य, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अधिकारोभवाऽऽसमाध्यायपरिसमात्रैः । यदित उर्जमनुक्रमिष्यामोऽङ्गस्यैवं तद्वैतितव्यम् ॥

1. Whatever will be taught here after upto the end of the Seventh Adhyāya, is consequent upon the stem (aṅga).

This is an adhikāra sūtra. Thus in VI. 4. 2 is taught the lengthening of the vowel of a samprasāraṇa : as हृतः, जीतः, संवीतः ॥ That means that the vowel preceded by a consonant belonging to the stem is lengthened. Therefore in निर्+वेष्ट+क्त=निरुतम्, the vocalised vowel उ is not lengthened, as निर् is upasarga and not stem. So दुरुतम् ॥ Similarly VI. 4. 3, teaches the lengthening of the final before नाम, as अधीनाम्, बाहूनाम् ॥ But क्रिमिणाम् पद्य, पामनां पद्य, as नि and म are not the end-portions of a stem. The stem is क्रिमिणा and पामना 'a female having क्रिमि or पामन्', formed by न affix (V. 2. 100). The forms क्रिमिणाम् and पामनाम् are Accusative Singular. Similarly VII. 1. 9 teaches that after अ, भिस् is changed into ऐस् ॥ As वृक्षैः, प्रज्ञैः ॥ There also, the अ must be the अ final in an aṅga or stem : hence not here ब्राह्मणभिस्सा, ओदनभिस्सा, the भिस does not follow an aṅga. भिस्स means boiled rice and भिस्सा means वधिः ॥

The maxim of अर्धवदृशदणे नामर्थकस्य does not apply here ; for had it been so, there would have been no necessity of making this sūtra. For example, in the sūtra नानि (VI. 4. 3), the affix नाम, having a meaning would have been meant, and not any other नाम ॥

The word अङ्गस्य must be read in the following sūtras, otherwise there would arise incongruity : *first*; sūtras teaching the lengthening of the vowel when सन् or Samprasāraṇa follows, thus : VI. 4. 16 ordains the lengthening of vowel before सन्, as विदीर्षति ; but not here वधि सनोति for इ of वधि is not that of aṅga. So also in Samprasāraṇa, but not in निरुत &c as shown above.

BK. VI. CH. IV § 2 ]

LENGTHENING.

1251

2ndly—For the purposes of एत्वे in sūtra VI. 4. 68. The optional change of आ into ए must refer to anga, as ग्लेयात् or ग्लायात्, but not here निर्यायात् or निर्यायात्, for here र् is not part of the anga, and so र् cannot be considered a conjunct part of anga.

3rdly—For the change of तु to तात् in VII. 1. 35. There also तु must be portion of the anga, and not the particle तु, therefore, जीवतु or जीवतात्, but not here जीव तु त्वम् ॥

4thly—For the substitution of इयद् and उवद् in VI. 4. 77. Therefore not here इयर्यम् and वर्यम् ॥

5thly—For the sake of तद् augment in VII. 1. 54. But not here कुमारी आभाति आह ॥

6thly—For the sake of shortening of vowels. Thus VII. 4. 13 ordains the shortening of अण् vowels before क ॥ It refers to the anga-vowel, as कुमारिका ॥ But not here, कुमारी कर्ते स्पृहयति or कुमार्याः कं मुखं = कुमारीकं ॥

And lastly for तत्व or त substitution. Thus VII. 4. 48 ordains the change of ए into त् in the case of अप् before भ ॥ It refers to anga, as अङ्गि: ॥ But not here अङ्गभारः, for अप् here is not anga.

To sum up in Sanskrit : सन् सम्प्रसारण दीर्घलेखताताङ्क्यङ्कुरुद्ध हस्वत्व तत्त्वे च अङ्गस्थलाधिकार प्रयोजनं ॥

The word अङ्गस्थ is in the Genitive case. But the force of Genitive is here not only that taught in I. 1. 49 (स्थाने योगः), but of mere relationship. Or अङ्गस्थ may be considered as a mere pratipadika, without any case-affix. In the subsequent aphorisms, it should be read with proper case-affixes as the exigencies of each sūtra may require. Thus in अतो भिस् ऐस् (VII. 1. 9) अङ्ग should be read in the ablative case : अकारान्ताद् अङ्गाद् भिस् ऐस् ॥ The Genitive case has force of स्थानपक्षी in sūtras like हन्तेज, where the whole of हन् is replaced (VI. 4. 36). It has the force of अवयवपक्षी in sūtras like ऊदुपधाया गोहः (VI. 4. 89). It has the force of निमित्तनिमित्ते सम्बन्धः in युवेरनाकी (VII. 1. 1). Or the Genitive case in अङ्गस्थ may be changed into any other case, as already shown.

हलः ॥ २ ॥ पदानि ॥ हलः, ( अङ्गस्थ सम्प्रसारणम् दीर्घः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अङ्गवयवाञ्जलौ यदुत्तरं संप्रसारणं तदन्तस्याङ्गस्थ दीर्घो भवति ॥

2. The long vowel is substituted for a vocalised half-vowel अ, इ and उ at the end of a stem, when it is preceded by a consonant which is a portion of the stem.

Both the words दीर्घ and अण् from VI. 3. 111, and संप्रसारण from VI. 3. 139 are understood here. Thus हृतः from ह्वा, जीनः from ज्वा, सर्वीतः from व्या ॥ Why do we say 'preceded by a consonant'? Observe उत्तः and उत्तवान् from वेष् ॥ Why do we say that the preceding consonant should be a portion of the stem?

1252

LENGTHENING.

[ Bk. VI. Ch. IV. § 5.

Observe निरुत्स, here र् is not an integral part of the stem, but a portion of the upasarga निर् and therefore उ is not lengthened. Why do we say 'at the end of a stem'? Observe विंदः, विचितः from व्यप् and व्यप्; here the vowel इ is in the middle of the stem. Why do we say 'अ, इ and उ substitutes of semivowels'? Observe तृतीयः ॥ Here वि has been vocalised into तु, क् being substituted for र् before the affix तीय (V. 2. 55). The क् will not be lengthened. Or the absence of lengthening in तृतीय is an irregularity countenanced by Pāṇini himself in sūtras like II. 1. 30 &c. The word अङ्ग should be repeated in this sūtra, first to qualify the word हल, and then to qualify the letters अ, इ and उ ॥

नाभि ॥ ३ ॥ पदानि ॥ नाभि, ( अङ्गस्य दीर्घः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ नामिलेत्त्वप्रीवहुवचनम् आगततुट्कं गृह्यते ॥ तस्मिन्परतोऽङ्गस्य दीर्घो भवति ॥

Kārikā—नाभि दीर्घ आनि चेदस्याङ्कृते दीर्घं न तुष्ट भवेत् ।

वचनाद्यत्र तमास्ति, नोपधायाय चर्मणाम् ॥

3. The long vowel is substituted for the final of the stem before the Genitive Plural affix नाम (having the augment तुष्ट).

Thus अग्नीनाम्, वायूनाम्, कत्तुणाम्, हर्तृणाम् ॥ The anuvritti of अण् (VI. 3. 111) ceases. The augment तुष्ट (VII. 1. 54) in नाम is for the sake of the subsequent sūtra; like VI. 4. 7. and the lengthening takes place after the addition of तुष्ट to the genitive affix आम् ॥ For if the lengthening took place before the addition of तुष्ट, there would be no occasion for तुष्ट which comes only after short stems.

न तिसुचतस् ॥ ४ ॥ पदानि ॥ न, तिसु, चतस्, ( नाभि दीर्घः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तिसु चतस् इत्येतयोर्नाभि दीर्घो न भवति ॥

4. The finals of तिसु and चतस् are not lengthened before नाम ॥

As तिसुणाम्, चतसुणाम् ॥ The very fact of this prohibition proves by implication that the final क् of these words is not changed to र् before a genitive plural, VII. 2. 100 notwithstanding. In fact तुष्ट is added before scope is given to that rule, and thus the preceding rule VII. 1. 54 prevents the application of the subsequent rule VII. 2. 100.

छन्दस्युभयथा ॥ ५ ॥ पदानि ॥ छन्दसि, उभय था ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ छन्दसि विषये तिसुचतसोनाभि परत उभयथा दृढ्यते, दीर्घधारीर्घम् ॥

5. In the Veda, the finals of तिसु and चतस् are found in both ways, before the Genitive plural नाम ॥

In some places they are seen as lengthened, in others not. As तिसुण मध्येऽपि or तिसुणाम् मध्येऽपि ॥ So also चतसुणाम् and चतसुणाम् ॥

तु च ॥ ६ ॥ पदानि ॥ तु, च, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तु इत्येतस्य नाभि परयुभयथा भवति ॥

BK VI. CH. IV. §. 10 ]

SOME MLES OF शेष ॥

1253

6. So also नृ before the Genitive Plural नाम is lengthened optionally.

As नृ नृणां नृपते, and नृ नृणां नृपते ॥ According to some this option is confined to the Vedas, according to others, it extends to secular literature also.

नोपधायाः ॥ ७ ॥ पदानि ॥ न, उपधायाः, ( नामि दीर्घः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ नान्तस्याङ्गस्योपधायाः नामि परतो दीर्घो भवति ॥

7. In a stem ending in नृ, the preceding vowel is lengthened before the affix नाम ॥

Thus पञ्चन् + नाम (VII. 1. 55) = पञ्चान् + नाम (VI. 4. 7) = पञ्चानाम् (VIII. 2. 7); संतानाम्, नयानाम्, इयानाम् ॥ Why do we say 'ending in नृ'? Observe चतुर्णाम् ॥ But not in चर्मणाम् where the affix is not नाम but आम् without नृ ॥

सर्वनामस्थाने चासंबुद्धौ ॥ ८ ॥ पदानि ॥ सर्वनामस्थाने, च, असम्बुद्धौ ( नोपधायाः दीर्घः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सर्वनामस्थाने च परतो ऽसंबुद्धौ नोपधायाः दीर्घो भवति ॥

8. In a stem ending in नृ, the preceding vowel is lengthened in strong cases, with the exception of the Vocative singular.

As राजा, राजानो, राजानः, राजानम्, राजानो ॥ So also सामानि तिष्ठन्ति ॥ राजा was राजान्, the स् was elided by VI. 1. 68, and नृ by VIII. 2. 7. Why do we say 'in strong cases'? Observe राजाने (Loc-Sing); सामानि (Loc. Sing). Why do we say 'but not in the Vocative Singular'? Observe हे राजन् ! हे तक्षन् !

वा पपूर्वस्य निगमे ॥ ९ ॥ पदानि ॥ वा, प, पूर्वस्य, निगमे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पपूर्वस्याचो नोपधायाः निगमविषये सर्वनामस्थाने परतो ऽसंबुद्धौ वा दीर्घो भवति ॥

9. The lengthening of the penultimate vowel of a stem ending in नृ, before the affixes of the strong-case, is optional in the Veda, when प precedes such a vowel.

Thus स तक्षाणं or तक्षणं, तिष्ठन्तमब्रवीत् । ऋग्विश्वाणं or ऋग्विश्वणमिन्द्रम् ॥

Why do we say 'in the Veda'? In the secular literature we have तक्षा, तक्षाणो तक्षाणः always.

सान्तमहतः संयोगस्य ॥ १० ॥ पदानि ॥ सान्त, महतः, संयोगस्य, ( दीर्घः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सकारान्तस्य संयोगस्य यो नकारः महतश्च तस्योपधायाः दीर्घो भवति सर्वनामस्थाने परतो ऽसंबुद्धौ ॥

10. In the strong cases with the exception of Vocative singular, the penultimate vowel is lengthened, in the case of a stem ending in स्, with a Nasal consonant preceding it, and of महत् ॥

28

1254

LENGTHENING.

[ Bk. VI. Ch. IV. § 12

That is, a stem ending in the conjunct consonant न्, elongates its penultimate vowel before the affixes of the first five cases. Thus श्रेयान्, श्रेयांसि, श्रेयांसः, श्रेयांसि, पयांसि, यशांसि ॥ महन्—महान्, महान्ती, महान्तः ॥ But हे श्रेयन्, हे महन् in Vocative Singular. The Nasal is inserted by VII. 1. 70.

अन्तुन्तुच्चस्वस्तुन्तुन्तुच्चद्वक्षन्तुहोतुपोतुप्रशास्तृणाम् ॥११॥ पदानि ॥ अप्, तुन्, तृच्, स्वस्तु, नन्तु, नेष्टु, त्वष्टु, क्षन्तु, होतु, पोतु, प्रशास्तृणाम् ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ अप् इत्येतस्य तृजन्तस्य स्वस्तु नन्तु नेष्टु त्वष्टु क्षन्तु होतु पोतु प्रशास्तु इत्येतेषां चान्नानामुपधाया दीर्घो भवति सर्वनामस्थाने परतो ऽसंबुद्धौ ॥

11. In the strong cases, with the exception of the Vocative Singular, the penultimate vowel is lengthened in अप्, in stems formed by तुन् and तृच् affixes, and in स्वस्तु, नन्तु, नेष्टु, त्वष्टु, क्षन्तु, होतु, पोतु and प्रशास्तु ॥

Thus आपः तिष्ठन्ति ॥ Some would have it even in compounds; as बह्वानि तदागानि ॥ The Samāsānta rule is not applied here, because it is *anitya*. If it be considered *nitya*, then also there is lengthening, but without the addition of the nasal. तत्र समासान्तो विधिनित्य इति समासान्तो न क्रियते । नित्यमपि च तुरमस्कृत्वा दीर्घत्वमिष्यते । नन्। कर्तारः कटान् । वदितारः जनापवादान् । कर्तारः । तृच् । कर्तारः कटस्य । कर्तारः । हर्तारः भारस्य । हर्तारः । स्वस्तु । स्वर्ताः । स्वर्तारः । स्वर्तारः । नन्तु । नमा । नम्रारः । नम्रारः । नेष्टु । नेष्टारः । नेष्टारः । त्वष्टु । त्वष्टारः । क्षन्तु । क्षत्तारः । क्षत्तारः । होतु । होतारः । होतारः । पोतु । पोतारः । पोतारः । प्रशास्तु । प्रशास्तारः । प्रशास्तारः । नन्तादीनां महणमव्युत्पत्तिपक्षे विध्यर्थम् । व्युत्पत्तिपक्षे नियमार्थम् । एवमुतानामन्येषां संज्ञा-शब्दानां दीर्घो मा भूविति । पितरः । पितरः । मातरः । आसंवृद्धाविति किम् । हे कर्तः । हे स्वः ॥

If the words नन्तु &c. be considered as कृति, not derived from any root, then their enumeration is here for the sake of Vidhi (injunction); if they be considered as derivative words formed by Upadi affixes, then their enumeration is for the sake of niyama (restriction), so that other words formed similarly are not to be governed by this rule. As पितरः, पितरः, मातरः, मातरः ॥ Why do we say 'not in the Vocative Singular'? Observe हे कर्तः, हे स्वः ॥ In the above examples अप् is substituted for कृ by VII. 3. 110.

इन्द्रपुष्पार्यणां शौ ॥ १२ ॥ पदानि ॥ इन्, इन्, पूष अर्यणां, शौ, ( दीर्घः ) ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ इन् इन् पूषन् अर्यमन् इत्येवमन्तानामङ्गानां शौ परत उपधाया दीर्घो भवति ॥

12. The penultimate vowel is lengthened before the affix शि (Nominative and Accusative Pl.), when the stem ends in इन्, or इन्, or पूषन् or अर्यमन् ॥

According to the maxim (See VI. 4. 14 also) that 'अन्, इन्, अस्, मन महणान्यर्थवता चानर्थकेण च सदन्त विधि प्रयोजयन्ति', the employment of इन् in this sūtra includes and means 'words ending in the syllable इन्' ॥ As regards the rest (इन् &c.), the affix शि (Neuter Pl.) is never added to them alone, but when they are parts of a compound. Thus इन् is a noun formed by the addition of

BK. VI. CH. IV. §. 12 ]

LENGTHENING.

1255

the affix बिप्प to the root हन्; and the affix Kvip is added to it only then, when it is preceded by another word like “Brahma” &c. See III. 2. 87. Similarly the words पूषन् and अयेमन् are masculine and cannot take the Neuter Plural affix शि in their original state. They must be parts of a neuter compound, to admit this affix. Hence we have used words “when the stem ends in इन् &c.”

Thus बहुवण्डीनि and बहुञ्छनीणि। बहुवृक्षाणि। बहुभृणाणि। बहुपूषाणि। बहुर्यमाणि ॥
सिद्धे सत्यारम्भो नियमार्थः। इन् नूपार्थमणामुपधायाः। शाबेव दीर्घो भवति नान्यच। इण्डिनो। छचिणो।
वृक्षिणो। पूषणो। अयेमणो ॥

Though this result could have been obtained by VI. 4. 8, the special mention of these words shows that except in Accusative and Nom. Pl. the lengthening does not take place in other strong cases. As इण्डिनो, छचिणो, वृक्षिणो, पूषणो, अयेमणो ॥

Kārikā :—Regarding the rule of lengthening taught about इन् &c here, let the wise reader, after making a restrictive rule with regard to सूद (sarvanāmas thāna) affixes in general, make again another rule regarding the affix शि in particular, (i. e., make a yoga-bibhāga). By so doing, the form भृणहनि (Loc. sin.) of the Achārya, will not be found fault with.

2. (But if yoga-vibhāga be not made) then I rule that the anuvritti of सूद being dropped, let the rule be made with regard to शि affix in general (without regarding it as a Sarvanāmasthāna affix). And as the rule of lengthening applies to penultimates, there would arise no fault, if the vowel of इन् is lengthened before the demonstrative affix य (in words like वृक्षायते=वृक्षाय इष आचरात, This refers to VII, 4. 25).

3. Or if the anuvritti of सूद (Sarvanāmasthāna) be taken into this Sūtra, because of the context, then the mention of शि in this Sūtra, (would be redundant, because the word Sarvanāmasthāna includes it, so far as the strong cases are concerned) but it would find scope and utility in preventing the lengthening in those cases to which the context of Sarvanāmasthāna does not apply. That is, the Sarvanāmasthāna will be restricted with regard to इन् &c to the affix शि and not to सूद affixes generally.

Note :—शि is the affix of the Nom. and Acc. Pl. in Neuter (VII. 1. 20.) It is a Sarvanāmasthāna by I. 1. 42. But the word Sarvanāmasthāna may be read into this sūtra from the preceding VI. 4. 8. What is then the necessity of employing शि in this? The above karika answers this.

In the case of इन् ending words, the subsequent rule VI. 4. 15, which required the lengthening of the penultimate vowel before an affix having an indicatory क् or इ्, is however debarred by the present restrictive rule. Thus the Locative Singular (हि) is वृक्षनि, and भृणहनि ॥ How do you make this? By splitting up the present sūtra into two parts, the first part being इन् इन् पूषार्थमणाम्, and the second being शौ ॥ It would then mean :—

1256

LENGTHENING.

[ Bk. VI. Ch. IV. § 14

(1) The penultimate vowel is lengthened, in strong cases only and no where else, when the stem ends in इन् or हन् or in पूषन् or अर्धमन् ॥ (2) So also it is lengthened before the strong case शि and no where else. These two restrictive rules therefore, would debar all other rules of penultimate lengthening which would otherwise have been applicable. But a rule which does not relate to penultimate vowel, is not debarred by this restriction, but does take effect. Thus वृक्षायते, भूणायते denominative verbs in क्यह् ॥

Or even though the Sarvanāmasthāna may be read into the sūtra by anuvṛtti, yet this may be considered a Restrictive Rule in general, and not only with regard to शि considered a Sarvanāmasthāna or a Neuter affix शि is the Sarvanāmasthāna affix of the Neuter: which has no other Sarvanāmasthāna, therefore, it is a general Niyama and not only a Sarvanāmasthāna or a Neuter niyama. Therefore in this niyama the word “नपुंसकस्य”—“of the Neuter”—is not to be taken.

For if it be taken, then the Sūtra would mean, the neuter stems in इन् &c are lengthened in शि only and no where else. The result would be that in examples like भूणहनि ब्राह्मणकृते (loc. sin), there would be no lengthening at all (i.e. we shall never have the form भूणहनि in loc. sin. by force of VI. 4. 15); moreover, by so doing, there would arise this anomaly also, that words other than Neuter would also not be lengthened.

The force of the definition of Sarvanāmasthāna applies to Neuter also in certain cases, therefore, any rule (niyama) made with regard to Sarvanāmasthāna would apply to Neuter also.

सौ च ॥ १३ ॥ पदानि ॥ सौ, च, ( उपधायाः दीर्घः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सावसंवृद्धौ परत इन्दुम्पुण्यमणापुण्याध्या दीर्घो भवति ॥

13. The penultimate vowels of a stem ending in इन्, हन्, पूषन् or अर्धमन् are lengthened before the affix सु of the Nominative Singular but not in Vocative Singular.

Thus इण्डी, वृक्षा, पूषा, अर्धमा ॥ The न् is elided by VIII. 2. 7, and the case-affix by VI. 1. 68. In the Vocative singular we have हे वण्डिन्, हे पूषन्, हे वृक्षन्, हे अर्धमन् ॥

अत्वसन्तस्य चाधातोः ॥ १४ ॥ पदानि ॥ अनु, असन्तस्य, च, अधातोः ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ अनु अस् इत्येवमन्तस्य अधातोऽपधायाः सावसंवृद्धौ परतो दीर्घो भवति ॥

14. In the Nominative Singular (with the exception of the Vocative Singular) the penultimate vowel is lengthened in a stem ending in अनु, and अस् when the consonant (अस्) does not belong to a root.

Thus मवान् (with डवतु) Un I. 63 from भा to shine), कृतवान् (with कवतु); गोमान् and यवमान् (with मतुप्) ॥ The नुस् (न्) is added to the above by VII. 1. 70, after the elongation has taken place, for if added before elongation, the

BK. VI. CH. [V. §. 16 ]

LENGTHENING.

1257

vowel no longer being *penultimate*, will not be lengthened at all. अस् :—as सुपया:, सुयशा:, सुयोता: ॥ Why do we say 'not belonging to a dhātu'? Observe पिण्डम: where स् belongs to the root अस् (पिण्डं असते), so also चर्मव: (चर्मं पस्ते) ॥ The अस् having no significance as an affix &c is also included here, on the strength of the maxim 'whenever अस् or इन् or अस् or मन्, when they are taught in Grammar denote by I. 1. 72, something that ends with these, there they represent these combination of letters both in so far as they possess, and also in so far as they are void of a meaning'. (अनिनस्मन् महानि अर्थवता चानर्थकेन च तदन्ताविर्ध प्रयोजयन्ति) ॥ The word अन्त in the sūtra indicates whatever *ends* in अतु whether when first enunciated (उपदेश), such as उवतु, कवतु &c, or which assumes the form अतु in grammatical inflection, such as मतुप् which in upadeśa ends in अतुप्, but becomes अतु in प्रयोग or application. In Vocative singular we have हे गोमन्, हे सुपय: this rule not applying there.

अनुनासिकस्य किङ्गलो: किङ्गति ॥ १५ ॥ पदानि ॥ अनुनासिकस्य, कि, झलो:, किङ्गति, (दीर्घः) ॥

वृत्ति: ॥ अनुनासिकान्तस्याङ्गस्य उपधाया दीर्घो भवति किंवप्रत्यये परतो झलादौ च किङ्गति ॥

15. The penultimate vowel of a stem, ending in a nasal, is lengthened before the affix कि, and before an affix having an indicatory क् or इ्, which begins with a consonant other than a semivowel or a nasal.

Thus प्रशान् and प्रतान् from the roots शम् and तम् by VIII. 2. 64. So also before an affix beginning with a झल् consonant (any consonant but a nasal and a semivowel). As शान्त: (with क्), शान्तवान् (with कवतु), शान्त्वा (with क्त्वा), and शान्ति: (with किन्). These are all formed with किन् affixes. As to डिन् affixes we have शशान्त: and तन्तान्त: formed by तस् 3rd Person Dual added to the Intensive roots शम् and तम् ॥ तस् is डिन् by I. 2. 4. Why do we say 'ending in a Nasal'? Observe ओदनपक, पक्:, पकुवान् ॥ Why do we say 'before कि and jhalādi affix'? Observe गम्यते, रम्यते ॥ Why do we say a डिन् or a किन् affix? Observe गन्ता and रन्ता ॥

अञ्जनगमां सनि ॥ १६ ॥ पदानि ॥ अञ्, हन्, गमाम्. सनि, ( वा दीर्घः ) ॥

वृत्ति: ॥ अजन्तानामङ्गमां हनिगम्योऽ सनि झलादौ परे वा दीर्घो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ गमैरिङ्गदिशस्येति वक्तव्यम् ॥

16. The lengthening of the vowel takes place in the case of a stem ending in a vowel, as well as of हन् and गम्, when the Desiderative affix सन् being jhalādi (i. e. not taking the augment इन्) follows.

Thus of roots ending in vowel we have :—विधीषति, तुष्टुपति, चिकीर्षति, जिहीर्षति (VII. 1. 100); of हन् and गम्, जिघांसति, and अधिजिगांसते ॥

2158

LENGTHENING.

[ Bk.VI. Ch. IV. 19.

*Vârt*:—The rule applies to that गम् which is the substitute of इह (II. 4. 48) 'to study'. Therefore, not here, संजिगंसते वस्सो मात्रा (cf. VII. 2. 58); In the Veda we read स्वर्गे लोके संजिगंसत्, where though गम् means 'to go' and is not, therefore, the substitute of इह, the lengthening takes place by the rule VI. 3. 137. Or the word अच् should not be added in the sūtra at all: which should be read as हनगं सनि meaning 'There is lengthening of the stem when the Desiderative सन् follows'. This would apply of course, to vowel-ending stems, because the sentence would mean that, for there cannot be lengthening of a consonant. This will apply to गम् also, in this way:—'A stem ending in a vowel is lengthened in the Desiderative, and so also of गम् which is a substitute of the vowel-stem इ' ॥ In this way, we may see, that there is no necessity of the Vārtika.

तनोतेविभाषा ॥ १७ ॥ पदानि ॥ तनोतेः, विभाषा ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तनोतेव्यस्य सनि ज्ञात्री विभाषा दीर्घो भवति ॥

17. The lengthening of the stem of तन् is optional, before the Desiderative सन्, when it does not take the augment इह ॥

Thus तितांसति or तितंसति ॥ But in तितानिषति no alternative is allowed, as इह is added to सन् by VII. 2. 49 Vârt: optionally.

क्रमश्च कि ॥ १८ ॥ पदानि ॥ क्रमः, च, कि, ( झलि ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ क्रम उपधाया विभाषा दीर्घो भवति स्वापत्यये ज्ञात्री परतः ॥

18. The penultimate of क्रम is optionally lengthened, before the affix क्वा, when it is without the augment इह ॥

Thus क्त्वा or क्त्वा; but क्त्वा only, with इह augment. But when क्त्वा is replaced by ल्यप्, the rule does not apply: as प्रक्रम्य, उपक्रम्य ॥ This is on the maxim अन्तर्ज्ञानपि विधीत् बहिर्ज्ञात्यप् बोधते 'a bahiranga substitution of ल्यप् supersedes even antaranga rule'.

च्छोः शूडनुनासिके च ॥ १९ ॥ पदानि ॥ च्छोः, शूड, अनुनासिके, च, ( किञ्चलोः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ छ इयेतस्य सतुक्रस्य वकारस्य च स्थाने यथासम्बन्धे श ऊइ इयेतावादेही भवतः, अनुनासिकादे प्रत्यये परतः वचो ज्ञात्री च क्त्विति: ॥

19. For च्छ (including the augment तुक्) is substituted श्, and for व is substituted ऊइ, before an affix beginning with a Nasal, as well as before कि and jhalādi ङित् and कित् affixes (VI. 4. 15).

Thus प्रक्षः, विश्वः from प्रच्छ and विच्छ, with the affix नङ् (III. 3. 90) the च्छ being replaced by श् ॥ Similarly from the root सिब् we have स्योनः thus: सिब्+न (Un III. 9).=सि+ऊ+न=स्व+न=स्योनः (VII. 3. 84). Here the ऊ is added to the stem prior to the scope being given to the guna rule of VII. 3. 86, otherwise the form would be सिब्+न=सेब्+न=से+ऊ+न ॥ Having thus added ऊ,

BK. VI. CH. IV § 20. ]

LENGTHENING.

1259

before scope could be given to the *guṇa* rule VII. 3. 86, we make *sandhi* of *स+अ=स्व*, because semivowel substitution is *antaranga* operation and of wider scope than *guṇa*, and the maxim of *वाणाद्वाङ्ग बलियो भवति* has no scope here. “An operation which is taught in the *Angādhikāra*, and affects the *anga* or stem, possesses greater force than an operation which concerns a combination of letters (i. e. is taught in a *sandhi* rule)”.

With *कु* we have *शब्दांशु* formed with *किप्* (Uṇ II. 57) added to *पच्छ*, there is no vocalisation of the semivowel *र*, and there is lengthening of *अ*, and *च्छ* changed to *श*. So also *गोविष्* ॥

Of the change of *व* into *क* we have the following:—*अक्षयुः*, *हिरण्ययुः* (*विष्+किप्=वि+अ=स्वः*) ॥ Here the *क* substitution is *Bahiranga*, and *वि+अ=स्व*, the change of *इ* into *य* is *antaranga*, therefore on the maxim of *असिद्धे बहिरङ्ग-मन्तरङ्गे* (a *bahiranga* is non-existent for the purposes of an *antaranga*), there should be no change of *इ* into *य*, for *क* is non-existent. That maxim is however set aside by *नाजानन्तर्यं बहिरङ्गं प्रबन्धम्*: “A *bahiranga* operation is not regarded as *bahiranga*, and consequently *asiddha*, when an *antaranga* operation is to take effect, which depends on the immediate sequence of a vowel and something else”.

So also before a *jhalādi affix*; as *पच्छ+क=पृष्टः*, *पृष्टवान्* (*कवत्*), *पृष्ट्वा* (*कत्वा*); here *च्छ* is changed to *श*, there is vocalisation by VI. 1. 16, and *श* changed to *ष* by VIII. 2. 36.

So also *व* is changed to *क* as, *शूनः*, *शूनवान्*, *शून्वा* ॥

When the affixes are not *डिन्* or *किन्*, the rule does not apply: as *शुभ्याम्*, *शुभिः* ॥ Some do not read the *anuvritti* of *किन्* and *डिन्* into this *sūtra*, and explain *शुभ्याम्* and *शुभिः* by VI. 1. 131: *उ* short being substituted for *व* of *विष्* ॥

In “*छशां व*” (VIII. 2. 36) the letter *छ* should not be taken, because by the force of the present *sūtra*, *श* is ordained to come every where in the place of *छ* ॥

The indicatory *इ* in *कइ* is for the sake of distinguishing this *क* in *sūtras* like *एते* *धन्युद्* *छ* (VI. 1. 89). In the *sutra* *वाह* *कइ* (VI. 4. 132) there is also indicatory *इ* ॥

*ज्वरत्वरश्चिद्यविमवामुपधायाश्च* ॥ २० ॥ *पदानि* ॥ *ज्वर*, *त्वर*, *श्चिवि*, *अवि*, *मवाम्*, *उपधायाः*, *च*, (*किङ्गलोः वस्य*) ॥

*वृत्तिः* ॥ *ज्वर* *त्वर* *श्चिवि* *अव* *मव* *इत्येत्तामङ्गानां* *वकारस्य* *उपधायाश्च* *स्थाने* *कडित्ययमादेशो* *मवति* *कवो* *परतो* *उन्नासिके* *इत्यादौ* *च* *कडिति* ॥

20. In *ज्वर*, *त्वर* *श्चिव*, *अव*, and *मव*, before the above-mentioned affixes (*किन्*, a *Nasal* or a *jhalādi* ‘*किन्*’ or *डिन्*) there is the single substitution of *कइ* for the *व* and the vowel preceding the final consonant.

Thus जूः, जूरो, जूः, जूति: ॥ स्वरः—जूः, जूरो, जूः, जूति: ॥ श्रिविः—जूः, जूरो, जूः, जूतः, जूतवान, जूतिः ॥ अचः—जूः, जूरो, जूः, जूति: ॥ मयः—जूः, जूरो, जूः, जूतः, जूतवान, जूतिः ॥ ज्वरस्वरो—रूपधा वकारात् परा, श्रिव्य वमवां पूर्वा ॥

In ज्वर and स्वर the ज replaces व as well as the अ which follows व; and in श्रिव्य, अच and मय it replaces the व and the vowel व and अ which precede व ॥ Another reading is श्रिव ॥

असिद्धवद्वाऽऽ भात् ॥ २२ ॥ पदानि ॥ असिद्धवत्, अत्र, आभात् ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ असिद्धवद्विद्ययमधिकारो यदित ऊर्जुमनुकमिष्याम आ अध्यायपरिसममिस्तद् असिद्धवद्विदितव्यम् ॥
वार्तिकम् ॥ दुग्धुदाइवद्वयणोः सिद्धो भवत इति वक्तव्यम् ॥

22. The change, which a stem will undergo by the application of any of the rules from this sūtra upto VI. 4. 129, is to be considered as not to have taken effect, when we have to apply any other rule of this very section VI. 4. 23 to 129.

This is an adhikāra rule. The above translation is given according to Prof. Bohtlingk. According to Kāsika the असिद्धवत् extends up to the end of the chapter. Dr. Ballantyne translates it thus:—"The rules, reckoning from this one to the end of the chapter, are called Abhiya, because the chapter ends with a series of rules dependant on the aphorism 'bhasya' VI. 4. 129. When that (i. e. one of the abhiya rules) is to be brought into operation, having the same place for coming into operation as another abhiya, which has already taken effect, that one which has taken effect, shall be regarded as not having taken effect".

The word आभात् means 'up to म' i. e. upto VI. 4. 129. in which last sūtra the word म occurs: i. e. in applying the rules taught upto VI. 4. 129. The word अत्र shows that the two rules must have the same आश्रय or place of operation, where their places of operation are different, they are not asiddha to each other. The word असिद्ध shows that an utsarga or general rule must take effect, as if existing in spite of a special rule, and that an 'ādesa' or substitution taught by another rule should not be considered to have taken effect in applying the special rule. Thus in forming एधि and शाधि (Imperative 2nd person)

BK. VI. CH. IV § 22 ]

ABHIYA-RULES.

1261

ए is first substituted for अस् 'to be' by VI. 4. 119 : and शा for शास् by VI. 4. 35 and then is धि added by VI. 4. 101. The latter rule says that धि is added in the Imperative, only after those roots which end in a consonant of झल् class. Now अस् and शास् end in a *jhal* consonant, and can take धि, but their substitute ए and शा end in a vowel and not a consonant and should not take धि ॥ The present rule helps us here, and for the application of धि (VI. 4. 101) the substitution of ए for अस् or शा for शास् should be considered as asiddha or not to have taken effect. Similarly in आगहि (Vedic Imperative, शप् being elided by II. 4. 73) and जहि from गन् and हन्, the nasal being elided in the case of गन्, VI. 4. 36 and ज being substituted for हन् (VI. 2. 36) we have the stems आग and ज, which ending in अ would require the elision of हि by VI. 4. 105. But since the change of ज &c is not regarded as having been accomplished, the elision of हि does not take place.

Why do we say आभात् 'up to VI. 4. 129'? In applying any other rule the changes ordained by abhiya rules would not be considered as asiddha. Thus अभाजि and रागः from भञ्ज् and रञ्ज् ॥ Here the nasals of rañj and bhañj have been elided by VI. 4. 27-28 and 33 before the affixes घम् and चिन् respectively, and we have the stems रङ्, and भञ् to which rule VII. 2. 116 applies and we have Vriddhi of अ preceding the final consonant. Had the elision of the nasal been considered as non-effective for the purposes of VII. 2. 116, then अ could not have taken Vriddhi, as it would not then be उपधा or penultimate.

Why do we use the word अच् in the aphorism? The rules are asiddha to each other with regard to a common place of operation and not otherwise. Thus पा + वस् (कुम्) + अस् (शस् Acc. Pl.) = पपा + उस् + अस् (VI. 4. 131 vocalisation of व). If this व substitute be considered as asiddha for the purposes of sutra VI. 4. 64, then we cannot elide the आ of पा, because आ is not then followed by a vowel (व being non-existent). व however is not considered as asiddha, and आ being thus elided, we have पपुषः in पपुषः पदय ॥ Similarly चि + वस् + अस् = चिचि + उस् + अस् ॥ Here also व is not considered asiddha, and we apply rule VI. 4. 82, and substitute य for व as चिच्युषः पञ्य ॥ Similarly ल् + वस् + अस् ल्ल् + उस् + अस् = ल्ल्ल्वुषः ॥ Here also व is not considered asiddha, and we change the क of ल् into उव् by VI. 4. 77. In all the above three cases, the elision of आ, or change of इ to य, or of क to उव्, takes place in reference to वस्, while the samprasāraṇa of व takes place with reference to the Accusative plural case-ending अस् which makes the stem Bha. So they have not the same आभय ॥ Nor does the maxim of असिञ् (बहिर्कमन्तर्क) apply here, because the special maxim of Abhiya governs the sutras of this section, so there cannot be the relation of Antaranga and Bahiranga among these sutras, simultaneously with their being asiddha to each other.

*Vārti:*—The substitute युक् (VI. 4. 88), and युद् (VI. 4. 63) should however be considered as not asiddha, and rule VI. 4. 77 teaching उवक् and VI. 4. 82, teaching यु substitution should not be applied simultaneously with them. Thus भु—बभूव, बभूवतः बभूवः with युक्, and उपदिशीये, उपदिशीयते, उपदिशीयरे with युद् of VI. 4. 63. In the case of भु, when युक् is added, there is not the addition of उवक्, and in the case of धीक्, when युद् is added, there is not यणदिश ॥

The आ in आभात् has the force of limit inclusive, so that, the asiddha rule applies to the sūtras governed by भ ॥

आश्लोपः ॥ २३ ॥ पदानि ॥ आत्, न लोपः, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आडिति अमययुस्सुहमकारो गृह्यते तत उत्तरस्य नकारस्य लोपो भवति ॥

23. After न, which is added to the roots of the seventh class as a characteristic (i. e. the vikaraṇa अम), there is the elision of the following न ॥

Thus अनक्ति and मनक्ति from अञ्ज 'to anoint', and भञ्ज 'to break'. Thus अञ्ज+अम्+तिप्=अनञ्ज+ति (I. 1. 47)=अनञ्ज+ति (VI. 4. 23)=अनक्ति ॥ So also हिनस्ति from हिंसि (हिन्स्) 'to injure'. Why do we say 'after अ' and not merely 'after न', without the indicatory श? Observe यज्ञानाम्, यज्ञानाम्, where the न of नाम् is not elided after the न of यज्ञ and यज्ञ, the lengthening of अ by VII. 3. 102 being sthānivat would not have prevented the elision. In the case of विश्रामाम् and प्रश्नानाम् (formed by विश्र+नाम् and प्रश्न+नाम्) also, the न of नाम् is not elided after अ of विश्र ॥ For the अ of the sūtra is the technical अ the vikaraṇa, and not any combination of the letters श and न ॥ The prati-padokta maxim applies here. लक्षणप्रतिपदोक्तयोः पतिपदोक्तस्यैव महणम् ॥

अनिदितां हल उपधायाः कृडिति ॥ २४ ॥ पदानि ॥ अनिदिताम्, हलः, उपधायाः, कृडिति ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अनिदितामङ्गानां हलन्तानामुपधाया नकारस्य लोपो भवति कृडिति प्रथये परतः ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ अनिदितां नलोप लङ्किकम्योरुपतापशरीरविकारयोरुपसंख्यानं कर्तव्यम् ॥

वा० ॥ रञ्जेणो मृगरमणउपसंख्यानं कर्तव्यम् ॥ वा० ॥ धितुणि च रञ्जेरुपसंख्यानं कर्तव्यम् ॥

वा० ॥ रजकरजनरजः मृपसंख्यानं कर्तव्यम् ॥

24. In a root-stem ending in a consonant preceded by न,—this न not being added to the root owing to its having an indicatory इ (VII. 1. 58)—the न is elided when an affix having an indicatory क् or ङ् follows.

Thus from अन्स् and धन्स् are formed अस्तः and ध्वस्तः with क्, अस्यते, ध्वस्यते with यक्, सनीअस्यते, इनीध्वस्यते with यक् the नी being added by VII. 4. 84. But नन्यते and नानन्यते, the न is not elided, the root being written in the Dhātupātha as हुणादि संख्यो, and न being added by VII. 1. 58. Why do we say ending in a consonant? Observe नीयते, ननीयते from नी which has a penulti-

BK VI. CH. IV § 28 ]

ELISION OF NASAL.

1263

mate nasal, but ends in a vowel. Why do we say 'penultimate'? Observe नक्षते, नानक्षते ॥ Why do we say having an indicatory क or ङ? Observe संसन्, ध्वंसन् with ल्युद् ॥

Vårt:—The roots लङ् (लङ्) and कम् (कम्) are exceptions, where meaning 'to feel pain or difficulty' and 'a disease of the body'. These, though exhibited in the Dhātupatha with an indicatory इ, are treated as exceptions to the rule of अनिदित्: thus विलगितः and विकपितः, when not having the above meanings, we have विलङ्दितं and विकपित् ॥

Vårt:—The causative of the root रञ्ज, loses its nasal when meaning 'to hunt deer': as, रञ्जयति घृगान् 'he hunts the deer', but रञ्जयति वस्त्राणि 'he colors the clothes'.

Vårt:—रञ्ज loses its nasal before the affix चिदुण्, as रागी ॥

Vårt:—The words रञ्जकः, रञ्जनम्, and रञ्जः are formed from रञ्ज by the elision of the nasal.

दंशसञ्जस्वञ्जां शपि ॥ २५ ॥ पदानि ॥ दंश, सञ्ज, स्वञ्जाम्, शपि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ दंश सञ्ज स्वञ्ज इत्येतेषामङ्गानां शपि परत उपधाया नकारस्य लोपो भवति ॥

25. The nasal of दंश, सञ्ज and स्वञ्ज is elided before the vikaraṇa शप् of the roots of the 1st class.

Thus दधाति, सजति and परिष्वजते for the change of the स् of स्वञ्ज to प see VIII. 3. 65

रञ्जेश्च ॥ २६ ॥ पदानि ॥ रञ्जेः, च, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ रञ्जेश्च शपि परत उपधाया नकारस्य लोपो भवति ॥

26. The nasal of रञ्ज is also elided before शप् ॥

As रजति, रजतः, रजन्ति ॥ The separation of this from the preceding is for the sake of the subsequent sūtras in which the anuvṛiti of rañj only runs and not of dañs &c.

घञि च भावकरणयोः ॥ २७ ॥ पदानि ॥ घञि, च, भावकरणयोः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ भावकरणवाचिनि घञि परतो रञ्जेरुपधाया नकारस्य लोपो भवति ॥

27. The penultimate nasal of रञ्ज is elided before घञ्, when the word formed with it expresses a state or an instrument.

Thus रागः 'passion, color, or the coloring stuff'. Thus आश्चर्यो रागः, विचित्र रागः denote भाव, while रञ्जतेऽनेनिति रागः denotes instrument. The घञ् is added by III. 3. 121; and च् changed to क् by VII. 3. 52. But रञ्जः=रजन्ति तस्मिन् 'a theatre;

28. The word स्यद is formed by घञ् in the sense of 'speed'.

1264

ELISION OF NASAL.

[BK. VI, CH. IV. 32]

This word is derived from स्यन्द, the nasal is elided, and the Vriddhi prohibited irregularly. Though the ardhadhatuka affix घम् causes here the elision of a portion of the root, viz of न् of स्यन्द, yet rule I. 1. 4 does not apply here. That rule prohibits Guna and Vriddhi, only in case of इक् vowels, here the Vriddhi is prevented with regard to ञ् ॥ The prevention of this Vriddhi is irregular and not governed by I. 1. 4. Thus गोस्वः 'अम्बस्वः' meaning 'cow-speed,' 'horse-speed,' but तैलस्वः, and पूतस्वः meaning 'dripping of oil or ghee'.

अवोदैचौघप्रश्रथहिमश्रथाः ॥२९॥ पदानि ॥ अवोद, एघ, ओघ, प्रश्नथ, हिमश्रथाः
वृत्तिः ॥ अवोद एघ ओघप्रश्रथ हिमश्रथ इवेते निपातन्ते ।

29. अवोद, एघ, ओघ, प्रश्नथ, and हिमश्रथ are irregularly formed by the elision of न ॥

Thus उन्द्—अव+उन्द्+घम्=अवोदः; इन्ध्+घम्=एघः, the guna is irregular, for I. 1. 4 applied here, and prevented guna. उन्द्+मन्=ओघ (Unadi मन्). प्र+श्रन्थ+घम्=प्रश्नथः (The want of Vriddhi is the irregularity). So also हिमश्रथः ॥

नाञ्जेः पूजायाम् ॥ ३० ॥ पदानि ॥ न, अञ्चेः, पूजायाम्, ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ अञ्चेः पूजायामर्थे नकारस्य लोपो न भवति ॥

30. The nasal of अञ्च is not elided when the meaning is to honor.

Thus अञ्चिता अस्य गुरवः, अञ्चितमिव शिरो बहति ॥ The इद् augment is added by VII. 2. 53. When the sense is not that of 'honoring', we have उदकृप्तक कृपात् 'the water was drawn from the well.' Here the इद् is prohibited by VII. 2. 15.

कि स्कन्दिस्यन्दोः ॥ ३१ ॥ पदानि ॥ कि, स्कन्दि, स्यन्दोः, ( न लोपः ) ॥

31. स्कन्द and स्यन्द retain their nasal before the affix क् ॥

Thus स्कन्द्वा, and स्यन्दिव्वा or स्यन्द्वा, the इद् being added when स्यन्द is considered as having an indicatory क् in the dhatupatha. When इद् is added, क्का is no longer क्ति by virtue of the rule I. 2. 18, and elision would not take place, for no rule of elision would apply in that case.

जान्तनशां विभाषा ॥ ३२ ॥ पदानि ॥ जान्त, नशाम्, विभाषा ( न लोपः ) ॥

32. The nasal may be optionally elided before क्का in a root ending in ज् and in नश् ॥

Thus रङ्गस्वा or रङ्गस्वा, मङ्गस्वा or मङ्गस्वा, नङ्गस्वा or नङ्गस्वा See ॥ VII. 1. 60 for the augment न् in नश् ॥ When इद् comes, we have नशिव्वा ॥

33. The nasal may be optionally elided in भज before the third person Passive of the Aorist in चिण् (ई)

Thus अभाजि or अभाज्जि ॥ This is an aprāpta vibhāshā, and teaches for the first time the elision of न in a certain contingency.

शास इदुहल्लोः ॥ ३४ ॥ पदानि ॥ शासः, इत्, अङ्, हल्लोः, ( कङ्किति ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ शास उपधाया इकारादेशो भवति अङ् परतो हल्लो च कङ्किति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ क्वी च शास इदं भवतीति वक्तव्यम् ॥ वा० ॥ क्विष् प्रत्यये तस्यापि भवतीति वक्तव्यम् ॥

34. Before the Aorist in अङ् and before an affix beginning with a consonant having an indicatory क् or ङ्, there is the substitution of इ for the vowel of शास् ॥

Thus अन्वशिषत्, अन्वशिषताम् and अन्वशिषन्; so also शिष्टः (with क्), शिष्टवान् (with क्तवत्), तो शिष्टः वयं शिष्यः (with the tense-affixes तः and नः which are ङ् by I. 2. 4). The स is changed to ष by VIII. 3. 60. Why do we say 'before the affixes of अ Aorist and consonant affixes'? Observe शासति, शशासत्, शशासः ॥

Vart:—There is the substitution of इ for the vowel of शास् before the affix क्वि ॥ As आयैशीः = आयैश् शास्ति ॥ So also मिथशीः ॥ The form is thus evolved, शास् + क्वि = शिस् + ० = शिर + ० = शीः (the short इ being lengthened by VIII. 2. 76.

The root शास् is that root which takes अङ् aorist; namely the second Adādi शास् (शास् अनुशिष्टो), and not the Bhvādi and the first Adādi शास् (अङ् शास् इच्छायाम्) ॥ Therefore not here आशास्ते, आशास्यमानः ॥

Vart:—But before क्किप्, this शास् also is changed, as आशीः, आशिषो, आशिषः ॥ Or this is an irregular form indicated by the author in the word सियाशीः used in VIII. 2. 104.

शा हो ॥ ३५ ॥ पदानि ॥ शा, हो, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ शासो हो परतः शा इत्ययमादेशो भवति ॥

35. Before the Imperative affix हि, शा is substituted for शास् ॥

Thus अनुशाधि, प्रशाधि ॥ The हि is changed to धि by VI. 4. 101. See VI 4. 22. The anuvritti of उपधायाः is not here; so शा is substituted in the room of the full word शास् and not only for the penultimate vowel of शास् ॥ The anuvritti of क्तिव् and ङ् also is not here. Therefore, when this हि is treated as पिन् (III. 4. 88), then too the substitution takes place, though a पिन् Sārvadhātuka is not ङ् (I. 2. 4). Thus शाधि is also found in the Vedas as having acute on the first syllable, which can only be when धि is पिन् and consequently anudātta (III. 1. 4)

हन्तेजः ॥ ३६ ॥ पदानि ॥ हन्तेः, जः, ( हो ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ हन्तेजः इत्ययमादेशो भवति हो परतः ॥
