36. ज is substituted for ह्व् before हि ॥

Thus जहि शत्रूम् ॥

अनुदात्तोपदेशवनतितनोत्यादीनामनुनासिकलोपो झलि कडिति ॥ ३७ ॥ पदानि ॥
अनुदात्तोपदेश, वनति, तनोत्यादीनाम्, अनुनासिक लोपः, झलि, कडिति ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ अनुदात्तोपदेशानामज्ञानां वनतितनोत्यादीनां चानुनासिकलोपो भवति झलादि कडिति प्रत्यये परतः ॥

37. The final nasal of those roots which in the Dhātupāṭha have an unaccented root-vowel, as well as of वन and तन &c, is elided before an affix beginning with a consonant (except a semi-vowel or nasal), when these have an indicatory क् or ङ् ॥

Thus यमु gives us यल्वा (with त्वा), यतः (with क्त), यतवान् (with क्तवत्), यतिः (with किन्), Similarly यमु gives us रल्वा, रतः, रतवान्, रतिः ॥ यम्, रम, नम्, गम्, हम् and मम् which end in a nasal are to be considered as unaccented roots, though taught as accented in the Dhātupāṭha. So also of वनः i. e. यतिः with किन्; with किन् the nasal is not elided as वन्ति; (VI. 4. 39): and before other jhalādi affixes व, retains न् as all those affixes take the augment हम् ॥ The तनादि roots belong to the eighth class. Thus ततः, ततवान् The Tanādi roots are ten in number, तन, सन, क्षण, क्षिण, क्षण, क्षण, घण, वन, मम् and क्तम् ॥ Of these सन् takes long आ also (VI. 4. 45): क्षण—क्षतः, क्षतवान्, क्षण—कृतः, कृतवान्; क्षण—कृतः, तुतवान्; घण—घृतः, घृतवान्; वन—वतः, वतवान्; मम्—मतः, मतवान् ॥

Why do we say before a ङिन् affix? Observe अतत, अतथाः (I. 2. 11 these affixes are ङिन्) So also not in शान्तः, शान्तवान्, शान्तः, शान्तवान्, शान्तः, शान्तवान्, not being anudātta in the Dhātupāṭha. If the root does not end in a nasal, the rule does not apply, as in पवनः, पवनवान् ॥ If the affix does not begin with a jhal consonant, the rule does not apply: as गन्धते, रन्धते ॥ If the affix is not किन् or ङिन् the rule does not apply: as, यन्ता, यन्तव्यम् ॥ Why do we say “anudātta by upadesa”? So that the rule may apply to गम् root, as गतिः, but not to शम्, as शान्तः शान्तवान् ॥ For गतिः is formed by किन् affix and is accented with udātta on the first, but it is a secondary udātta and not of upadesa or dhātupāṭha, and does not prevent the elision of न् of गम् ॥ Similarly शम् is udātta-upadesa though in शान्त it has become अनुदातः ॥ The former though taught in the Dhātupāṭha as udātta, has been specifically mentioned above as anudātta, and शम् is taught as udatta in the Dhātupāṭha, and no where else taught as anudātta.

वा ल्यपि ॥ ३८ ॥ पदानि ॥ वा, ल्यपि, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ल्यपि परतो अनुदात्तोपदेशवनतितनोत्यादीनामनुनासिकलोपो वा भवति ॥

38. The nasal of the above roots (i. e. anudātta ending in a nasal, and वन and तनादि) is optionally elided before the Absolutive affix ल्यप् ॥

BK. VI. CH. IV § 42 ]

ABHYA-RULS.

1267

This is a vyavasthita-vibhāṣā. The option applies to roots ending in स. In the case of roots ending in other nasals, the elision is compulsory. Thus प्रथम् or प्रथम्, प्रथम् or प्रथम्, प्रणथम् or प्रणथम्, आगत्य आगत्य, but no option in आहत्य, प्रमत्य, प्रथत्य, प्रथत्य ॥

न किंचि दीर्घैश्च ॥ ३९ ॥ पदानि ॥ न, किंचि, दीर्घैः, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ किंचि परतो ऽनुवाचोपदेशादीनामनुनासिकलोपो दीर्घैश्च न भवति ।

39. Before the affix किंच्, the above roots neither drop their nasal nor lengthen their root-vowel.

The above roots i. e. anudāttopadeśa, ending in a nasal, and वन and तनादि, do not lose their nasal before किंच्. Thus यन्ति, तन्ति, वन्ति ॥ The lengthening would have taken place by VI. 4. 15, when the nasal was not elided : that also is prohibited.

गमः कौ ॥ ४० ॥ पदानि ॥ गमः, कौ, ( अनुनासिकलोपः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अनुनासिकलोप इति वर्तते । गमः क्वो परतो ऽनुनासिकलोपो भवति ।

वार्तिके म् ॥ गमादीनामिति वक्तव्यम् ॥ वा० ॥ ऊह् च गमादीनामितिवक्तव्यम् ॥

40. The nasal of गम् is always elided before कि ॥

Thus अङ्गगत्, कलिङ्गगत्, अघ्यगतो हरयः ॥ The त् is added by VI. 1. 71.

Vārt:—It should be stated of गम् and the rest. The elision takes place here also संयत्, परीतत् ॥

Vārt:—The nasal of गम् &c. is elided before ऊह् : as, अभ्रेयुः, अभ्रेयुः ॥

विद्वनोरनुनासिकस्यात् ॥ ४१ ॥ पदानि ॥ विद्वनोः, अनुनासिकस्य आत् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ विद्वि वने च प्रथये परतो ऽनुनासिकान्तस्याङ्गस्याकार आदेशोभवति ॥

41. A stem ending in a nasal, and followed by the affix विद्व् or वन, always substitutes long आ for its nasal.

Thus अञ्जाः, गोजाः, ऋतजाः, अद्विजाः, गोषाः (e. g. गोषा इन्द्रानुषा असि Rig V.), कृपखाः, शतखाः, सहस्रखाः, दधिकाः, अभ्रेया उन्नेतृणाम् ॥ The affix विद्व् (which is totally elided) is added under III. 2. 67. The स of सन् is changed to प by VIII. 3. 108. in गोषा ॥ With the affix वन we have the following:—विजावा, अभ्रेयावा (III. 2. 75). The repetition of the word अनुनासिक in this sūtra shows that the limitation of anudāttopadeśa &c. which applied to the अनुनासिक of sūtra VI. 4. 37 does not apply here.

जनसनखनां सनझलोः ॥ ४२ ॥ पदानि ॥ जन-सन-खनाम् सन्-झलोः, (आत्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ जन सन खन इत्येतेषामङ्गानां सनि झलादौ क्विति झलादौ प्रथय परत आकार आदेशो भवति ।

42. The long आ is substituted for the final of जन, सन् and खन् before the consonant beginning Desiderative affix सन्, and before any other affix beginning with a jhal consonant, which has an indicatory क् or ङ् ॥

1268

ABHIYA-RULES

[ Bk. VI. Ch. IV §. 44.

Thus जातः, जातवान्, जातिः, सातः, सातवान्, सातिः, सिपासति; खातः, खातवान्, खातिः॥
In जन् and खन् the Desiderative does not begin with a consonant, but takes the augment इन्, the न् is not therefore elided, as जिजनिपति, चिखानिपति ॥ In the case of the root सन्, the Desiderative takes इ, so we have two forms सिपासति and सिसनिपति (VII. 2. 49). The Desiderative has, therefore, been mentioned in the aphorism, only for the sake of the root सन् ॥

If the phrase सन्झलोः be taken to mean 'the Desiderative beginning with a consonant', then we should read the anuvṛtti of झलि कडिति from the preceding sūtras, to complete the sense of this; and if the phrase means "when the Desiderative of a jhalādi affix follows", then we should qualify the word Desiderative by the word jhal from the preceding sūtras. Or we may divide the sūtra into two (1) Before a किन् or डिन् jhalādi affix long आ is the substitute of the न् of 'jan', 'san' and 'khan'. (2) And so is the case, when the Desiderative affix follows, not having the augment इ, for then also the न् of 'jan', 'san' and 'khan' is replaced by long आ ॥

The न् of the root सन् would have required elision by VI. 4. 37, because this verb belongs to Tanādi class, still the आ substitution taught in this sūtra takes place, by preference, on the maxim of विप्रनिषेधे परं कार्यम् (I. 4. 2). In fact, though in this section of asiddha (VI. 4. 22) one rule is considered as asiddha for the purposes of the operations of another rule, yet one rule supersedes another by the maxim of vipratisedha. That that maxim applies in this section also, is to be inferred from the employment of the term इन् in VI. 4. 66, which supersedes the lopa of आ taught in VI. 4. 64, and substitutes instead the long ई ॥

ये विभाषा ॥ ४३ ॥ पदानि ॥ ये, विभाषा, (जनसनखनाम् आत्) ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ यकारादि द्विति प्रत्यये परतो जनसनखनामाकार आदिशो भवति विभाषा ।

43. There is optionally the substitution of long आ for the finals of जन्, सन् and खन् before an affix beginning with य and marked with an indicatory क् or इ ॥

Thus जायते or जन्मते (with यक्) जाजायते or जञ्जन्यते (with यङ्) । So also सायते or सन्यते, सासायते, or संसन्यते, खायते, or खन्यते, चाखायते or चङ्खन्यते ॥ Before the vikaraṇa खन् of the Fourth class, which is डिन् according to I. 2. 4; the आ is always substituted for जन् by VII. 3. 79. No option is allowed there.

तनोतेयेकि ॥ ४४ ॥ पदानि ॥ तेनोतेः, यकि, (विभाषा आत्) ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ तेनोतेयेकि परतो विभाषा आकार आदिशो भवति ।

44. The long आ may be optionally substituted for the final of तन् before the Passive characteristic यक् ॥

Thus तायते or तन्यते; but no option is allowed in तन्तन्यते with यङ् ॥

सनः किचि लोपश्चास्यान्यतरस्याम् ॥ ४५ ॥ पदानि ॥ सनः, किचि, लोपः, च, अस्य, अन्यतरस्याम्, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सनोतेङ्गस्य किचि प्रत्यये परत आकार आदिशो भवति लोपश्चास्यान्यतरस्याम् ।

BK VI. CH. IV. §. 46 ]

LENGTHENING

1269

45. The long आ is optionally substituted for the final of सन् before the affix किञ्च; and there is also elision optionally of the Nasal.

Thus we have three forms सातिः, सन्ति: and सति: ॥ The word अन्यतरस्याम् 'optionally' has been employed in the sūtra for the sake of clearness only; for the विभाषा of VI. 4. 43 could have been read into it by annvṛtti. Lest any one should doubt, that the annvṛtti of विभाषा had ceased with the last aphorism, this word अन्यतरस्याम् is employed here.

आर्जधातुके ॥ ४६ ॥ पदानि ॥ आर्जधातु के ।

वृत्तिः ॥ आर्जधातुकदस्यधिकारो न व्यपीति प्रागेतस्माद्यदित ऊर्ध्वमनुक्रमिष्याम आर्जधातुकदस्येवं तद्वेदित्ययम् ।

46. From this upto VI. 4. 68 inclusive, is always to be supplied "before an affix called ārdhadhātuka ( III. 4. 114 &c )."

This is an adhikāra sūtra and extends upto VI. 4. 69 ( exclusive). In all the sūtras upto VI. 4. 68 should be supplied the phrase "before an affix called ārdhadhātuka". Thus VI. 4. 48 teaches "the अ standing at the end of a verbal stem is elided". To complete the sense we should add: "before an ārdhadhātuka affix". Thus the final अ of the verbal stem चिकीर्ष is elided before the ārdhātuka affix छ, as चिकीर्षित्, जिहीर्षित्, but the final अ is not elided before a sārvadhātuka affix, as the अ of भव in भवति, भवतः ॥ The luk-elision of शप् after roots of अशादि class, implies that there is never lopa of शप् ॥

The following purposes are served by this sūtra, i. e. an ārdhātuka affix causes the following special changes (1) अतोऽप्:— The elision of अ of a stem, as shown above, in चिकीर्षिता, चिकीर्षितुम्, (2) यलोपश्च, The elision of य by VI. 4. 49, 50: as बेमिदिता, बेमिदितुम्, बेमिदितव्यम् from बेमिध्य the Intensive stem. Before Sārvadhātuka, we have बेमिध्यते, चिच्छिद्यते ॥ (3) गिलोपश्च प्रयोजनम्, The elision of णि by VI. 4. 51, as कारणा हरणा पाच्यते (पाच्चि+यक्+ते=पाच्च+य+ते), याज्यते ॥ In Sārvadhātuka, पाचयति, याजयति, कारयति, हारयति ॥ (4) आल्लोपः, the elision of आ, VI. 4. 64— as पपत्तु, पपुः, ववत्तु: वदः, In Sārvadhātuka, यान्ति, यान्ति (5) ईस्वम्— The substitution of long ई for आ in some roots, VI. 4. 65 as धीयते, धीयते; in Sārvadhātuka अवाताम्, अवाताम् (6) एस्वम्— The substitution of ए for आ, VI. 4. 68; as स्नेयात्, स्नेयात्; in Sārvadhātuka, स्नायात्, स्नायात् ॥ This is confined to the Precative (āsirlin). (7) चिण्वद्भावश्च सीयुटि, the treatment of the Precative like Aorist Passive in चिण्, by VI. 4. 62. as कारिषीष्ट, हारिषीष्ट ॥ In Sārvadhātuka, क्रियेत, क्रियेत ॥

Kāśikā:—अतो लोपो यलोपश्च गिलोपश्च प्रयोजनम् ।

आलोप ईस्वमेत्स्व च चिण्वद्भावश्च सीयुटि ॥

भ्रस्जो रोपधयोरमन्यतरस्याम् ॥ ४७ ॥ पदानि । भ्रस्जः, र-उपधयोः, रम, अन्यतरस्याम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ भ्रस्जो रेफस्योपधायाश्च रमन्यतरस्यां भवति ।

30

1270

ARDHADHATU-CHANGES

[ Bk.VI. Ch. IV. 49.

47. In the room of the र and the penultimate letter स of the root भ्रम, there is optionally the substitute रम, when an ārdhadhātuka affix follows.

The र and स cease to exist and र takes their place. The substitute having an indicatory म comes after the final vowel (I. I. 49). Thus भ्रम+तू= भर्ज+तू= भर्हा the अ being changed to ष by VIII. 2. 36, and त to ट by VIII. 4. 41. The other form will be भ्रहा; so also भ्रहुम् and भर्हुम्, भ्रह्म्यम् and भर्ह्म्यम्, भ्रह्म्यम् or भर्ह्म्यम् ॥ But भ्रहः and भ्रह्म्यम् by VI. I. 16, in spite of this rule. The word उपदेश (VI. 4. 37). is understood here also. The rule therefore applies to the simple root bhrasj as originally taught in the Dhatupātha, and not to any Derivative root from it. As the Intensive (यक्ष) is बरीभुज्यते ॥

अतो लोपः ॥ ४८ ॥ पदानि ॥ अतः, लोपः, (आर्ज्धधातुके) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अकारान्तस्यार्ज्धधातुके लोपो भवति ।

वार्तिकम् ॥ वृजिदीर्घाभ्यामतो लोपः पूर्वविमतिषेधेन ॥

48. The अ standing at the end of a stem is elided before an ārdhadhātuka affix.

Thus चिकीर्षिता, चिकीर्षितुम्, and चिकीर्षितव्यम्, from the Desiderative stem चिकीर्ष ॥ So also धितुतः and कृणुतः from the roots धिन्व् and कृण्व् thus, धिन्व्+उ (III. I. 80)=धिन्व्+अ+उ (III. I. 80)=धिन्व्+उ (अ being elided before the ārdhātuka उ)=धितु, the 3rd Personal dual of it is धितुतः ॥ The addition of अ by III. I. 80 and its subsequent elision by the present sūtra, may appear a redundancy, but the elided अ being sthānivat, prevents guṇa of धि ॥ So also कृणुतः ॥ See sūtra III. I. 80. Why do we say “the अ is elided”? Observe चेता, श्रोता here र and उ have not been elided. Why do we say “अतः with a त्”? The long आ will not be elided: as याता, वाता ॥ Why do we say “before an Ardhadhātuka”? Before a Sārvadhātuka there will be no elision of अ nor before a Taddhita: as वृक्षत्वम् and वृक्षता ॥

Vārt:—The elision of such अ takes place even to the supersession of the subsequent rules relating to Vṛiddhi and lengthening. As चिकीर्षकः, जिहीर्षकः, चिकीर्ष्यते and जिहीर्ष्यते ॥

यस्य हलः ॥ ४९ ॥ पदानि ॥ यस्य, हलः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ हल उत्तरस्य यशश्चर्यार्ज्धधातुके लोपो भवति ।

49. When a consonant precedes the final य in a verbal stem, this य is elided also before an ārdhadhātuka affix.

Thus बेमिदिता, बेमिदितुम्, बेमिदितव्यम् from the Intensive stem बेमिदा ॥ In the sūtra यस्य is given, which is the Genitive singular of य namely of the letters य अ ॥ By the rule of अलोऽन्यस्य (I. I. 52), the अ of य ought to be elided

BK. VI. CH. IV. §. 52 ] ARDHADHATU CHANGES

1271

and not च्; but that rule is evidently inapplicable here, since the elision of च would have taken place by the preceding rule: the present rule therefore teaches the elision of च (ya). Or the word हलः may be considered as in the ablative case, and then by I. 1. 54, the first letter would be elided namely च् ॥ Why have we taken [the two letters (संघात) conjointly viz.] च and not च्? Observe ईष्यता, मष्यता, शुष्यता from the simple roots ईष्य, मष्य, and शुष्य ॥ Here च् not being followed by च्, is not elided (see Bhvadi 541—546). Why do we say 'when preceded by a consonant?' Observe लोहयिता, पोषयिता ॥

कयस्य विभाषा ॥ ५० ॥ पदानि ॥ कयस्य, विभाषा, ( आष्ठेधातुके ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कयस्य हल उत्तरस्य विभाषा लोपो भवति आष्ठेधातुके ।

50. The elision of च of the Denominative stem (कय) is optional, when preceded by a consonant and followed by an ārdhadhātuka affix.

The कय denotes the affixes कयच् and कयच् ॥ Thus समिधिता or समिधिता, इषधिता or इषधिता meaning समिधमामन इषधिता or समिध इषधिता &c.

गेरमिति ॥ ५१ ॥ पदानि ॥ गेः, अनिति, ( आष्ठेधातुके ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अनिद्वाद्वाष्ठेधातुके गेरोपो भवति ।

51. The इ of the verbal stem formed with the affix णि, is elided before an ārdhadhātuka affix which does not take the augment इह ॥

This debars इयच्, the semi-vowel च, the guṇa, Vṛiddhi and the long substitutions. Thus अततश्चत्, अरश्चत्, आशिश्चत्, आदितत्, कारणा, हारणा, कारकः, हारकः, कार्यते, हार्यते and शीप्सति (see VII. 4. 1 for the shortening of the stem of the Aorists in these). Why do we say 'not having the augment इह?' Observe कारयिता and हारयिता ॥

निष्ठायां सेटि ॥ ५२ ॥ पदानि ॥ निष्ठायाम्, सेटि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ निष्ठायां सेटि परतो गेरोपो भवति ।

52. The affix णि is elided before the affixes क and कयतु when these take the augment इह ॥

Thus कारितम्, हारितम्, गणितम्, लसितम् ॥ Why do we say 'before an ārdhadhātuka affix having the augment इह?' Observe संज्ञपितः पशुः ॥ This is the part participle of the causative, the इ being the sign of the causative. By VII. 2. 15 read with VII. 2. 49, इष is a root which takes no इह augment in the Nishthā. It may be objected that VII. 2. 15 preventing इह augment applies to verbs of one syllable (VII. 2. 10), and the causative इष being of two syllables will always have इह in the Nishthā, and so it is useless to use the word सेटि in the sūtra. The word सेटि in the sūtra fixes the time when the elision of णि should take place. Namely, first there should be added the

1272

ARDHADHATU CHANGES. [ Bk. VI. Ch. IV. § 56

augment इह and then, there should take place the elision of णि ॥ Otherwise we shall have this difficulty कारि+त, here let us elide the णि first: and we get कार्+त, now we cannot add इह to त, for कार् being a verb of one syllable will not take इह by VII. 2. 10. Therefore, the reverse process must be adopted. We must elide इह first. For शपित: see also VII. 2. 27.

जनिता मन्त्रे ॥ ५३ ॥ पदानि ॥ जनिता, मन्त्रे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ जनितेति मन्त्रविषये इजादौ गिलोपो निपाय्यते ।

53. In a Mantra, the word जनिता is formed irregularly by the elision of णि before the affix य् with the augment इह ॥

Thus यो नः पिता जनिता ॥ Otherwise जनविता in secular literature. It is an exception to VI. 4. 51.

शमिता यज्ञे ॥ ५४ ॥ पदानि ॥ शमिता, यज्ञे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ यज्ञकर्मणि शमितेति इजादौ गिलोपो निपाय्यते ।

54. शमिता is formed irregularly by the elision of णि before an इह augmented affix, when meaning a sacrificial act.

Thus शूत् हविः शमितः ॥ It is formed by शूत् and is in the Vocative case. Why do we say 'when referring to a sacrificial act'? See शूत् हविः शमयितः ॥ See Satpatha Br. III. 8. 3, 4 and 5.

अयामन्ताल्वाय्येतन्विष्णुपु ॥ ५५ ॥ पदानि ॥ अय, आम-अन्त-आलु-आय्य-इलु-इष्णुपु, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आम अन्त आलु आय्य इलु इष्णु इय्येतेषु परतो णेरयादेशो भवति ।

55. अय is substituted for the इ of णि, before the affixes आम, अन्त, आलु, आय्य, इलु, and इष्णु ॥

Thus कारयां चकार, हारयां चकार, गण्डयन्तः, गण्डयन्तः (formed by the Unādi affix हाय, हा=अन्त, added to the roots गंड and गंड) आलु । स्फुहयालुः । आय्य, स्फुहयाय्यः, गृहयाय्यः ॥ इलु:—स्तनायलुः ॥ इष्णु:—पोषयिष्णुः ॥ Thus sūtra could have been well dispensed with; for the इ of णि would take guna ए which will be changed to अय by the rules of Sandhi, be fore these affixes. This substitution of अय for इ is for the sake of the subsequent sūtra however, because there इ could not be changed to अय by any sandhi-rules.

ल्यपि लघुपूर्वात् ॥ ५६ ॥ पदानि ॥ ल्यपि, लघु पूर्वात् ( णेः अय ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ल्यपि परतो लघुपूर्वादुत्तरस्य णेरयादेशो भवति ।

56. अय is substituted for the इ of णि, before the Absolutive affix ल्यप्, when the vowel preceding the इ is light.

Thus प्रशमय्य गतः, संदमय्य गतः, प्रबेमिदय्य, प्रगणय्य ॥ But प्रपात्य गतः the vowel preceding the इ being long. Here VI. 4. 51 applies. The shortening, the

BK. VI. CH. IV § 60.] ARDHADHATUKA CHANGES.

1273

elision of य and the elision of अ should not be considered as asiddha, as their place of operation is not the same. Thus श्व+ णिष्= श्वि; this आ is shortened by VI. 4. 92, and we have श्वि ॥ This shortening is not to be considered as asiddha, for if asiddha, there being no laghu purva, the present rule would not apply. Similarly वेनिष् is the Intensive root, its य is elided by VI. 4. 49, this elision is not considered as asiddha, if it were asiddha, the इ of भि would not be laghu. Similarly the elision of अ in गण which is a root which ends in अ, (see Dhātupātha Churadi 309), is not considered as asiddha for similar reasons.

विभाषा, ऽपः ॥ ५७ ॥ पदानि ॥ विभाषा, आपः, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आप उत्तरस्य णेल्यपि परतो विभाषा ऽयावेशो भवति ॥

57. अय् is optionally substituted for the इ of णि before the affix ल्यप्, after the verb आप् ॥

Thus प्राप्य or प्राप्य गतः ॥ This however does not apply to the आप् substitute for इह्, as अध्याप्य गतः (VI. 1. 48, VII. 3. 36). The maxim of Pratipadokta applies here.

यु-ल्लुवोर्द्वैधैच्छन्दसि ॥ ५८ ॥ पदानि ॥ यु-ल्लुवोः, दीर्घः, छन्दसि, ( ल्यपि ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ यु-ल्लुवोर्द्वैधैच्छन्दसि विषये दीर्घो भवति ॥

58. In यु and ण्, long is substituted for उ, before ल्यप् in the Veda.

Thus श्वान्प्रतुपूर्वे विद्यु; यथा यो दक्षिणा परिप्लव ॥ Why do we say 'in the Chhandas'? Observe संधुल, आप्लुल in the secular literature.

क्षियः ॥ ५९ ॥ पदानि ॥ क्षियः, (दीर्घः ल्यपि) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ क्षियश्च दीर्घो भवति ल्यपि परतः ॥

59. A long is substituted for the इ of क्षि before ल्यप् ॥

As प्रक्षीय, उपक्षीय ॥

निष्ठायामण्यदर्थे ॥ ६० ॥ पदानि ॥ निष्ठायाम. अ-ण्यदर्थे, ( दीर्घः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ण्यतः कृत्यस्यार्थो भावकर्मणी ताभ्यामन्यश्च या निष्ठा तस्यां क्षियो दीर्घो भवति ।

60. A long is substituted for the इ of क्षि before the Participle in क्, when it has not the sense of the future Passive Participle in ण्यत् ॥

The force of ण्यत् is to denote condition (Impersonal action) and object (passive). When the Past Participle has not the force of ण्यत्, the vowel of क्षि is lengthened. Thus आक्षीणः, प्रक्षीणः, परिक्षीणः all used in the active sense. The क् is added to the Intransitive क्षि to denote the agent (III. 4. 72). Thus प्रक्षीणमिर्देववृत्तस्य 'this is the spot where Devadatta perished'. Here क् is used with a Locative force (III. 4. 76). Why do we say 'not having the force of

1274

ARDHADHATUKA CHANGES. [ Bk. VI. Ch. IV. § 62

एवम् ?' Observe असितनसिनामेशोः ॥ Here न is added with the force of condition, and akshitam means 'imperishable'. The vowel not being lengthened the न is not changed to न (VIII. 2. 46).

वा ऽकोशदैन्ययोः ॥ ६१ ॥ पदानि ॥ वा, आकोश-दैन्ययोः (क्षियः दीर्घः विभाषा) वृत्ति ॥ आकोश गन्धमाने दैत्ये च क्षियो निष्ठावानन्यदर्थे वा दीर्घो भवति ॥

61. The long is optionally substituted, for the इ of क्षि, before the Past Participle क्, not having the sense of the Future Passive Participle ण्यत्, when the word means 'imprecation' or 'a miserable plight'.

Thus क्षितायुरेधि or क्षीणायुरेधि, क्षितकः or क्षीणकः, क्षितोयं तपस्वी, क्षीणोऽयं तपस्वी ॥ When not having the sense of cursing or miserable condition, we have one form only, as क्षीणबन्धः ॥

स्यसिचसीयुट्तासिबु भावकर्मणोरुपदेश ऽज्वनप्रहृदशां वा चिण्वदिष्ट च ॥ ६२ ॥ पदानि ॥ स्य-सिच-सीयुट्-तासि, भाव-कर्मणोः, उपदेशो, अच्-हन्-प्रह-दशाम्, वा, चिण्वत, इद्, च, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ स्य सिच्-सीयुट्-तासि इत्येतेषु भावकर्मणोपदेशे परत उपदेशे ऽज्वनानामङ्गानां हन्-प्रह-दश इत्येतेषां च चिण्वत्कायं भवति वा । यथा चिण्वत तथा इदागमो भवति ।

62. Before the affixes स्य (First Future and Conditional), सिच् (S-Aorist), सीयुट् (Benedictive) and तासि (the Priphrastic Future), when there are used in the Impersonal (भाव) and Passive (कर्म) Voices, (1) the verbal stems ending in a vowel in the Grammatical system of instruction (उपदेश), as well as the verbs (2) हन् (3) प्रह् and (4) इश् are treated optionally in the same way as in the third person of the Passive Aorist in चिण्, and when so treated, they have the augment इत् ॥

The augment इत् is, of course, added to the affixes स्य, सिच्, सीयुट् and तासि and not to the stem. What are the special objects served by this atidesa aphorism? They are given in the following verse :—

Kārikā चिण्वद् वृजिर्युक्त् च हन्तेभ् पत्यं
दीर्घोक्तो यो मितां वा चिणाति ।
इद् चासिजस्तेन मे लुप्यते णि-
नित्यभावं वलनिमित्तोऽविधाती ॥

First :—The Vṛddhi takes place as in चिण् (VII. 2. 116, VII. 3. 34), secondly, there is the addition of युक्त augment (VII. 3. 33), thirdly च is substituted for the इ of इत् (VII. 3. 54), fourthly, the roots having indicatory

BK. VI. CH. IV. §. 63 ]

CHIN-VAD-BHĀVA

1275

(Bhuādi 809 to 873) optionally lengthen their vowel (VI. 4. 93), and lastly the addition of the augment हृद being considered as asiddha or not to have taken effect by VI. 4. 22, the rule VI. 4. 51 applies and the causative affix ण is elided : and this हृद is added irrespective of the conditions and limitations of VII. 2. 35 &c.

(1) Roots ending in a vowel in the Dhātupāṭha with the affix स्य as, चि:—चायिष्यत or चैष्यते, अचायिष्यत or अचेष्यत ॥ So also with शा, as, वायिष्यते or शास्यते, अचायिष्यत or अचास्यत ॥

In शनि there are three forms, the two शानिष्यते or शमिष्यते, अशानिष्यत and अशानिष्यत being given by the elision of the causative ending by VI. 4. 51, in spite of the हृद augment which is considered as asiddha : and शम् being a root of मित् class, the अ is lengthened optionally by VI. 4. 93. The forms शमयिष्यते and अशमयिष्यत are given when not treated as चिण्, the causative is retained, the penultimate being shortened by VI. 4. 92. With the affix सिच्—अचायिषाताम् or अचेषाताम्, अचायिषाताम्, or अचिषाताम् and अशानिषाताम् or अशमिषाताम् ॥ With the affix सीयुद्—चायिषीष्ट or चैषीष्ट, वायिषीष्ट or शासीष्ट and शानिषीष्ट or शमिषीष्ट ॥ With the affix तासि:—चायिता or चैता, वायिता or शाता, शानिता or शमिता ॥ The चिण् aorist model of these roots is अचायि, अचायि (VII. 3. 33), and अशानि (VII. 3. 34) or अशानि (VI. 4. 93).

(2) हृद:—Fut. पानिष्यते or हनिष्यते; Con. अपानिष्यत or अहनिष्यत, Aor. अपानिषाताम् or अवधिषाताम् and अहसाताम् (II. 4. 44); Ben पानिषीष्ट or वधिषीष्ट; Per. Fut. पानिता or हन्ता ॥ The चिण् model is अपानि ॥

(3) मह:—Fut. माहिष्यते or महीष्यते Con. अमाहिष्यत or अमहीष्यत; Aor. अमाहिषाताम् or अमहीषाताम् (अमहिषाताम्)?; Ben. माहिषीष्ट or (महिषीष्ट)? महीषीष्ट, Per. Fut. माहिता or महिता ॥ The lengthening of ही takes place by VII. 2. 37. The चिण् model is अमाहि ॥

(4) हृद:—Fut. रशिष्यते or हृश्यते, Con. अरशिष्यत or अचृश्यत; Aor. अरशिषाताम् or अचशाताम्; Ben रशिषीष्ट or हृशीष्ट; Per. Fut. रशिता or हृदा (रशि)? ॥ The चिण् model is अरशि ॥

Why do we say before स्य &c? Observe चैतव्यम्, शानव्यम् ॥ Why in the Impersonal and Passive? Observe चैष्यते and शास्यते ॥ Why in Upadeśa? The rule applies to कारिष्यते also, though कार (after gūṇa change) ends in a consonant, but in its original enunciation it ends with a vowel. The atideśa rule being enunciated with regard to stems (aṅga), prevents the substitutions of हृद and हृद and हृण् ॥ Thus हनिष्यते, पानिष्यते, एष्यते or आयिष्यते, अचेष्यते or अच्यायिष्यते ॥ The substitutes वध or गा (II. 4. 42, 43, 45, 50) do not come according to the Kāśikā, when these roots are treated as चिण् ॥

दीडो युडचि कूडिति ॥ ६३ ॥ पदानि ॥ दीडः, युड्, अचि, कूडिति ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ दीडोयुडागमो भवति अजादौ कूडिति प्रथये परतः ॥

1276

ARDHADHĀTU CHANGES

[ Bk. VI. Ch. IV § 66

63. युद्ध is the augment after दीङ्, of an ārdha-dhātuka affix beginning with a vowel and having an indicatory क् or ङ् ॥

Thus उपविधीये, उपविधीयाते and उपविधीये ॥ The Personal ending is किह् by I. 2. 5. दीङ्: being in the Ablative case, the augment is applied to the affix. This augment, however, is not to be considered as asiddha (VI. 4. 22) for the purposes of semi-vowel substitution under VI. 4. 82. If that substitution were allowed, the augment would become useless. Why before an affix having क् or ङ्? Observe उपदानम् ॥

आतो लोप इटि च ॥ ६४ ॥ पदानि ॥ आतः, लोपः, इटि, च, ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ इदावावाञ्छधातुके कुडिति चाकारान्तस्याङ्गस्य लोपो भवति ॥

64. The final आ of a root is elided before an ārdhadhātuka affix with the augment इट् as well as when it begins with a vowel and has an indicatory क् or ङ् ॥

Thus पपिय and तस्थिय ॥ Here the affix has the इट् augment. पपतु, पपुः, सस्यतु, तस्यु ॥ Here the affixes are किह् by I. 2. 5 गोः, कञ्चलः with the affix क् (III. 2. 3). So also प्रवा (fem), प्रधा (fem) by अङ् III. 3. 106. Before Sārvadhātuka affixes, we have यान्ति, यान्ति, व्यत्ये and व्यत्ये ॥ The two latter are the Imperfect 1st Pers. Sing. Atm. of रा and ला with the affix इ (इट्). When it does not begin with a vowel, we have ग्लायते, शसीय ॥

ईयति ॥ ६५ ॥ पदानि ॥ ईत, यति, ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ ईकार आवेशो भवति आकारान्तस्याङ्गस्य यति परतः ॥

65. The final आ of a stem is changed into ई before the Krit-affix यत् ॥

Thus देयम्, धेयम्, देयम्, and स्तेयम् ॥ The Guṇa takes place according to VII. 3. 84.

घुमाख्यागापाजहातिसां हलि ॥ ६६ ॥ पदानि ॥ घु, मा, खा, गा, पा, जहाति साम, हलि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ घुसंज्ञकानामङ्गानां मा स्था गा पा जहाति सा इत्येतेषां हतादौ कुडिति प्रत्यये परत ईकारवेशो भवति ॥

66. For the final of the roots of the form of दा and धा (घु), as well as for that of the roots मा, स्था, गा, पा, हा (जहाति) and सा (सो), there is substituted ई before an ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with a consonant, which has an indicatory क् or ङ् ॥

Thus दीयते, धीयते with यक, दैदीयते, दैपीयते with यङ् ॥ So also मीयते मेमीयते स्थीयते, तेष्टीयते, गीयते, जेगीयते, अध्यगीट, अध्यगीपाताम्, अध्यगीपत, पीयते, पेपीयते, हीयते, जेहीयते, अवसीयते, अवससीयते ॥

The पा 'to protect' of Adadi (47) is not meant here. be come the

BK. VI. CH. IV § 69 ]

ABHIVA-RULES.

1277

vikarana श्वः is elided in roots of that class. Its form will be पायते. It is Bhvādi पा 'to drink' that is taken here. So also हा-जिहीते is not to be taken here. Its form is हायते ॥

Why do we say 'before a consonant'? Observe वदतु:, वदुः ॥ Here had ह्वः not been used in the sūtra, the आ of वा would be replaced by ई by the present sūtra, even before a vowel-affix अतुः o उस्; for the lopa of आ taught in VI. 4. 64 is prevented by this *subsequent* sūtra teaching ई substitution. In fact, the employment of the word ह्वः in the aphorism is a jñāpaka that the rule of vipratishedha (I.4.2) applies in this section of asiddha (VI. 4. 22), and the lopa of आ is *superseded* by the present rule substituting ई instead. So also शता and धाता before non-कित् and non-डित् affixes.

पल्लिडि ॥ ६७ ॥ पदानि ॥ ए:, लिडि, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ धुमास्थागापाजहातिसामङ्गानां लिडि परत एकारादेशो भवति ॥

67. ए is substituted for the आ of the above roots in the Benedictive mood Active.

Thus देयात्, नेयात्, धेयात्, स्थेयात्, गेयात्, पेयात् and अवसेयात् ॥ Before non-कित् and non-डित् we have हसीट and धासीट ॥ By the word लिड् is here meant the आशीर्लिङ्ग or the Precative mood; the Personal endings of which mood are ārdhadhātuka by III. 4. 116. More-over by III. 4. 104 the Parasmaipada affixes only of the Benedictive are कित्, so the present rule does not apply to the Atmanepada affixes of the Precative.

वा ऽन्यस्य संयोगादेः ॥ ६८ ॥ पदानि ॥ वा, अन्यस्य-संयोग, आदेः, ( लिडि ) ( आतः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ धुवादिभ्यो ऽन्यस्य संयोगादिराकारान्तस्य वा एकारादेशो भवति लिडि परतः ॥

68. For the final आ of any other root than those mentioned in VI. 4. 66, ए may optionally be substituted, in the Benedictive active, when the root begins with a conjunct consonant.

The स्या was the only root of VI. 4. 66, which could have been affected by this rule. It has been, however, specially exempted by the word अन्यस्य ॥ Thus ग्लेयात् or ग्लायात्, ग्लेयात् or ग्लायात्, but only स्थेयात् (VI. 4. 66), and थायात् (not commencing with a double consonant). The phrase किङति is understood here and therefore the rule applies to Parasmaepada affixes (III. 4. 104). Thus ग्लासीट in Atmanepada. The root considered as an aṅga, should consist of a double consonant, therefore in निर्वायात् (from निर्+वा), ई is not to be considered as a root having a double consonant, for र is no part of the aṅga, but of the preposition.

न ल्यपि ॥ ६९ ॥ पदानि ॥ न, ल्यपि, धुमास्थागापाजहातिसाम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ स्थपि प्रत्यये परतो पुनश्चागापाजहातिसां बहुक्तं तन्न ॥

69. The ई substitution for आ under rule VI. 4. 66, does not apply when the absolutive affix ल्यप् follows पु मा, स्था, गा, पा, हा and सा ॥

Thus प्राय, प्राय, प्राय, प्रायाय, प्रायाय, प्रायाय, प्रायाय and अनसाय ॥ The affix ल्यप् as the substitute of बन्धा, is a किंतु affix by I. 1. 56.

मयतेरिदन्यतरस्याम् ॥ ७० ॥ पदानि ॥ मयतेः, इत्, अन्यतरस्याम्, ( ल्यपि ) ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ मयतेरिकारदिशो वा भवति ॥

70. इ may optionally be substituted for the आ of मा, ( मयति ) before ल्यप् ॥

Thus अपनित्य or अपनाय ॥

लुङ्लङ्लङ्श्चद्वदात्तः ॥ ७१ ॥ पदानि ॥ लुङ्, लङ्, लङ् श्रु, अद्, उदात्तः ( अङ्गस्य ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ लुङ् लङ् लङ् इत्येतेषु परतोऽस्याङ्गनो भवति, उदात्तश्च स भवति ॥

71. अद् acutely accented is the augment of the verbal stem in the Aorist, Imperfect and the Conditional.

Thus अकार्पीत्, अकार्पीत्, अकरोत्, अहरत् and अकरप्यित्, अहिरिप्यत् ॥

आडजादीनाम् ॥ ७२ ॥ पदानि ॥ आद्, अच्-आदीनाम्, ( उदात्तः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आङ्गनो भवत्यजादीनां लुङ्लङ्लङ्श्च परतं उदात्तश्च स भवति ॥

72. आद् acutely accented is the augment of a verbal stem beginning with a vowel, in the Aorist, Imperfect and the Conditional.

Thus ऐशिट, ऐशत, ऐशिष्यत; औजीत्, औजजत्, औजिष्यत् ॥ ऐशिट, ऐशत and ऐशिष्य औजीत्, औजजत्, and औजिष्यत् ॥ The Vriddhi takes place by VI. 1. 90.

The Passive Imperfect ( लङ् ) of यज्, यप् and यङ् are ऐज्यत, औप्यत and औहात formed by आद् and not अद् ॥ First, the affixes of the Imperfect are added and then the Passive characteristic यङ् is added to these roots, which causes the vocalisation of the semi-vowels, and we have इज्यत, उष्यत, and उहात stems (VI. I. 15). The stems having now assumed a form in which they begin with a vowel, take आद् ॥ The addition of tense-affixes being an antaranga operation precedes the addition of augment. After the affixes have been added, the vikarapa यङ्, being nitya, is added and precedes in order the augment, the latter being so far anitya; after यङ् addition the roots assume a form in which we can add आद् ॥ Why आद् is considered anitya depends on the following maxim:—शब्दान्तरस्य प्राप्युत्वं विधिनित्यो भवति “when the word-form in reference to which a rule teaches something; after the taking effect of another rule that applies simultaneously would be different from what it was before that other rule had taken effect, then the former rule is not nitya.”

BK. VI. CH. IV § 76 ]

THE AUGMENT अ ॥

1279

छन्दस्यापि दृश्यते ॥ ७३ ॥ पदानि ॥ छन्दसि, अपि, दृश्यते, आह ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ छन्दसि विषये आडागमो दृश्यते । यत्र हि विहितस्ततोऽन्यापि दृश्यते ।

73. The आह augment is found in the Veda also.

It is found there before the roots beginning with a vowel as well as before consonant roots. Thus आवः, आनक्, and आयुनक् ॥ आवः is the Aorist of युग्म, the affix being elided by II. 4. 80. आनक् from नध् (II. 4. 80), and आयुनक् is the Imperfect of युग्म ॥

न माङ्गयोगे ॥ ७४ ॥ पदानि ॥ न, माङ्ग, योगे (लुङ्ग लङ् लङ्) ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ माङ्गयोगे लुङ्गलङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ् लङ्

74. In connection with the prohibitive particle मा, the augment अह् or आह is not added in the Aorist, Imperfect and the Conditional.

Thus मा भवान् कार्पीत्, मा भवान् हार्पीत्, मा स करोत्, मा स हरत्, मा भवानीहिष्टमा, भवानीहिष्ट, मा स भवानीहृत, मा स भवानीहृत ॥

बहुलं छन्दस्यमाङ्गयोगे ऽपि ॥ ७५ ॥ पदानि ॥ बहुलम्, छन्दसि, अ माङ्ग योगे, अपि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ छन्दसि विषये माङ्गयोगे ऽपि बहुलमाङ्गो भवतः अमाङ्गयोगेपि न भवतः ॥

75. There is diversity in the Veda : the augment अह् or आह is added even with मा, and sometimes not added even when there is no मा ॥

Thus in अनिष्ठा उभः (Rig X. 73. 1), काममुनयीत् (Rig I. 53. 3) and काममवैषीत्; the augment is not added though there is no मा ॥ In मा वः क्षेत्रे परबभिज्ञान्यवाप्युः, मा अभित्याः, मा आवः, the augment is not elided, though the particle मा is added.

इरयो रे ॥ ७६ ॥ पदानि ॥ इरयोः, रे, ( बहुलंछन्दसि ) ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ इरे इत्येतस्य छन्दसि विषये बहुलं रे इत्ययमादेशो भवति ॥

76. रे is diversely substituted for इरे in the Veda.

Thus कं स्विहर्मं प्रथमं इधे आपः (Rig X. 82. 5) या स्य परिबधे ॥ In इधे, the आ of धा is elided before the affix इरे by VI. 4. 64, the रे substitution being considered as asiddha (VI. 4. 22) for the purposes of the elision of आ ॥ Sometimes the substitution does not take place, as परमाया धियेग्निम्माणि चक्रिरे ॥ Here इह् augment is first added to रे after the सेद roots and the affix thus becomes इरे, then रे is substituted again for this इरे by this sutra, thus the affix is brought back to its original condition. To show this repetition—रे—इरे—रे the sutra has exhibited the word इरयोः in the dual number.

अचि हनुधातु मुर्वा व्योरियडुवडौ ॥ ७७ ॥ पदानि ॥ अचि, हनु, धातु, मुवाम, व्योः, इयङ्, उवडौ, ॥

77. Before an affix beginning with a vowel, there are substituted for the उ of ठु, the characteristic of the roots of the fifth class, for the final इ, ई, उ and ऊ of a root, as well as for the ऊ of भु, the इय (for इ or ई) and उव (for उ or ऊ).

Thus आप्तुवन्ति, राधुवन्ति, शक्रुवन्ति, from roots of the 5th class. चिशियतुः लुडुवतुः, लुडुः, नियो, नियः, लुवो, लुवः and भुवो and भुवः ॥

Why do we say before an affix beginning with a vowel? Observe आप्तुवात, शक्रुवात, राधुवात ॥ Why “of ठु &c.”? Observe लभ्ये, लभ्याः, वभ्ये, वभ्याः ॥ Why “of इ and उ”? Observe चक्रुतः, चक्रुः where the vowel is क ॥

Vårt:—The Guṇa (VII. 3. 84) and Vṛiddhi (VII. 2. 115) however take place to the supersession of इयङ् and उवङ्: as from चि—चयनम् and चायकः, लु—लवनम् and लावकः, with लुपु and णुलु ॥

Vårt:—In the Chhandas there is deversely the substitution of इयङ् and उवङ् in the case of तन् &c. Thus तन्नं पुघेम or तन्नं पुघेम ॥ विपुत्रं पुघेम, स्वर्गो लोकः, सुवर्गो लोकः, त्र्यम्बकं यजामहे, त्रियम्बकं यजामहे ॥

अभ्यासस्यासवर्णे ॥७८॥ पदानि ॥ अभ्यासस्य, अ, सवर्णे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अभ्यासस्येवर्णो वर्णान्तस्यासवर्णे णचि परत इयङ् उवङ् इत्येतावादिशी भवतः ॥

78. इयङ् and उवङ् are substituted for the इ and उ of a reduplicate, before a non-homogenous vowel.

Thus इयेप, उवोप, इयत्ति, (VII. 4. 77) but इयतुः and इयुः, ऊयतुः and ऊयुः before homogenous vowels and इयाय and उवाय before a non-vowel.

वृत्तिः ॥ खीइत्यतस्याजादी मत्ये परतः इयङादेशो भवति ॥

79. इयङ् is substituted for the ई of खी before an affix beginning with a vowel.

As खी, खियो, खियः; but खीणाम् the न् being added by a subsequent rule, supersedes this rule. The making this a separate sutra is for the sake of the subsequent aphorisms.

वा ऽमशसोः ॥ ८० ॥ पदानि ॥ वा, अम, शसोः (इयङ् खियाः) ॥

Thus खी पञ् or खियं पञ्, खीः पञ् or खियः पञ् ॥
